Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison has received a court fine after being caught driving through a red light in his £60,000 Chevrolet sportscar.

The 29-year-old Brazilian striker was recorded by a camera mounted on the A41 in Hendon, north London, driving his Chevrolet Corvette Stingray through traffic signals 1.5 seconds after they had turned red at 6.45pm on 15 April.

At a hearing conducted behind closed doors at Barkingside Magistrates’ Court last week, the Premier League footballer was convicted of failing to comply with a red light signal. He was given a £200 fine, three penalty points on his licence, and ordered to pay £120 in prosecution costs alongside an £80 victim surcharge.

Court papers reveal the Metropolitan Police gave the player options to avoid criminal prosecution for the traffic offence on the A41. A police worker told the court that Richarlison confirmed in writing that he was driving the car when it was filmed running the red light.

The Met stated that Richarlison was offered the chance to take a driver retraining course, which he did not accept. He was then permitted to settle the matter by paying a fine; however, while he transferred the money, he failed to submit a copy of his driving licence.

open image in gallery Richarlison has been frozen out by Robert De Zerbi ( Getty )

Consequently, Richarlison was prosecuted using the Single Justice Procedure, entering a written guilty plea without providing any mitigation for the offence.

Richarlison was a key figure in Tottenham’s successful bid for Premier League survival last season. However, the striker has been frozen out under Roberto De Zerbi this term, following a proposed move back to former club Everton that fell through at the 11th hour.

He has not featured for Tottenham since starting their 3-0 loss to Brentford on the opening day of the season.

Richarlison has spent the last four years at Spurs since joining from Everton back in 2022. He also has 54 caps for Brazil, and has scored 20 goals for his country.

However, he has not played for Brazil since October 2025 after falling out of favour with manager Carlo Ancelotti ahead of the World Cup earlier this year.

News.title: Woman treated for Ebola in Nigeria evacuated to Switzerland
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Swiss woman being treated for Ebola in Nigeria has been flown home to Switzerland alongside her husband, as health authorities continue to track 52 people who were in contact with her.

Nigerian Health Minister Muhammad Pate said the patient, who was the country’s first case in the present outbreak, departed the capital, Abuja, early on Monday with his authorisation. Her health had improved significantly, leaving her stable, conscious and capable of communicating, he said.

"This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place," Pate wrote on X. Her spouse, a Swiss diplomat stationed in Nigeria, has displayed no symptoms.

Mohamed Janabi, the World Health Organization’s regional director for Africa, explained that the evacuation occurred because the pair are Swiss citizens, adding that local medical teams had stabilised her after managing the acute phase of the disease.

open image in gallery The woman tested positive after returning to Abuja from Uganda. Nigerian authorities said Friday they had yet to establish how she contracted the virus ( AP )

Switzerland is taking over her treatment and monitoring her husband, while Nigeria tracks the remaining 52 contacts.

"With the evacuation of the patient and her husband, Nigeria currently has no Ebola cases," Janabi stated, emphasising that continued caution is essential. Pate confirmed that containment efforts stay in effect and asked Nigerians to remain alert.

The woman tested positive after returning to Abuja from Uganda. Nigerian authorities said Friday they had yet to establish how she contracted the virus.

Switzerland’s foreign ministry said that she had not visited Congo and was believed to have been infected while traveling to Uganda with her husband.

The Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said the first patients in Nigeria and Kenya had both traveled through Uganda’s Entebbe International Airport on Oct. 3. Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases but later declared itself free of the virus.

Kenya has recorded nine cases, including two deaths, since confirming its first case earlier this month.

The spread of Ebola beyond Congo has heightened longstanding fears among health authorities about the rapid transmission of the rare Bundibugyo virus.

The latest figures from Congo’s health ministry show more than 9,900 cases, including more than 4,800 deaths, since the outbreak began in May.

The WHO has said the outbreak is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record and is on track to surpass the death toll of the deadliest: West Africa’s 2014-2016 outbreak, which killed 11,000 people. Nigeria was among the countries affected, recording 20 cases before its outbreak was declared over after three months.

News.title: Lloyds boss backs devolution plan - but warns against further taxes on banks
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lloyds Bank chief executive Charlie Nunn says the devolution plan of new prime minister Andy Burnham can help the government to “actually get stuff done” - but has also warned against taxes on banks.

Ahead of the Budget on 28 October, the first since Mr Burnham appointed John Healey as chancellor, there has been much speculation about where Labour will raise additional funds.

Banks are widely expected to be one sector which will be asked to fork out more than previously, though several industry experts have cautioned against the wisdom of doing so.

While the financial sector can generate huge profits, that money tends to go towards those who plough it back into the economy in other ways, critics say, including wide-ranging investors, those who run other business and the financial industry itself, which employ many and is part of the stronghold of British industry.

Speaking to the Financial Times, the CEO of Lloyds Banking Group - which also includes the likes of Bank of Scotland, Scottish Widows and what’s left of the Halifax brand - said the UK shouldn’t be focusing on windfall taxes for successful parts of the economy, as those who run successful businesses would be backing those horses, not reigning them in.

“Tax is obviously a matter for the government [...] we are not in an era of windfall returns,” said Mr Nunn in the FT’s Patrick Jenkins Interview. “We want to go faster, not slower” to continue building economic growth, he continued, adding that governments should “look at the UK economy as a CEO would” to help fuel that progression.

“It’s not the response that anywhere else in the world took. Most of the world realised that if you kill banking, you’re killing the ability of your economy to borrow and invest.

“In my ten years at [previous employer] HSBC, working with 50 countries, typically the conversation I’d have with regulators and governments was what can you do to drive productivity and growth. They’d tell us what sectors, what parts of their country they were trying to grow.

“The UK seems to have moved away from [that approach] since the financial crisis.”

Experts at tax and audit firm Blick Rothenberg have highlighted to The Independent that the last time banks faced a so-called windfall tax, the wider corporation tax was actually lower than it is now.

As such, it’s a far bigger overall hit that banks may face if their profits are taxed additionally again this time around.

Charlie Nunn has backed AI use and devolution to boost the economy ( PA Wire )

With banks typically determining where to invest their money by what their expected rate of return is, it stands to reason that a nation offering a lower projected return therefore might face less investment in it than previously, compared to bigger opportunities overseas.

That’s something which might be more impactful for multinational and global banks - such as Barclays or HSBC - than the more domestic-facing ones, including NatWest or Lloyds.

But the inclusion of such a tax might also hint at whether this is a Budget “to grow the economy, or just to cover its costs”, as Blick Rothenberg director Robert Salter put it.

Mr Nunn is rather more upbeat about the prospects of devolution and artificial intelligence giving the UK economy a boost.

“When I came back to the UK to do this role, we realised that one of the best ways of getting things done was down at a local combined authority or mayoral level, because they could join the dots between the assets they had, like land, and businesses or universities,” he said.

“The devolution agenda done properly could unlock [...] the ability for government to actually get stuff done.”

Meanwhile, AI offers a “massive opportunity” to reskill workers and offer AI-led advice to customers, particularly through encouraging them to invest - though Mr Nunn warns that so far “there hasn’t been enough thinking about the regulatory consequences if things go wrong for customers”.

However, AI offers another prospective positive for clients too: robots aren’t swayed by big commissions, which has been a problem in the past across the Payment Protection Insurance (PPI) scandal and with motor vehicle finance.

“If you look at what are classified as mis-selling scandals, it’s about the incentives,” said Mr Nunn. “You don’t have to incentivise an [AI] agent.”

News.title: Nurse accused of spreading Ebola murdered by mob
News.content:
A nurse was killed and a teacher badly injured in a mob attack after being accused of spreading Ebola in the water supply in Congo.

The unnamed victims were set upon in Bafwasende territory of Tshopo province after a group of young people accused them of being responsible for the outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever.

The nurse was killed outright and the teacher, who local media reported was close to the health worker, only survived after being rescued by police.

The World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the attack, which is only the latest incident of health workers being attacked by suspicious, scared or angry locals.

Medical workers have been forced to deal with widespread rumours that the outbreak – the world’s second largest – is spread by them.

Other conspiracy theories claim the outbreak is a money-making hoax for aid agencies, or that foreigners are using it as a pretext to grab the country’s minerals.

Strict rules imposed on how to conduct funerals in order to stop mourners becoming infected, have become another flashpoint.

Last month, a Congolese politician was beaten to death in North Kivu after publicly defending the government’s response.

He had been calling on the public to obey response measures, particularly social distancing and hand washing, on a radio show.

News.title: ‘Our world is yellow’: Fears for children as sickening smog blankets Indonesia
News.content:
For two months now, Natanael Undas has opened his curtains not to blue skies, but a sickening sepia haze that blocks out any sunlight. As the relentless fires smoulder nearby, his city looks “more like Mars” than Indonesian Borneo.

“We start our day in yellow, and we end our day in yellow,” the 32-year-old headteacher told the Telegraph. “When you inhale and take a breath, it feels like you’re choking. Your eyes hurt, your nose hurts… when you go outside, it feels like someone is burning dry leaves next to you.”

Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan, is on the front lines of an environmental crisis that has cloaked much of Southeast Asia in a toxic haze for months.

According to Nusantara Atlas, an open-access platform that tracks deforestation, fires have torched roughly 1.9 million hectares across the archipelago so far this year – including one million hectares in September alone.

“I’ve seen burning in the city, burning in the forests, burning near the river, burning in the peatlands, burning near the street – it’s devastating,” said Mr Undas. “It’s the longest burning season I’ve seen. Usually the rainy season comes in October, but everything is still on fire.”

News.title: Britain sanctions warlords accused of rape in Sudan
News.content:
The British government is to sanction senior military and militia commanders accused of atrocities, including rape and sexual violence, during the fall of the city of El Fasher in Sudan.

At least 15 commanders from both the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been sanctioned after investigations found they used rape as a weapon of war during the brutal siege of the Sudanese city in October last year.

The siege, perpetrated by the RSF paramilitary group who have been battling SAF since 2023, resulted in the massacre of at least 60,000 people.

The fall of the city came after an 18-month blockade in which the city’s population were deliberately starved into submission, according to a report from the UK-government funded think tank the Centre for Information Resilience.

Reports from aid organisations, UN investigators, and eyewitness accounts have previously found that rape was used on a mass scale by both sides.

In one incident, aid workers said at least 54 children were raped or sexually assaulted by RSF fighters while fleeing the city to Tawila, a town 25 miles west of El Fasher.

News.title: Wolff puts ‘tequila on ice’ with Antonelli two points away from title
News.content:
Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Ferrari’s Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs. Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

A late virtual safety car after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac ground to a halt by the side of the track made the final laps rather processional, denying the huge crowds at COTA the opportunity of seeing the fast-closing Hamilton take on Verstappen for the final podium spot.

That might have been fun, with Verstappen having lost his cool with his team midway through the race, furious that they didn’t order team-mate Hadjar out of the way when he came up behind him after stopping: “Thanks guys. Really good strategy there. Stuck in the dirty air.”

Incredibly, his third place finish in Austin means is the first time since the final race of 2020 that Verstappen has been out of title contention.

But it hardly mattered. The day belonged once again to Antonelli who should be champion by the end of next week. Not that he was getting carried away. “It was the result we needed,” he said. “The whole team deserved it so much, bringing this [upgrade] package. It was also the perfect execution with the strategy to do the one stop.”

Asked about the title, he added: “We’re very close, we try to finish on a high and hopefully we can finish it very soon. I mean, the perfect way will be to finish in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season. I’m very aware that it’s very close, but the mindset doesn’t change. I want to finish on a high to go into 2027 with momentum.”

“Yeah, what a boy, no?” Wolff said, admiringly. “I was just saying before, I got a question about whether he was nervous before the race, and I said, ‘Oh, he just sneaked into my office before getting ready and said, ‘I’m just going to enjoy this right now, and it’s weird, I’m not thinking about the championship at all. Isn’t that funny?’”

Wolff added that there would “definitely be a lot of tequila on ice” in Mexico. In hindsight it was always going to be a more appropriate venue to crown the sport’s youngest ever champion. Antonelli is not, after all, old enough to drink yet in the state of Texas.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1
News.content:
Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

News.title: Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off
News.content:
This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

Sports.title: Kieron Dyer reveals X-rated blast that sparked infamous Lee Bowyer fight amid ‘tension’ with ex-Newcastle team-mate
Sports.content:
Next

KIERON DYER has revealed the X-rated insult that sparked his infamous on-pitch brawl with Newcastle team-mate Lee Bowyer.

The former England midfielder had an extraordinary bust-up with Bowyer during the Magpies’ 3-0 defeat to Aston Villa in April 2005.



Both players were sent off in the game for trading punches in front of stunned supporters.

And Dyer, 47, has now admitted he effectively told Bowyer he was too rubbish to receive a pass.



Speaking to The Telegraph, he recalled snapping: “I’m not (passing) because you’re f****** s***”, although he stressed the exchange was only an approximate recollection.

The pair had to be separated by players from both teams as extraordinary scenes unfolded at St James’ Park.

But more than 21 years later, Dyer has revealed he was surprised to hear Bowyer claim there had been simmering tensions between the pair before the fight.

Bowyer recently suggested on Mick McCarthy and Tony Pulis’s podcast that they had been competing for the same position.

Dyer insisted “there was no tension from me” and rejected his former team-mate’s suggestion that he had deliberately avoided passing to him because he did not want Bowyer to shine.

The extraordinary incident saw both Newcastle stars shown straight red cards by referee Barry Knight as Graeme Souness’s side suffered a humiliating home defeat.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The former Ipswich star maintains he only threw a punch in self-defence and insists the incident was the only fight of his football career.

Despite the spectacular fallout, the pair have repaired their relationship and remain in contact today.

Sports.title: ‘You’re going to be fined for excessive beauty’ – Fans go wild for Eleonora Incardona as glam presenter stuns at game
Sports.content:
Next

DAZN presenter Eleonora Incardona took social media by storm as she put on a glam display while covering the Serie A.

Eleonora, 36, was on duty for Saturday’s thriller between Napoli and Roma at the Diego Armando Maradona Stadium.



The TV host posed in a smart rain coat before kick-off and shared a series of snaps on Instagram.

Eleonora added the following caption: “Match day 8. Napoli-Roma.”





And the Italian left her 1.5million followers in awe as they stormed the comments’ section.

One fan posted: “You’re going to be fined for excessive beauty.”

Another commented: “Beautiful.”

A third wrote: “Have a good evening.”



This fan said: “Wow wow wow wow!”

That one added: “The most beautiful!”

And a follower gushed: “She’s precious.”

Eleonora had a night to remember as the two Serie A giants played out an entertaining 3-3 draw in Naples.

Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa and Scott McTominay gave Napoli the lead before Matias Soule and Leonardo Ballerdi equalised for the visitors.



Ex-Manchester United ace McTominay put the hosts back in front but Ballerdi saved a point just a minute before full-time.

Sports.title: Former Tottenham star would have been world champion boxer if he wasn’t a footballer, says trainer
Sports.content:
Next

SEBASTIEN BASSONG could have been a WORLD CHAMPION boxer had he not pursued football, according to trainer Don Charles.

The esteemed Charles took time out of training two-time heavyweight champ Daniel Dubois to be in Bassong’s corner for A Night to Remember III last week.



The charity fundraising event, in which ex-footballers were pitted against each other in the ring, was headlined by Bassong’s bout with former Arsenal full-back Armand Traore after the original main event, between Nile Ranger and Jay Emmanuel-Thomas, was cancelled due to Ranger failing a pre-fight medical.

It was billed as a North London showdown between ex-Tottenham star Bassong and former Gunner Traore.



And Bassong, who also played for Newcastle, Wolves and Norwich during his time in the Premier League, looked mightily impressive as he dictated the scrap, which was waved off in round three.

Charles, who was interviewed in the ring, said: “It was very impressive. I knew he would do it. This guy is so driven and he’s such a competitor.



“He spars me and he gives me a bloody hard time.”

When asked if Bassong could have been world title material if he had got hold of him as a youngster, Charles responded: “Without a shadow of a doubt. Because of his competitiveness.

“He’s very, very competitive. Someone who has got that can do anything.”

Bassong came into the Pro Project Promotions event with some prior boxing experience, having developed a passion for the discipline since retiring from football in 2019.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The former Cameroon international told SunSport at the press conference in September: “I’ve been boxing for quite a while. I’ve been sparring.

“I was supposed to have a couple of fights by now. I got into it because of my competitiveness. I started taking it seriously two years ago.

“I’m an athlete so I was looking for something very intense.



“Nothing can replace football or get to the level of playing in front of 60,000 people. I was looking for something different, and that is what boxing gave me.”

Sports.title: Arsenal to play at Highbury stadium for first time in 20 years – but not all is as it seems
Sports.content:
BACK HOME Arsenal to play at Highbury stadium for first time in 20 years – but not all is as it seems







Next

ARSENAL fans may have done a double take when they saw this week’s game was at Highbury.

Hearing that name brings back memories of the club’s beloved old ground, which they left in 2006 to move into the Emirates Stadium.



But Gunners supporters and players will not be greeted by the famous marble halls of their former home when they arrive at Fleetwood Town for this Carabao Cup fourth-round clash.

The League Two side’s stadium might share the same name as the Gunners’ old home, but that is where the connection ends.



Fleetwood’s Highbury has a capacity of 5,327 and the lively atmosphere includes goals being celebrated with the theme tune from Captain Pugwash.

Arsenal fans had to listen to the can-can music at Bayern Munich last week, but if they conceded tonight it will be a children’s cartoon song adding to the misery.



Fleetwood stadium announcer Rod Allsworth said: “Other teams use songs like Glad All Over, but I said let’s be a little bit unique.

“What music is to do with a seafaring town? And I came up with Captain Pugwash. It’s loved by home fans – and absolutely hated by away fans. But it’s unique to Fleetwood Town.”

Arsenal and Fleetwood’s grounds sharing the name Highbury is purely a coincidence – and not due to any obscure unknown link between the two clubs.

Fleetwood moved into their home in 1939 and its name was born out of the fact it is on Highbury Avenue.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The ground has been redeveloped since then and the most recent refurb came in 2011, when the Parkside Stand was opened by none other than Fabio Capello.

The Italian, who was England manager at the time, is no stranger to the area as in 2007 it was revealed by The Sun he had a long-lost second cousin from the area.

Opposite the Parkside is the Highbury Stand and it is one of the most unique in English football.

Opened in 2008, it was built directly in front of the original main stand from 1939 – which is still standing.

It was not demolished at the time as the dressing rooms from it were still used, until the Parkside opened.



The stand has still not been knocked down, though, and fans at the game tonight will notice the old structure slap bang behind it.

Arteta and his players will use the newer dressing rooms on the other side of the ground.

The away ones are, of course, more basic than those used by Fleetwood.

Arteta would be a fan of the home dressing room as motivational quotes – such as ‘winning takes talent, to repeat it takes character’ – are splashed on the walls.

From there, players will head out a tunnel flanked by red lighting and accompanied by the words “this is our town”.

Fleetwood, who are 18th in League Two, cannot wait to host the Gunners and last Friday volunteers spent the day cleaning the ground.

Arsenal fans will make up 941 of the 5,327 at Highbury tonight after swiftly selling out their away allocation.

The club was originally given 841 tickets, but they landed another 100 due to the demand.



Some supporters have splashed out on away hospitality packages organised by Fleetwood.

They start at £250 per person, but ramp up in price depending on how much fans want to splash the cash.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The most high-end package offers 20 supporters the chance to take over the club’s old boardroom, the Harriet Lounge.

Any fans sitting there must be classed as fully signed-up members of the Prawn Sandwich Brigade, as a three-course dinner and all-inclusive drinks come before what should be a routine win for Arsenal.

Sports.title: Inside Man Utd’s shell-shocked dressing room with flops left ‘speechless’ after being mercilessly booed by fans
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED players were left “speechless” by the stick they received from supporters at the end of their 3-0 drubbing by Bournemouth.

United matchgoers sang head coach Michael Carrick’s name and applauded him on what was essentially a farewell lap at full-time ahead of his expected sacking.



Once Carrick headed down the tunnel, United fans in the Stretford End loudly and specifically booed the players.

A dressing room source admitted they were “lost for words” over the performance and the stick that the United squad received.



United sunk to a generational low with their third 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth within the last three years, with a different manager in charge for each one.

Carrick is expected to be sacked with United 16th after one win in eight games, while the club could clear the decks next year in the squad.

Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes are all at risk of being released or sold.

The quartet have entered the final year of their deals and Shaw, 31, has missed more games than he has played in through two separate injuries.

United have the option of an additional year on the contracts of Maguire, Martinez and Fernandes but Maguire turns 34 in March.

Martinez was recently fined for rounding on the United hierarchy over a lack of investment in the summer transfer window.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

His injury record and inconsistent form mean, as well as the fact Martinez turns 29 in January, mean he has little resale value.

Fernandes has struggled for form for two months and publicly questioned Carrick’s tactics after the 4-1 thrashing by Como.

Footballer of the year Fernandes received a mixed reception from the Stretford End when he warmed up in the 58th minute against Bournemouth on Sunday.

Fernandes, 32, remained an unused substitute and Carrick repeatedly said his absence from the line-up was a “pure football” decision.



MICHAEL CARRICK UPDATES: LATEST ON MAN UTD MANAGER’S FUTURE

Despite playing no part against Bournemouth, the United captain arrived at the club’s Carrington training complex on Monday morning for treatment. United players are on a day off.

Joshua Zirkzee, Mason Mount, Diogo Dalot, Noussair Mazraoui and Marcus Rashford also face uncertain futures next year.

Under 18 coach Darren Fletcher was among the arrivals at Carrington this morning. Fletcher took caretaker charge of United for two games in January.

Sports.title: Why is the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony in London?
Sports.content:
Next

THE 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony will take place TONIGHT – but in different surroundings.

England captain Harry Kane and Barcelona wonderkid Lamine Yamal are the front runners for the highest individual accolade in football.



BALLON D’OR LIVE COVERAGE

Kane can become only the fifth English player to win the Ballon d’Or and the first since Michael Owen in 2001.



The past seven editions of the iconic ceremony have been held at the Theatre du Chatelet in Paris.

But tonight, the world’s best player will be crowned in London at the legendary London Palladium.



SunSport brings you the reason for the change of scenery.

Why is the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony in London?

The Ballon d’Or ceremony has been moved to London to celebrate the 70th anniversary of the crowning of Sir Stanley Matthews.

The Blackpool and England icon was the very first winner of the trophy back in 1956.



Matthews, who won the Ballon d’Or at 41, remains the oldest recipient of the award.

Known as the ‘Wizard of the Dribble’, he narrowly edged out Real Madrid legend Alfredo Di Stefano to win the inaugural trophy.

Three years earlier, Sir Stan inspired his Blackpool team to come from 3-1 down against Bolton to win 4-3 in the 1953 FA Cup final, which is dubbed the ‘Matthews Final’.

How to watch Ballon d’Or 2026 FREE

Football fans worldwide can watch the entire ceremony without paying a penny.

Streaming giant DAZN has secured the exclusive broadcasting rights for the prestigious event.



Fans can access the live stream by signing up for a free DAZN account using just an email address.

The free broadcast on DAZN will include the red-carpet arrivals, pre-ceremony build-up and the main awards presentation, which starts at 8pm GMT.

Fans can also stream the ceremony live on the official Ballon d’Or website.

Sports.title: Chelsea’s front three backfires at worst possible time for Dream Team managers
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA players were supposed to dominate Gameweek 8.

Cole Palmer (£5.6m), Morgan Rogers (£5.5m) and Joao Pedro (£5.7m) were all among the most popular recruits ahead of the deadline as Dream Team managers decided to target a rare double header for the Blues, with good reason.

Xabi Alonso’s preferred front three has thrived in Dream Team this season, despite a lack of European fixtures.



After the first seven Gameweeks of the season, Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro had 25 goal involvements between them and more points than several top stars who are regularly active in midweek.



Hence why the trio were highly desirable assets for Gameweek 8, when the Carabao Cup round of 16 would give Chelsea’s top performers a second point-scoring opportunity.

The logic was sound but, as is often the way, reality proved to be unpredictable.

The problems began when Joao Pedro was revealed to be absent from the matchday squad to face Tottenham on Saturday.

Unbeknown to Dream Team bosses, the 28.1%-owned striker suffered a recurrence of the knee injury that forced him to withdraw from Brazil duty last month during Friday’s training session.

A build-up of fluid prevented a quick scan and the 25-year-old’s condition remains unclear but, at this stage, he’s not expected to feature away to Liverpool on Wednesday night.

An unexpected injury to the game’s second-most popular forward would have been bad enough but things didn’t get any better when the game kicked off at Stamford Bridge.



Palmer, Dream Team’s most selected midfielder, was given his marching towards in the form of a second yellow card in the 80th minute.

Spurs fans would argue the hosts’ No10 should have been shown a straight red for an aggressive barge into Mateus Fernandes (£3.3m) a few minutes before his early bath.

Consequently, the three points Palmer had earned up to the moment of his sending off were wiped out (red cards incur minus three points) to leave him with nothing.

And his Gameweek haul will remain zero as he will serve his one-game domestic suspension when Chelsea visit Anfield in the cup.



Rogers was not hindered by injury or disciplinary issues but his owners were not satisfied either as he scraped one solitary point from the 2-0 defeat.

The England international, who is the second-most popular midfielder right now with an ownership of 29.6%, was cautioned in stoppage time.

And so the three players who combined for 212 points across the first seven Gameweeks of the campaign managed just one from Saturday’s game, when expectations were sky high.

With Joao Pedro sidelined and Palmer suspended, Rogers is the only one with a chance at redemption on Wednesday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Looking further ahead, Chelsea will be back to just one fixture next Gameweek – a trip to Old Trafford – when nine other clubs will play twice courtesy of their European commitments.



At the time of writing, Palmer, (first), Joao Pedro (second) and Rogers (fifth) are among the most transferred-out players ahead of Gameweek 9.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes was Man Utd’s hero when he saved Solskjaer from sack… now he’s playing villain role under Carrick
Sports.content:
Next

BRUNO FERNANDES was Manchester United’s hero when he signed to help turn Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s season around – but the captain is now making headlines for all the wrong reasons under Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season, collecting just seven points from their opening eight games.



As a result, Carrick is under intense pressure after yesterday’s dismal 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

Yet there is still time to turn things around, and the parallels with Solskjaer’s early reign are striking.



If United beat Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, they will have matched their start to the 2019/20 campaign, when they had ten points after nine games.

Carrick was part of Solskjaer’s coaching staff back then.



But let’s go back to the Norwegian’s first three-and-a-half months in charge when United collected more Premier League points than any other side, outperforming even Manchester City and Liverpool between mid-December 2018 and the end of March 2019 – some achievement in a campaign when City finished on 98 points and Liverpool on 97.

But after Solskjaer was appointed permanent manager, United won just two of their next 12 matches in all competitions – the same statistic they have at the start of this season.

Back then, the slide continued into 2019/20, before a 1-1 draw against eventual champions Liverpool in United’s tenth league match offered a brief lift.

Including the Liverpool game, they then lost just one of their next nine games, but the improvement proved temporary with four defeats in their following seven matches – forcing the club into the January transfer market – the point when Fernandes arrived.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

7 Credit: Alamy Live News.

MICHAEL CARRICK UPDATES: LATEST ON MAN UTD MANAGER’S FUTURE

The Portuguese midfielder arrived from Sporting Lisbon and transformed United’s season.

He won the club’s Player of the Season award despite joining halfway through the campaign, underlining just how quickly he became their most influential player.

United finished the 2019/20 season unbeaten in their final 14 Premier League games, winning nine and drawing five to secure third place and Champions League qualification.



They may need a similarly dramatic recovery to reach Europe’s elite competition for 2027/28 — although, with this squad, the task looks increasingly difficult.

A January signing or two could yet change the picture, just as Fernandes did six years ago.

However, the man who once helped rescue United is now at the centre of a fresh crisis.

Fernandes enjoyed some of the best form of his career under Carrick last season, finishing with 21 assists and nine goals.

His 30 goal involvements equalled his tally from 2020/21, leaving him joint-record holder for goal involvements by a United midfielder in Premier League history.



But the relationship between captain and manager now appears under strain.

After United’s 4-1 defeat to Como in Italy on Wednesday, Fernandes openly questioned the team’s approach, suggesting they needed to be braver when pressing their opponents.

He told TNT Sports: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man. But sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence. They have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people frustrated.”



Asked whether United had got their tactics wrong, Fernandes added: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. I just said that I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.

“I think we started on the wrong foot again, and they scored very early. Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements without the ball, not many things going our way.

“Conceding the goal very early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat, and it’s very difficult to get out of that at the moment.”

Those comments came from the club captain and amounted to a public critique of the manager’s tactics.

Fernandes was then dropped to the bench for yesterday’s Bournemouth defeat and did not even come on, with United’s players were booed off the pitch while club legend Carrick received cheers from sections of the crowd throughout.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The contrast was stark. The captain who once arrived to help save a struggling United side is now watching from the sidelines as supporters turn against the team.

The question is whether the board still believe Carrick can turn things around, or whether another change is looming at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Sheikh Mansour doubles down on Man City commitment with £100m injection AFTER guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Sheikh Mansour doubles down on Man City commitment with £100m injection AFTER guilty verdict

Man City remain at the heart of a bitter legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of a number of financial charges but owner Sheikh Mansour continues to pour his money in

View 2 Images Sheikh Mansour has owned Manchester City since 2008 (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour has invested a further £100million into the City Football Group as the club’s appeal rolls on. The eight-time Premier League champions were found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League charges levelled at them last month.

‌



‌



They confirmed that they would be lodging an appeal, which will now be heard by another independent commission, and maintain their innocence. While that is ongoing, it appears that Mansour remains keen on pouring the money into the side and his footballing portfolio.

‌



Filings at Companies House have shown that the City Football Group have managed to raise around £100m by issuing 11,327,163 new shares. Mansour’s Newton Investment and Development purchased all of those shares, marginally increasing his majority holding in the company.

‌



The City Football Group are currently valued at just under £6billion, with Man City, Girona, Lommel SK, Troyes and Palermo among their European clubs. New York City, Montevideo City Torque, Bahia, Melbourne City and Shenzhen Peng City round off their portfolio.

Mansour has yet to speak out on the charges that City face, albeit CEO Ferran Soriano sent a lengthy message to staff in the aftermath of the guilty verdict.

He said: "This has gone for so long that it is important to remind ourselves that the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation - that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.

‌



"Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League commission that shows that it could not happen and that it did not happen. This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate that the money did not come from the owner. Every other false charge that has been thrown at us - and aggressively marketed and promoted - comes from the simple, central, and completely false accusation.

View 2 Images Sheikh Mansour has yet to speak out on the charges City face (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Surprisingly for us, and for our lawyers, after nearly two years the Premier League Commission has introduced an opinion that supports the Premier League's conspiracy theory. To do so, the opinion had to ignore the extensive evidence provided by the club in order to reach a conclusion that is clearly wrong.

"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and it is unsafe. Remember we have been here before. In 2020 we were also wrongly ruled against for many of the same issues. We appealed to an independent body in CAS and we won.

Article continues below

"We will now be relentless in our work. We will focus on the independent appeal process and also all other legal avenues available to us in order to win the case, and we will take all necessary action to protect the club and seek compensation from any party that tries to damage it now, and in the future.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick arrives at Man Utd training ground as bosses prepare for next move
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick arrives at Man Utd training ground as bosses prepare for next move

Michael Carrick was at the helm for another damaging defeat as Manchester United boss and has headed into Carrington ahead of a potential defining decision

View 2 Images Michael Carrick travelled into Carrington as his Man Utd future hangs by a thread

Michael Carrick is a man seemingly waiting for his fate to be sealed and has arrived at Carrington as the Manchester United hierarchy decide on their next move.

‌



‌



The United boss drove into the club's training ground on Monday afternoon, with talks expected to take place over the coming hours.

‌



Even before Sunday's loss at Bournemouth Carrick had presided over the club's worst start to a season in 40 years, but things went from bad to worse as they were outclassed by the Cherries, who picked up another 3-0 win at Old Trafford.

‌



It came in the same week that Carrick saw United beaten 4-1 in Como, before Bruno Fernandes took aim at his tactics, and the United boss appeared to do a lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday that had all the hallmarks of a farewell.

He was cheered by the home fans, who sang his name throughout, before turning on the players, who were jeered off. Carrick's demise has been rapid given the success he had last season, but the current run of results cannot continue.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌

United are languishing down in 16th and Carrick confessed that he would accept whatever was best for the club, where he was a serial winner as a player.

‌



He said: "Listen, it's a tough situation. There's no hiding from it. What it looks like, what's next, I really don't know. But I'll always do what's best for this football club. I've said it all along. I don't change that now. I love what I do, I love the position I'm in and I feel the responsibility, but we'll have to wait and see.”

United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox, who have copped the brunt of the anger and frustration for the club's poor start to the season, will be making the decision alongside co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with the axe potentially coming down on Monday.

‌



View 2 Images The former player is only 12 games into the new season, but could see his tenure prematurely ended

Sky Sports reports that United's bosses were already considering alternatives for the head coach role even before the defeat to Bournemouth and now former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, who left Germany in the summer, are the two frontrunners.

‌



Gary Neville said after Sunday's defeat: "They are probably going to sack him. Tomorrow (today), they will probably make a decision that will disgust Manchester United fans but it is probably necessary."

Since Ratcliffe came in to reshape the club he's already sacked Erik ten Hag and got rid of Ruben Amorim, who lasted just over a year, with their decision making heavily called into question.

Virgil van Dijk has told Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak that they need to deliver for Liverpool in every game before they can be considered a success.

‌



Wirtz, Barcola and Isak are shouldering a great deal of expectation after Liverpool invested a combined £364million on them. All three cost over £100m and are beginning to find their feet under Andoni Iraola.

‌



They were instrumental in the 2-0 win over Brighton on Sunday which was Liverpool fourth win in succession across all competitions. But the expensive trio have difficult acts to follow in the form of club legends Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mane and Roberto Firmino.

‌



Van Dijk enjoyed the success with their predecessors and says his current team-mates are aware of the expectations.

Sports.title: Lucky punter turns £4 into £1million jackpot with 12-fold football corner accumulator
Sports.content:
Lucky punter turns £4 into £1million jackpot with 12-fold football corner accumulator

The 45-year-old man, who was not named, defied odds of 249,345-1 to scoop £997,385 with a 12-fold accumulator on Saturday's English Football League matches

View 2 Images The man placed an accumulator on the number of corners in 12 games including Bromley against Peterborough (Image: Darren Woolley/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock)

A lucky football fan bagged a £1m jackpot with an astonishing £4 bet on the number of corners in 12 matches.

‌



‌



The man, 45, who was not named, defied odds of 249,345-1 to scoop the prize. He placed a 12-fold accumulator on Saturday's English Football League matches - netting him a return of £997,385.

‌



The punter bet just £4 that 12 games would have more than 11.5 corners each. The man, from Portsmouth, only learned of his success after the final whistles had blown. He said: "I didn't actually realise it had come in until about half an hour after all the games had finished.

‌



View 2 Images The punter's 12 matches included Preston against West Brom and QPR hosting Swansea (Image: Betfred)

"I'm an Aston Villa fan and was out with my son watching the early kick-off, which started the day really well. Then we walked back home and got soaked with the weather, and when I checked my account I couldn't believe it. I don't know how to describe it really. It was emotional, I felt a little bit sick at first making sure it was real, and then obviously the reality kicked in.

"My wife was out at the time when I checked, I needed her to come back to clarify the amount that was in there. I kept asking her, 'This is right, isn't it?' It didn't seem real. It's hard to put into words. I didn't sleep much last night, thinking about what we can do with the money. It's a really good feeling, it's brilliant."

‌



The punter now plans to spend more time watching Aston Villa with his son. The rest of the money is due to go towards paying off his mortgage, buying a new car for himself and his wife, plus a family holiday.

He said: "Me and some friends usually do an accumulator on the weekend for a bit of fun, we all pick a leg and put them in our group chat, both teams to score usually, and I like to do corners. I had £4 in my account so I decided to do one of my own with a few more corners in. I'm sure that I'll be treating my mates after winning this one, it will be my round all the time."

‌



The 12-fold accumulator consisted of 10 games in League One and two in the Championship, with the matches averaging 14 corners each. Among the fixtures which helped win the prize were Oxford Utd against Bradford, Reading against Barnsley, and Stevenage against MK Dons.

Betfair spokesperson Sam Rosbottom said: "We are absolutely delighted for this Portsmouth punter and couldn't be happier to pay out such a large sum of money. It's an incredible amount to win on a football accumulator; congratulations from everyone at Betfair."

‌



It is not the first time simple bets have landed big. Last year Arron Freeman and Kelly Dighton won £11.5m on Betfred's online slot game Mega Moolah with a £1.50 stake. Since then, the biggest winners in the betting firm's 58-year history splashed the cash. Arron has apparently bought a BMW M8, which costs £150,000 new.

Kelly, who has shared on TikTok her progress recovering from a drug addiction, showed off a mammoth diamond ring, said to be from Tiffany & Co. as she announced their engagement. In her videos she wears a £315 Gucci brooch and a diamond-encrusted Rolex, while talking about having face fillers, a Brazilian butt lift and liposuction in Turkey.

Article continues below

Arron, from Mulbarton, Norfolk, previously said he wants to sell his story so he can build a homeless shelter. He is said to have celebrated the win with champagne at the pub run by Kelly's parents in the town. Betfred founder Fred Done called him to offer his congratulations and invited him to Old Trafford as his guest.

Manchester United fan Arron said: "It was class of Fred to phone me. He told me to look after my cash and that is my plan. I've been a horse racing punter my whole life... but obviously never hit the jackpot like this. It was the missus' idea to give the casino a go. I love racing so I will still have a bet on the horses, but it will still be my normal small stakes."

Sports.title: 'Best in class, you're having a laugh' - Sir Jim Ratcliffe doesn't have a clue and should be embarrassed
Sports.content:
Sir Jim Ratcliffe is being hoisted by his own petard at Manchester United. Almost everything he has said about the club has come back to haunt him in the last 32 months.

It was in February 2024 when Ratcliffe's investment in the club was confirmed, and he sat in Ineos' Knightsbridge offices and talked confidently about what had gone wrong and how he intended to fix it.

Unfortunately for the British billionaire, he has discovered that in football, identifying the problems is the relatively simple bit. Actually fixing them is considerably more difficult than it might be in petrochemicals, report the Manchester Evening News.

On a churn through managers since Sir Alex Ferguson left, Ratcliffe said the "only conclusion you can draw is the environment in which they were working in didn't work."

‌



Ratcliffe is about to change managers at Old Trafford mid-season for the third season in a row. What does that say about the environment he has created since taking control of the club?

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It's fair to say that it's a rhetorical question. We've long since known that Ratcliffe doesn't really know what he's doing when it comes to running United. Supporters lumped him in the same bracket as the Glazer family long ago.

‌



The 74-year-old wasn't at Old Trafford for the latest capitulation against Bournemouth, but his ashen-faced executives were there. Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada copped plenty of flak from a fanbase that has seen enough and had enough.

But if Ratcliffe was watching on, and we can only presume he was, there was one moment that should have had him squirming on his expensive settee, wondering what on earth he had done since February 2024 and whether the only way to fix it now was to clean house.

'Best in class, you're having a laugh' rained down from the Stretford End after Bournemouth had made it 3-0 at Old Trafford once again. Ratcliffe's own catchphrase, the one he thought would lead to a turnaround in fortunes at United, was now being used against him.

And frankly, he must be having a laugh. Nobody in a position of power at Manchester United is best in class. Not off the pitch, and not on the pitch.

‌



"What you need are the foundations to be in a good place for Manchester United to be successful, which means that, from our point of view anyway, you need the right organisational structure," Ratcliffe said in February 2024.

"Which means not having a coach reporting to the chief executive, for instance, which is what they've got at the moment. You need the right organisational structure, and that's not going to be too complicated.

"Then we need to populate all the key roles with people who are best in class, 10 out of 10s, and there’s clearly a lot of interest in those roles in Manchester United, because it’s one of the biggest, if not the biggest football club in the world but it's also a fantastic challenge to take it from a difficult place to hopefully where it should be at the top of the pyramid. It does attract a lot of interest from very, very capable people. So we need to populate it with the right people, that sort of same thing."

View 2 Images Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Would Wilcox or Berrada rate their work as 10 out of 10? Wilcox fell into the role of director of football because Ratcliffe appointed the football executive widely considered the best in the country, a master at getting a structure right, only to sack him four months later because he didn't like him.

Remember when Dan Ashworth suggested the idea of appointing Ruben Amorim mid-season was a bad one, and that United might be better served going for a Premier League-proven head coach in Eddie Howe? Well, this is awkward, isn't it?

The only thing best in class at United is the ability to turn themselves into a punchline. The butt of the joke once again. However bad it gets at other big clubs, it always seems to be United who plumb the depths. Even Tottenham, twice surviving Premier League relegation by the skin of their teeth, now appear to be on an upward trajectory.

For the modern Manchester United, owned by absentee Americans intent on creaming every last cent they can off the club and run by a septuagenarian obsessed with building a new stadium that matchgoers don't want, we might only just be getting started when it comes to how bad it can get.

‌



Best in class, you're having a laugh.

Sports.title: Careers on the line for Australia in deciding South Africa Test?
Sports.content:
Australia are about to play a Test match in Cape Town for the first time since the ball-tampering scandal back in 2018 that paused a number of their cricketers' careers.

Should they lose to South Africa this week in the series decider, live on Sky Sports Cricket, a number of careers could be ended.

Having been humbled by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha last time out, a game in which they were torpedoed for 99 in the first innings, the Baggy Greens need a response.

If that does not come, the reaction from the Australian media could be more abrasive than the piece of sandpaper Cameron Bancroft aimed to conceal down his trousers eight years ago.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In 2018 footage emerged of Australia opener Cameron Bancroft using a foreign object to alter the condition of the ball against South Africa

The batting has been creaking for a while.

In the 4-1 Ashes thrashing of England last winter, it was held together by Travis Head, Steve Smith and Alex Carey as others toiled, while in South Africa so far the tourists have managed only three individual fifty-plus scores - one for Head and two for Matt Renshaw.

Without Head in Durban, things would have been even grislier. His second-innings 121 was 81 more runs than the next highest score by an Aussie in the game.

Even the great Smith - who received a ban for the role he played as skipper in 'Sandpapergate' in 2018, along with Bancroft and David Warner - has stuttered: three innings' in the 20s and a knock of three.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Steve Smith was dismissed by Marco Jansen in the first Test at Durban after being rapped on the gloves

He was hampered by a neck problem in Gqeberha and faces a late fitness Test ahead of the winner-takes-all Cape Town finale.

If he fails that, it could aid Marnus Labuschagne's hopes of staying in the side.

Labuschagne and selector Bailey under big pressure?

Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting had branded Labuschagne's spot as "untenable" after a lean return at home to Bangladesh left him without a Test century in 43 innings, stretching back to the 2023 Ashes in England. That has now extended to 47 innings.

Labuschagne has had no trouble starting in South Africa, the country of his birth - reaching the 30s in three of his four outings. But he has not kicked on.

Image: Australia's Marnus Labuschagne has not scored a Test century in over three years

Pinned lbw. Sliced loosely to cover. Brilliantly caught by Simon Harmer at gully. And then a criminal dismissal as he inexplicably holed out to long-on in the second innings of the second Test, a game Australia were trying to save.

If he misses out this week, it could be curtains. If he plays and fails, it could be a similar story. If Australia fail as a team, perhaps pressure will mount on head selector George Bailey?

Former skipper Steve Waugh said before the Ashes that Bailey has previously shown a lack of "appetite" to make the big calls, while the selection of the now-jettisoned Nic Maddinson for the South Africa tour was panned at the time by Matthew Hayden.

Maddinson ditching after recall highlights Australia's issues

Maddinson, 34, had not played a first-class game since March 2025 due to a testicular cancer diagnosis and averaged 6.75 from his first three Tests back in 2016.

Hayden accused selectors of "disrespecting first-class cricket" and "promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we've seen in a generation of cricket."

Image: The selection of Nic Maddinson was criticised and the 34-year old has now been dropped from the Australia squad after failing to score big runs in South Africa

Maddinson has not been as good as mediocre in this series, with his average a paltry 14 after amassing only 56 runs from four knocks - 48 of which came in one innings to punctuate a 33-ball duck, a four-ball duck and a 10-ball eight.

He has since been released from the squad, with Renshaw poised to open alongside Head in Cape Town.

Considering what he went through health-wise, people were rooting for Maddinson to perform but he hasn't. It raises the question over whether a younger player should have been given a go instead.

Ollie Davies, Sam Konstas and Campbell Kellaway were options. Nathan McSweeney, too.

The problem Australia have is that unlike in previous eras when they had players averaging north of 40 and banging out domestic runs - often in English county cricket as well as at home - waiting in the wings, they don't now.

All of the prospects mentioned above average mid-30s or lower in first-class cricket.

Will Bavuma extend excellent record as captain?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player South Africa captain Temba Bavuma scored a superb 179 from 334 balls in the second Test

South Africa, by contrast, have a pretty much guaranteed source of runs in captain Temba Bavuma, whose brilliant 179 from 334 balls in Gqeberha means he is averaging 49.95 across his last 28 Tests.

His nuggety ton last time out was scored after he came in at 12-2.

He was at the other end as the Proteas slumped to 110-6 before pushing them to 425-9 and was ultimately left to celebrate a 12th win in 14 Tests as skipper.

This feels like a great chance to make that 13 from 15 unless Australia are able to pull something out of the bag in Cape Town.

Unlike in 2018, something within the rules this time.

Sports.title: Makin wants to be Liverpool's next great champion
Sports.content:
Middleweight Callum Makin has excelled for the GB boxing team, but his Olympic future rests on a decision.

Makin has won medals for Britain at both the World and European championships at 75kgs. But, with Olympic qualification looming next year, he has to choose his weight category.

With 75kgs no longer an Olympic weight Makin has to move up or move down by five kilos.

Although he became a national champion twice over at light-middleweight, Makin expects to bulk up for his Olympic qualification campaign.

"It's either 70 or 80kgs for me, which is a massive jump either side," Makin told Sky Sports.

"I'm looking at doing 80 kilos and I'm going to progress on that. I'm going to go up a weight and build into a new weight.

"It's something that I'm confident of doing. With the right team around me, I'll be able to progress in that weight.

"It's a big ask to keep performing day after day, while getting your weight really low. I'd rather be boxing 100 per cent and giving everything."

Image: Callum Makin wants to follow in Liverpool's fine tradition of producing great fighters

Makin is still only 22 years old and a proven international medal winner. His bronze medal at the recent European Championships in Bulgaria backs up the bronze he won at the World Championships in his Liverpool hometown.

"I'm glad to come home back with another medal," he said. "With it being in Liverpool, the World Championships, there was a lot of pressure on me to do well, thankfully I did.

"Out in Bulgaria it was a little bit different. More relaxed and just focusing on the fight more than anything. Just mainly [thought] go out there and enjoy it, and I did.

"[The Worlds] was great for me as well, especially medalling in such a big tournament, the icing on the cake. It's definitely a memory that I'll always be thankful for and never forget as well."

Makin is targeting the Los Angeles Games in 2028, but longer term wants to follow in Liverpool's fine tradition of professional fighters.

"Especially with a lot of great champions that have come from the city, that's always been a massive dream of mine, to follow in their footsteps and create a story for myself," he said.

"I have ambitions of being a world champion and one of the best in the world, that's my aim come the end of my career.

"We're very well known for our great crowds and how we back our fighters, not even fighters but sportspeople. We get behind them and support them massively. It would be great one day to bring a massive fight to Liverpool and give the fans what they deserve and perform in front of them."

But Makin concluded: "It's all focused now on the Olympic qualifications which will be next year.

"I'm looking forward to a busy end of the year and a massive focus to next year."

Sports.title: How worried should England be after another unfathomable defeat?
Sports.content:
It's not just Manchester United who've had a chastening week.

The England cricket team have shown they are more than capable of crumbling, too.

If losing once from a dominant position could be considered misfortune then to do it twice in four days is just plain careless.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from last Thursday's ODI as Sri Lanka stunned England by pulling off a chase of 430 - the second-highest in the format's history

If you look at the last two games, we've been in positions where we should have won, so that is a massive positive as a group. If in a year's time we do get to those situations again and bank on our previous experiences then we'll look back at this tri-series as a huge positive.

That is not to denigrate the achievements of Sri Lanka for chasing down a colossal 430 and Pakistan for their successful pursuit of 242 after having been 154-9. Those should be lauded.

But they did expose a few cracks in England that were not really visible during the home ODI summer as Harry Brook's team recorded bilateral series wins over India and Sri Lanka.

England are not in the disarray Manchester United are. The coach won't be sacked and the captain is unlikely to be dropped for slamming the coach's tactics. But there are things to fix. Some easy, others a little more difficult.

England missing senior players, including Archer

It is worth noting that an England side sat on three defeats from three in the tri-series - they lost their first game against Pakistan after botching a chase of 303 - is missing some key personnel.

Image: England's Jos Buttler (left) and Jofra Archer (right) are missing the tri-series through injury and rest respectively

Jos Buttler (injured), Jacob Bethell (recovering from injury) and Jofra Archer (rested) are not here. Adil Rashid has not been picked for the last two matches. Josh Tongue missed Sunday's loss.

Having Rashid - whose recent omission has been somewhat of a mystery - and Archer would clearly have bolstered the bowling, while Bethell and Buttler could have acted as strong sounding boards for Brook when things started to unravel in the field.

Bethell and Buttler's absences were also keenly felt with the bat as, let's be honest, that is where this weekend's game was lost.

The Lahore strip was not the Rawalpindi road on which England and Sri Lanka struck a combined 859 runs but neither was it a minefield.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of Shadab's unbeaten hundred in Lahore as he put on a match-winning 89-run partnership with last man Haris Rauf

The fact Pakistan's No 8 (Shadab Khan) scored 113 not out and England's No 10 (Gus Atkinson) hit an unbeaten 36 shows you that.

England's 241 all out was under par. They should probably never have defended it. It's just the way they failed to defend it that rankled.

The lack of middle-overs wickets that blighted England against Sri Lanka - and has done in ODIs for some time - was not an issue versus Pakistan as Jamie Overton and Liam Dawson excelled.

This time the problems came when their opponents were nine down.

Image: What role should Sam Curran have in England's ODI side?

England's Curran conundrum

During the dismal 2025 Champions Trophy campaign in Pakistan - losing all three of their games - England were crying out for the variety Sam Curran's left-arm box of tricks provides.

Since his white-ball reinstatement, Curran has made a difference, notably with a clutch final over as England staved off a humbling defeat to Nepal in the T20 World Cup in India earlier this year.

But he has had a tough time in Pakistan over the last few days, perhaps owing to the rustiness caused by missing the last two months with a groin injury.

None of Curran's variations have really worked.

His moon balls, bouncers and yorkers have been more predictable than Manchester United getting to the autumn and changing manager. A stage we may be at again.

Image: Sam Curran (right) recorded the most-expensive England ODI bowling figures against Sri Lanka, with 2-103 from nine overs

Curran's 42 with the bat helped rally England from 52-4 against Pakistan and, in isolation, his bowling figures of 0-32 from eight overs are solid. That doesn't tell the entire story, though.

In his fifth, sixth and seventh overs, Curran offered up boundary balls to Shadab and then a single, while also failing to sufficiently test No 11 Haris Rauf when he had the opportunity.

Three days prior, the all-rounder was flogged for England's most-expensive ODI bowling figures as Brook persevered with him for too long. Curran's 2-103 from nine overs against Sri Lanka trumped his own 0-98 from 9.5 overs versus West Indies back in 2023.

Stuart Broad is one of many who think you get the best out of Curran when he has a defined and prominent role - and England need to work out what that is as he feels rather bit-part at the moment. If his toils with the ball continue that could be no part.

McCullum: England 'gutted' by ODI defeats England head coach Brendon McCullum: “We will learn from this. The boys are gutted, to be honest. They were gutted after the last game and they're even more gutted after this one. "These boys are immensely talented, they're incredibly driven to perform for England. “We know that we're not the best side that we can be just yet but that's the challenge that's in front of us. "There's some good lessons and learning opportunities and we will learn from it because we are desperate to get to South Africa and have a realistic chance of challenging for that World Cup. “When you've got an inexperienced line-up and you've got a big World Cup in 12 months' time and you've only got 20 games between now and then, you need to have that level of communication and those examples of real time experiences."

Should Overton continue to excel in the middle overs, banging out a hard length and nabbing crucial wickets Liam Plunkett-style, and offer a bit more with the bat than he is currently doing, Curran could be at risk, especially if England want to get another out-and-out seamer into the XI as they prepare for the 2027 World Cup in Africa.

Why is Rashid not playing?

They also need to find a way for Rashid to return to the side at some stage - unless the leg-spinner's recent absence is because they have moved on from a man who has been a linchpin for well over a decade.

The fact Rashid, 38, is in the squad to tour Australia next month would suggest not. His spell on the bench is perhaps due to still working back to full fitness following a hand injury that ended his home summer prematurely.

But his ODI figures in 2026 have not been amazing - nine wickets in seven games at an average of 36.22 and a strike-rate of 37.50 after a quality 2025 when he averaged two wickets a game (30 in 15 fixtures at an average of 23.63 and strike-rate of 24.10).

Image: Adil Rashid has been left out of England's last two ODIs

Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain said last week that Rashid's performances had "dropped off".

Rashid being omitted for Liam Dawson - who has done excellently in the tri-series, it must be said - for tactical reasons in Rawalpindi and again in Lahore has raised questions that were not there before.

Questions across the board are inevitable when you fluff your lines twice in a week. At least coach Brendon McCullum, perhaps unlike Michael Carrick at Manchester United after the Como and Bournemouth drubbings, will be around to try and provide the answers.

Sports.title: Kane, Mbappe and Lamine Yamal - who should win men's 2026 Ballon d'Or?
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, which could be one of the tightest results in recent history.

England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

Victory would see Kane become just the fifth English winner of the Ballon d'Or after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen, while he would also become the first Bayern player to claim it in 45 years.

When asked after Bayern's Champions League draw against Arsenal last Wednesday about winning the Ballon d'Or, Kane told Sky Sports News: "It'd be incredible if I do. It'd be special for sure. I'd love to win it, but we will have to wait and see. A big night, but I'm not getting carried away."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane gives his thoughts ahead of Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony

Kane's caution comes due to stiff competition from LaLiga duo Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Spain World Cup winner and Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal, who is 14 years Kane's junior at the age of 19, is aiming to become the youngest-ever Ballon d'Or winner - an award he has been campaigning for.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News’ David Reed delves into whether or not age has an impact on who wins the Ballon d'Or

"Being completely honest, it's not just this year I've been at a Ballon d'Or [winning] level, but longer," he told The Guardian in September, having also appeared to dismiss Kane's credentials earlier that month in a Spanish interview.

Lamine Yamal had been the bookmakers' closest challenger to Kane for the award, but a late surge in the betting means Real Madrid striker and France captain Kylian Mbappe is now second-favourite behind Kane.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kylian Mbappe's double gave Real Madrid a win at rivals Barcelona on Sunday

A first-time winner looks set to win the award on Monday night, with Kane eyeing a poetic victory in London, where the ceremony is being held to pay tribute to inaugural winner Matthews.

Here, Sky Sports assesses Kane, Lamine Yamal and Mbappe's stats, and hears the pundits' views on who should win the 70th edition of the Ballon d'Or…
