The honours…

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' David Reed explains the complicated process behind how the Ballon d'Or winner is chosen

It is important to note that players are judged for their performances over the entirety of last season from August 3, 2025 until July 19, 2026.

Looking at that period domestically, Kane helped Bayern to lift the Bundesliga and the German Cup, while Lamine Yamal won LaLiga but missed out on the Copa del Rey as both players won their respective Super Cups.

But Mbappe failed to win a trophy with either Real Madrid or France last season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We take a look at all Harry Kane's goals for Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga last season

In Europe, Kane went further than Lamine Yamal and Mbappe as Bayern reached the Champions League semi-finals after a thrilling 6-5 last-four aggregate defeat to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain.

Lamine Yamal's Barcelona and Mbappe's Real Madrid both exited the tournament in the quarter-finals.

But Lamine Yamal enjoyed the ultimate success with his country as he helped Spain earn World Cup glory in the summer, while Kane and England won the bronze medal after beating Mbappe's France in the third-place play-off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at Lamine Yamal's best league goals for Barcelona last season

The stats…

The goal statistics are what make Kane the favourite for the award.

He hit an astonishing 73 goals for club and country last season, while Mbappe fired in 58 and Lamine Yamal scored 25 goals.

Kane's goal-laden campaign led to the ex-Tottenham striker picking up the Golden Shoe, the award for Europe's leading goal scorer, for a second time after he claimed it in 2023/24 in his debut Bayern season.

Kane hit 61 goals for Bayern across all competitions last season, 19 more than any other player in Europe's big-five leagues. In fact, it was the most by a player in a season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014/15.

Kane also scored 12 goals for England, with his six goals in the Three Lions' 2026 World Cup semi-final run seeing him become England's all-time leading World Cup scorer.

But Mbappe scored more goals than Kane at the World Cup and in last season's Champions League.

The ex-PSG forward won this year's World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals - the most by a player in a single edition since Gerd Muller scored 10 in 1970 for West Germany.

The 27-year-old is now the all-time scorer in World Cup history with 22 goals.

At club level last season, Mbappe was the top goal scorer in LaLiga (25 goals) and in the Champions League, despite Real's last-eight exit, as he scored 15 goals - one more than Kane.

It was a quiet World Cup for Lamine Yamal, scoring only once in Spain's run to glory as team-mates Rodri and Pau Cubarsi picked up the player of the tournament and young player award, respectively.

Lamine Yamal, however, came into his first World Cup off the back of a hamstring injury which had initially led to doubts whether he would even play in the tournament.

Lamine Yamal picked up the injury in mid-April while playing for Barcelona, and he missed the remainder of the season before making his return as a substitute in Spain's goalless draw in their World Cup opener against Cape Verde on June 15, with his first start coming six days later as he scored Spain's first in their win over Saudi Arabia.

Despite his disrupted preparation for the tournament, he made the most dribbles both at the World Cup (58) and across Europe's top-five leagues (265) during the 2025/26 season.

Where Lamine Yamal is superior to Kane and Mbappe is in the assist column.

The winger provided 20 assists for club and country last season, while Mbappe had 13 and Kane had just eight.

It takes Lamine Yamal's goal involvements to 45, but that figure is not close to Kane's 81 and Mbappe's 71.

The pundits have their say...

Jamie Carragher: "Kane should win the Ballon d'Or and the reason is because he's scored 73 goals in a season and only Lionel Messi has scored more in a season.

"He also won the double with Bayern Munich and was part of an England team that got to the World Cup semi-finals."

Paul Merson: "It's such a hard one because Kane's scored a million goals and has been phenomenal, but Lamine Yamal's been phenomenal too and he's won the World Cup.

"But I'm hoping Kane because Lamine Yamal's going to win it three to five times in years to come, so I'd like Kane to win - and it's in London, which ticks another box.

"So I'd just go with Kane, but I wouldn't be shocked if it wasn't him."

Tim Sherwood: "Kane should win the Ballon d'Or - and I'm not being biased. I think he's had an unbelievable season with the amount of goals he's scored for Bayern Munich.

"There's a lot of pressure playing for big club like Bayern, but he never feels the pressure and he continues to score for England. If he doesn't win it now, then he never will."

Sue Smith: "Kane has got to win the Ballon d'Or. He's been absolutely brilliant. His goals, his movement, the way he drops into the No.10, the ability he's got and he's been outstandingly consistency."

Michael Dawson: "I believe it should be Kane. I'm probably slightly biased as I was lucky to play with him. The goals and everything he's given in the last year, he has to be the winner but Lamine Yamal is the guy he has to beat."

Clinton Morrison: "Kane should win because he's had a fantastic season at Bayern Munich and he leads England by example. Lamine Yamal and Michael Olise could dominate for years to come, but Kane thoroughly deserves it this year."

A third year in a row for a first-time winner?

Sports.title: Verstappen fumes at Red Bull radio dropouts during races
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen says technical issues with Red Bull's team radio are "a disaster" after he struggled to communicate with his engineer for a second successive race.

On his way to finishing third in Sunday's United States Grand Prix, Verstappen was trying to let the Red Bull pit wall know he was suffering from engine braking issues.

When his engineer attempted to offer him advice by suggesting a change of mode, Verstappen said that he couldn't hear him properly.

The issue appeared to be similar to the one Verstappen suffered two weeks earlier when he and the pit wall were forced to improvise their communication methods during his win in Singapore.

Speaking after Sunday's race in Austin, Verstappen said: "It's not the second time. It's already, I don't know how many times this year.

"Maybe we should just start communicating in sign language. It's probably cheaper as well.

"It's a disaster. Yeah, it's a disaster. It's really frustrating, to be honest."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Both Red Bulls suffer technical issues as Max Verstappen admits car is 'undrivable'

'The same always at the start'

Verstappen and his team-mate Isack Hadjar were both also frustrated with another race where they both made poor starts.

The Dutchman was overtaken by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc on the opening lap after being left vulnerable from a poor start, while Hadjar was cleared by both Leclerc and his team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

Verstappen told Sky Sports F1: "Just the same always at the start, the problem we have."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli got a flying start at the United States Grand Prix as George Russell was handed a five-second penalty

Hadjar went into more detail, telling Sky Sports F1: "My race start was… I do everything perfect in terms of procedure and I have clutch over delivery. These things are out of my control.

"I have poor radio coverage, can't hear what's happening, can't hear what's happening in the pits. I leave the pits with the wrong map, then I lose a second every lap on that hard tyre.

"It needs a redesign. That's it. The clutch. It's too fragile. It's not coping well with temperatures. It's a real struggle."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

Mekies: It's making everyone's lives difficult

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said the radio issue was "making everyone's lives very difficult" within the Milton Keynes squad.

"We are all frustrated to struggle for the second race in a row with the radio issues," Mekies said. "It's making everyone's lives very difficult.

"So, it is true that it's something that we would like to fix quite quickly, because it's an item that should be working without using too much of our energy."

Mekies also admitted that while he feels Red Bull's starts are improving, they can't become "the benchmark" before the end of this season due to the presence of issues that will only be possible to fix during the winter.

"The start is a slightly more complex issue to solve, meaning that the start performance is going across pretty much all the departments of the company, probably except aerodynamics," Mekies said.

"It's engine, it's gearbox, it's clutch, it's many things. We have certainly seen from the beginning of the season that we are not the benchmark in terms of launch performance.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

"As much as we have reduced the gap to competition, and you may remember how bad our starts were at the beginning of the year, we are still not the benchmark.

"The fact that the car in the meantime improved a lot and is fighting closer to the front makes that deficit even more painful now, because competition around us is very strong.

"On one side, I'm confident that we will continue to reduce the gap to the competition from now to the end of the year, because every race we learn, every race we come up with small ways to close the gap.

"On the other side, I equally know that we will not be the benchmark before the end of the season, that it will require significant design and hardware changes, and that this is something that we will see only next year."

Sports.title: Thunder star Williams stretched off with leg injury
Sports.content:
Jalen Williams: Oklahoma City Thunder star stretchered off with significant leg injury in win over Los Angeles Clippers

Oklahoma City Thunder guard Jalen Williams suffered a significant injury during their victory on Sunday

Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams was taken off the court on a stretcher after suffering a significant lower-leg injury during their 108-101 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.

Williams - a shooting guard who entered Sunday having averaged 18 points per game in his first 250 NBA contests - has been an All-Star and an All-NBA player already in his career, was a huge part of the Thunder team that won the 2024-25 NBA title.

He injured his lower left leg and saw his ankle turn in an unnatural angle in a drive with 1:14 remaining, with Williams immediately treated by medical personnel after going down underneath the basket on the Thunder's offensive end.

Williams' ankle was draped by towels before a stretcher was brought out, with players left visibly shaken by the incident and the game stopped for around five minutes before the Thunder completed their victory.

Williams looked emotional after seeing his injury before going off to a standing ovation

"Just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said in a post-match interview, fighting back tears as he spoke. "Nothing more than that."

Williams, seated up on the stretcher, saluted the cheering fans with two thumbs-up signals as he was wheeled off the court.

There was no immediate diagnosis from the Thunder, though it was clear that the injury was severe - and the stretcher was called for within just a few seconds of the play ending.

Oklahoma City coach Mark Daigneault said the team would be briefed Monday morning with the latest updates on Williams' condition.

"Our whole city will have JDub in our thoughts and prayers as he deals with this adversity and as he makes his way through his recovery," Oklahoma City Mayor David Holt posted on social media after the game.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Williams missed 49 games last season with an array of issues, mostly hamstring problems and recovery from a significant surgery on his right wrist.

"He just loves playing, loves the competition," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "That's who he is. It's unfortunate, his luck so far. But he's equipped for it."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick attends Manchester United training ground as club discuss his fate
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick was at Manchester United’s training ground on Monday afternoon as elsewhere at the Carrington base Jason Wilcox, the sporting director, and Omar Berrada, the chief executive, deliberated whether to sack the head coach.

Carrick arrived at about 1.50pm to watch the under-21s play a behind-closed-doors game.

Wilcox and Berrada met at Carrington on Monday morning after United’s 3-0 loss to Bournemouth on Sunday at Old Trafford that left Carrick’s job in the balance. Wilcox departed just before 5pm and Carrick went shortly after.

The defeat made it eight games without a win for Carrick’s side, who have two victories all season. United are in 16th in the Premier League, a point above the relegation zone.

If the 45-year-old is removed, Eddie Howe remains Wilcox’s preferred candidate, with contact between them understood to have been made. The former Newcastle manager is open to taking up the position, subject to negotiations.

Howe would be less expensive to recruit than Unai Emery, another admired manager, because Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the ­Spaniard.

Julian Nagelsmann, the former Germany and Bayern Munich head coach, is highly regarded by Christopher ­Vivell, United’s head of ­recruitment, who is believed to have sounded out his fellow German, but Wilcox’s view may hold more sway with Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who ­controls football policy at United. Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, is another who may be in the frame.

Carrick dropped Bruno Fernandes for the Bournemouth loss for “pure football reasons”, he said. This came after the 32-year-old criticised Carrick for his tactics in last Wednesday’s 4-1 loss at Como.

The captain was an unused substitute and was booed, along with other players, by fans in the Stretford End at the end of the defeat by Bournemouth.

On Monday Fernandes liked an Instagram post that said: “Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care.” The post also said: “The person holding everything together is usually the one nobody thinks to check on.”

Sports.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
José Mourinho had already done the por qué?, the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench, but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists.

He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600km west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out.

“We have the best goalkeeper in the world, but none of us cried because Thibaut couldn’t play,” Mourinho said. Plenty might have felt like it, more reason to be fearful. But the coach called Andriy Lunin, the sub goalkeeper so serious he bought a roll of astroturf and spent the pandemic diving round the living room of his flat, and told him this was his moment: “You train to play, not to sit on the bench, so go on.” As for the rest of them, the manager told them nothing changes: the plan remains in place. By the time they headed back to the dressing room, “Fucking get in!” echoing along the Camp Nou corridor, so it had proved.

Thirteen years later, Mourinho was back in Barcelona for a clásico and he had guided Madrid to a 2-1 win. It wasn’t supposed to be like this, or maybe it was. Barcelona, the team who had won nine in a row, banging in 4.3 goals per game, had been beaten by Madrid, the team who had lost twice already and, truth be told, were mostly just not very good. The night it could have been all over, the title race done when it’s not even in November, was instead the night it finally started. “If you leave here nine points behind, it’s very heavy psychologically; if it’s six, it’s more balanced; if it’s three, that’s different,” Mourinho said.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho returned to where it all began to continue his unbeaten streak against Barcelona. Photograph: Joan Monfort/AP

This was different, and so is the season now. Counting the clásicos all those years ago, Mourinho racked up his sixth consecutive meeting with Barcelona without defeat, and there had been no parked bus, nor many lumps kicked. They didn’t just desperately hang on, although there was a moment when Dean Huijsen saved a shot with his face. Nor had they just waited for a moment, resisting and then robbing it, even if João Cancelo did insist: “That’s Madrid; they don’t have many chances but they score them.” The final shot count said 18-10 to Barcelona, and possession was 62% Barcelona’s.

“The way we won is important: you can win luckily or by defending a lot. But we won with calmness and totally deservedly. We did it by being organised, concentrated and having the courage to come out from the back,” Mourinho said. And if that might have been pushing it a little – and, let’s face it, the analyses might be different had Lunin not made an astonishing save from Gerard Martín or Lamine Yamal’s second-half shot not faded just past the post – he had a point.

Barcelona were not at their best. They had been hurried and imprecise, Rodri telling his teammates to lower their “pulse rate” as they came out for the second half. Lamine Yamal somehow missed an extraordinary chance just before the break. And when they did tighten the screw in the second half, they couldn’t break the wall. Xavi Espart was forced off, yet another injury at the back, the failure to sign a centre-back in the spotlight again. Yet this was still a faster, more aggressive, tighter Madrid than anyone expected. Asked to define it, Lunin went for “discipline and attitude”. And if that is partly about occasion, the least you can ask for, it’s more than you sometimes get.

View image in fullscreen Andriy Lunin stepped up for Real Madrid in the absence of the ill Thibaut Courtois. Photograph: Jose Breton/AP

Besides, it was also more than that. More than Marc Cucurella getting under Lamine Yamal’s skin, although he certainly succeeded. They went for the space beyond Barcelona’s full-backs: superb in his first clásico, aged 19, Yan Diomandé – the left winger – got more touches than any Madrid player, and protected his full-back as well. But it was more than that, too. More than the wonderful winning goal, a flash of inspiration with Jude Bellingham going all Nureyev, the ball flitting between his feet and Gabriel Jesus’s legs, pirouetting to release Eduardo Camavinga. This was a team with an idea and a victory that vindicated their manager, some kind of resurrection.

Before the game, Rodri said that one of Madrid’s tricks is to convince you that they’re not that good, but insisted he wouldn’t fall into that trap. Still he felt that plan particularly. Pedri did too. Bellingham dealt with Rodri, Bernardo Silva with Pedri. Pressed and tired too, according to Hansi Flick, neither truly took control. The inclusion of Arda Guler and Silva – the surprise in the middle, starting his first league game in six weeks – underlined an intention for Madrid to keep the ball when the could. They actually had a midfield, which was new. From the back they tried to build, draw Barcelona in. And if a time came when they had to wait, to put bodies in before the ball, well, they would do that too. Six times Barcelona shots were blocked. At least twice more, shots were taken from their toes. At the other end, meanwhile, Madrid attacked with an intent and an incision that probably drew the clearer chances: the xG showed 1.19 v 1.94.

Thank you for your feedback.

Victory puts Madrid three points behind Barcelona and, Federico Valverde claimed, “will give us a kickstart”. It has taken 10 weeks but it’s game on. Hay liga, as they like to say. There is league. There is Madrid too. Something has shifted, starting in Rome, where 70 dreadful minutes gave way to 20 pretty good ones, another inexplicable comeback actually having something of an explanation too. The changes were impossible to ignore. Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni no longer the partnership in the middle, Valverde going to right-back instead. Guler playing. Diomandé playing. And, yes, Vinícius Júnior not playing. “I’m not stubborn; I can change,” Mourinho said. Madrid have won five in a row now; something was seen that night, a way ahead. They’ve won every game since Vinícius was suspended, facile and perhaps even cruel though that may be to say. And since Mourinho grew a beard, if you believe in that kind of thing.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé celebrates the goal that leaves Real Madrid only three points behind Barcelona in the league. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters

Before the clásico, Mourinho had said it wasn’t fair to compare his team, a side in construction and a long way from the finished product, to Barcelona. He insisted that he was still getting to know his players; he hadn’t been there long, after all. After the clásico, he admitted: “We have improved, we can’t hide that.” The idea has shifted, almost like it was an epiphany: “I’ve learned something about the middle of the pitch; I have learned that a mixture is better, that it is better to have a combination of qualities than two players of similar characteristics.” In short, Tchouaméni and Valverde doesn’t work. There needs to be some football in there somewhere, and so a shift started. Sunday came as a kind of confirmation, a hope, an identity emerging.

“The best Madrid is born at the Camp Nou,” ran the headline in El País. “Madrid are here now,” AS’s cover said. “I won’t let them have their heads on the moon; if we win this and then don’t win at the Sardinero, it won’t mean much,” Mourinho said, but this was a start, not just an end in itself. At full-time, Mourinho headed on to the pitch and shook Lunin’s hand as all around players embraced. High in the north-east corner, Madrid’s fans stayed and sang. Back home, Courtois was watching. He had “a horrible night” on Saturday, they said, but now he was feeling a little better. They all were.

Sports.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager. Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it.

But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically?

It’s worth remembering where all this began. The United story has taken on the aspect of a classical tragedy and, like all good tragedies, it begins with a small, seemingly unconnected moment, amplified by pride, that ends up bringing the whole edifice crashing down.

In 1999, Mull of Kintyre, a horse owned by the Irish millionaire John Magnier, won the Gimcrack Stakes at York. Traditionally, the winning owner would give a speech at the Gimcrack Dinner, but Magnier was a shy man who hated public speaking so he asked his friend, the United manager Alex Ferguson, to give the speech on his behalf. The racing establishment, though, refused: it had to be the owner. To spite them, Magnier named Ferguson as the owner of another horse, Juniper. The following year, Juniper was narrowly beaten in the Gimcrack Stakes. Magnier, though, was determined. So the year after that, he made Ferguson the owner of Rock of Gibraltar, which had won its first three races. Rock of Gibraltar won the Gimcrack easily and Magnier, waving a metaphorical two fingers at the racing authorities, watched Ferguson give the speech.

Magnier was largely making mischief, but he was also happy to do a favor for a friend, to give Ferguson a better experience of racing, and he benefited from the association of the horse with such a famous name. In addition, Ferguson did not get on well with the United chairman, Martin Edwards, and had a sense that football clubs were becoming good investments. Accordingly Magnier and his associate JP McManus bought shares in United. (The full story is explored by the journalist David Walsh here).

It turned out, though, that Rock of Gibraltar was a much better horse than anybody had realized, winning seven Group One races in a row. The stud fees would be worth tens of millions of pounds. Ferguson believed the verbal deal was that he could choose 50% of the prize money won by Rock of Gibraltar (about £800,000) or 50% of the stud fees, which ended up being worth tens of millions. He went for the latter. Magnier’s recollection was rather different: 5% of the prize money or one stud nomination a year.

Ferguson sued and, with his name on the ownership documents, probably would have won had it gone to trial. But then rumors started to spread about some of Ferguson’s financial dealings at United. Paid actors at United’s annual general meeting raised awkward points, then Magnier and McManus sent a list of 99 questions to the United board, which mysteriously found their way into the Daily Mail. United were highly embarrassed. Fans began to demonstrate against Magnier and McManus at race meetings. A settlement was reached, with Ferguson paid £2.5m to drop the action. But the damage was done.

Magnier and McManus had decided to sell their shares in United, and another shareholder was ready and waiting: Malcolm Glazer. Ferguson backed Glazer, who launched his leveraged buyout. Magnier and McManus sold up in 2005 for £260m, a profit of a little under £100m. Had they waited for Ratcliffe, who bought a similar stake in 2024, they would have received roughly £1bn more than that. For Ferguson, a threat had been dealt with.

The problem was that Glazer and his family would prove some of the worst club owners in English history. For 20 years, United have been addled by debt and have made consistently terrible footballing decisions. Ferguson’s team was good enough, and his personality big enough, that United won five league titles and a Champions League after the takeover, but once his genius had gone, there was nothing left.

A mismatched squad built up over seven flawed managerial appointments and a multiplicity of conflicting approaches will not readily be sorted out. Carrick is the latest victim of a crisis 21 years in the making. For the want of a horse a club was lost.

Sports.title: Davide Ancelotti wants to make a name for himself – will he do it at Lille?
Sports.content:
In a restaurant in Rio de Janeiro, two aspiring young managers sit around a table. Their respective clubs, Flamengo and Botafogo, are fierce rivals on the pitch. The relationship between the managers of the two clubs, Filipe Luís and Davide Ancelotti, however, is significantly more cordial.

Speaking before his first meeting with Ancelotti in Ligue 1 on Sunday, the Monaco manager, Filipe Luís, described his counterpart at Lille as a “really formidable person”. The Brazilian added: “It is something special for us. It will be a pleasure to face my friend.”

There were 12 managerial appointments in Ligue 1 over the summer; Filipe Luís and Ancelotti were two of the most interesting. Filipe Luís won the Premier League with Chelsea but is probably best known in Europe for his eight years at Atlético Madrid, where he won La Liga, the Copa del Rey and two Europa League titles across two spells. He carried on that success in his first job as a manager, winning the Copa Libertadores with Flamengo. “He knows what he’s talking about and how to motivate us,” says the Monaco forward Matthis Abline. “It motivates us even more to have a manager like him behind us.”

Davide Ancelotti has had a different route into management. When your surname is Ancelotti, you can’t exactly make a name for yourself; his father, Carlo, has already seen to that. “I hope to be able to write my story, with my first name, too,” said Davide before Lille played in the Champions League earlier this season. No manager has won more titles (five) or as many games (218) in the competition as his father.

Bar a brief 33-game stint as manager at Botafogo, Davide has spent the last 14 years following his father from club to club and then ultimately to the Brazil national team. From the banks of the river Mersey, to Bavaria, the fervour of the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, the grandeur of the Bernabéu and the vibrancy of the Maracanã. His trip around the world was enriching but he was always in the shadows. Until now.

View image in fullscreen The former Brazil defender Filipe Luís was appointed Monaco manager in the summer. Photograph: Manon Cruz/Reuters

Ancelotti’s appointment over the summer marked a radical departure at Lille. There was a common thread linking the club’s appointments of Christophe Galtier, Jocelyn Gourvennec, Paulo Fonseca and Bruno Génésio: they were all “a safe pair of hands” and most had considerable experience in Ligue 1. Génésio left Lille in the summer after his contract expired even though he had met the club’s key objective of qualifying for this season’s Champions League. The club’s president, Olivier Létang, simply said it “was the right moment” for a parting of the ways.

Unlike the wider public, Létang was at least familiar with Davide Ancelotti thanks to their time together at Paris Saint-Germain in 2012. Carlo Ancelotti was manager at the time, Létang was the director of football and Davide was the fitness coach. Létang did, nonetheless, use Carlo as a middleman when making his approach for Davide this summer. Carlo has even observed Lille’s start to the season from the stands, attending a draw with PSG in August.

Quick Guide Ligue 1 results Show Monaco 1-1 Lille Angers 0-0 Lorient Auxerre 1-1 Le Mans Marseille 4-3 Le Havre Rennes 3-0 Strasbourg Toulouse 0-0 Troyes Brest 1-2 Nice Lens 2-1 Paris Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Lille have lost all three of their matches in the Champions League this season and sit second from bottom in the 36-team table but, after their 1-1 draw at Monaco on Sunday, they were just one point behind the Ligue 1 leaders, Rennes. The point earned at the Stade Louis II took Lille’s tally to 15 points from eight games; they have not started a domestic campaign this well since they won the title in 2020-21.

Comparisons to his father are unfair but they are inevitable; the expectations on Davide have been moulded by two decades of his father’s unprecedented success. And it will always be extremely hard, borderline impossible, to live up to them. Every game is seen as proof of hereditary genius or – as had sometimes been the case in the opening weeks – its absence.

View image in fullscreen Ethan Mbappé gives Lille the lead at the Stade Louis II on Sunday. Photograph: Philippe Magoni/AP

The game on Sunday did not offer much evidence of genius. Ethan Mbappé gave Lille the lead from the only clear chance of the first half. Thereafter, they retreated inside their shell. Even before Tanguy Nianzou was sent off for a reckless challenge on Paris Brunner, Monaco had them under the cosh. Ancelotti’s decision to take off a striker in the form of Soriba Diaoune for a defender in Isaac Cossier reflected the manager’s infectious fear.

Lille could not hold on for the win and, in the end, they nearly lost the game. Monaco equalised through Edan Diop with 15 minutes to play and had numerous efforts during a late siege. One side dominated, but the points were shared. In the absence of any clear identity, Ancelotti praised his side’s “solidarity”. For signs of who Davide is beyond the son of the most prolific manager in Europe, the wait goes on. He is out of his father’s shadow but not yet truly in the light.

Talking points

There was no “headline” fixture in France on Sunday night. The game between Paris Saint-Germain and Lyon was postponed until Monday. As was the case last year, it means that many of PSG’s nine Ballon d’Or nominees will miss the ceremony in London. Their absence last year was the result of a storm, which led to their game in Marseille being delayed by 24 hours.

Unlike in the provincial cities, the planned protest in Paris on Saturday was not banned. With a significant police presence in the capital in an attempt to prevent a recurrence of last week’s riots and looting, and an NFL game to host on Sunday afternoon, the prefecture issued the directive, later adopted by the French league, on Friday.

There was further disruption. Elsewhere in Ligue 1, Toulouse’s home game against Troyes was moved from Saturday to Sunday. In Ligue 2, Montpellier’s game against Red Star was moved from Saturday to Monday. There wasn’t the same degree of disruption in Saint-Étienne, who nonetheless delayed the kick-off of their game against Nantes by 45 minutes following a police directive.

Another year, another call for bids for Ligue 1’s broadcasting rights, the value of which has plummeted in recent seasons. Dazn pulled out after just one season in 2024, giving rise to the Ligue 1+ experiment. The league-owned broadcaster, now in its second season, has been an editorial success but not a financial one. As a result, the president of the French league, Vincent Labrune, has announced a fresh auction for Ligue 1’s broadcasting rights, which will begin next month and end in December.

The prospective deal would begin at the start of next season. Labrune spoke of a “new context” and one more conducive to bigger offers. Recent changes in legislation mean that the rights can be sold in a single “bundle”, offering the option of exclusivity to any prospective buyer. Without citing any broadcasters, Labrune also revealed “registered concrete interests from different actors”. Ligue 1 cannot afford another botched deal.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
Sports.content:
Will derby win kick-start Arsenal’s season?

The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack

Match report: Tottenham 1-2 Arsenal

Godfrey a star in the making

View image in fullscreen Freya Godfrey of London City Lionesses Photograph: Clare Overfield/SPP/Shutterstock

Is Freya Godfrey England’s future? That’s what Alexia Putellas thinks of her London City Lionesses teammate, and the Spain icon heaped praise on the 21-year-old winger after she scored in her second consecutive WSL game. Godfrey – who made her senior England debut earlier this month against Greece – capitalised on a Khiara Keating mistake to score in the 2-2 draw with Liverpool on Sunday and her all-round display delighted Putellas, who told Sky Sports: “She can arrive where she really wants. I always tell her, she’s a star girl. She will be the future of this club. She has to keep working like she is doing now. She will be the future of England as well as the present.” TG

United show progress under Olid

Manchester United’s display in Sunday’s derby draw was night and day compared to their most recent previous home league fixture against a title challenger, when they were torn apart in a 5-0 defeat at home against Chelsea just six weeks ago. Against Manchester City on Sunday they competed toe-to-toe with the defending champions, and while it would be wrong to suggest that Eva Olid’s team are anywhere near the finished article, their improvements are striking, both with and without the ball. Olid feels that heavy defeat early in her tenure actually helped her side. “It was a hard week after Chelsea but sometimes you need a difficult moment to happen, to react and see exactly where the problems [were] or the things we had to solve as a team,” she said. “It had to happen to now be the team we are.” Tom Garry

Match report: Manchester United 1-1 Manchester City

Birmingham earn first win of WSL return

Birmingham’s first win of the WSL season came in the first encounter between league newcomers this season. Following an impressive point at the Emirates the week before,the 1-0 win over Charlton marked another key step as Amy Merricks’ side continue to settle into the top flight. The Blues were almost made to pay for their profligacy in front of goal against a familiar foe from last season in WSL2. They dominated proceedings and created 20 chances in total but registered just five on target. Océane Hurtré and Lisa Naalsund rattled the crossbar while Lily Crosthwaite missed three gilt-edged opportunities before Wilma Leidhammar struck a 68th minute-winner. “That was the most important thing today,” Merricks said. “We needed to pick up three points and we delivered that. I don’t think the performance was our finest. You could feel the caginess across the pitch and that is something we need to work on. We are in a better place, and we keep pushing.” Sophie Downey

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Depth the difference as Chelsea produce comeback

View image in fullscreen Melvine Malard displayed her class as Chelsea despatched Crystal Palace. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

For 51 minutes on Sunday afternoon, it felt like it might just be one of those days for Chelsea. Despite dominating the first half – they created 12 opportunities to Crystal Palace’s four and registered 20 touches in the opposition box – they found themselves trailing and running out of ideas. A key difference between the two sides, however, is the strength in depth available to their respective managers. In bringing on Erin Cuthbert and Sandy Baltimore at half-time, Sonia Bompastor was able to call on the services of two experienced internationals. Cuthbert added a crucial bite to the midfield that had been lacking in the first half while Baltimore set up Melvine Malard to put the Blues in front before scoring from the spot to confirm the three points. In contrast, Jo Potter made just three substitutions with the first coming in the 77th minute. It is this ability to change things from the bench that truly illustrates the gap in class between the eight-time WSL champions and the league newcomers. SD

Sørensen makes statement against former club

Brian Sørensen and his Aston Villa side came away with a 3-2 win against Everton. Sørensen, who took over from Natalia Arroyo last month, faced the Merseyside club for the first time since his Goodison Park exit in February. Villa dominated the clash and went 3-0 up within 50 minutes thanks to goals from Noelle Maritz and Amalie Vangsgaard, but they were given a scare following a late comeback push with Holly McNamara and Noémie Mouchon both scoring. Villa saw the game out to take three points – just. Nevertheless, Sørensen will be thrilled with the outcome, especially as it moved his team up to eighth. It also marked the first time since the 2024-25 campaign that Villa have won back-to-back games. “I’m happy, it was overall a good performance,” the interim head coach said. “Of course, maybe they got a bit too excited at the end but I also think we had the opportunities to kill the game off a lot sooner. But three points is three points, that’s all that matters.” Emillia Hawkins

Symonds’ stunner inspires Brighton win

Maisie Symonds’ stunning strike set Brighton on course for a 3-0 victory over West Ham. The Brighton captain broke the deadlock in the 29th minute, meeting a headed clearance with a first-time strike from distance that swerved beyond West Ham goalkeeper Constance Picaud-Inconnu and kissed the post on its way in. It was her second goal of the season, rewarding Brighton’s early dominance. Fran Kirby doubled the lead in the 63rd minute before Kiko Seike struck three minutes later. Brighton’s head coach, Arturo Ruiz, called it his side’s “most complete” performance of the season, praising their confidence and tactical adaptability. Symonds said Brighton “got control” in the second half. It was the Seagulls’ first Women’s Super League clean sheet of the campaign. Mitul Samji

Sports.title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed a shot into the back of the net.

Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist.

What a difference it makes to this Napoli team when their Scottish star is fit and firing. McTominay was out of action for all of September, recovering from an ablation procedure to correct an irregular heartbeat – known medically as an arrhythmia. The condition was characterised by the club as mild and benign, and the medical intervention a complete success.

Napoli had struggled in McTominay’s absence. They continued to struggle right after his return, too. His first two starts back in the side came in defeats to Villarreal and Serie A’s last-placed team, Venezia – leaving the Partenopei with five losses from their first nine games in all competitions. The latter result prompted speculation about whether Massimiliano Allegri’s job as manager could soon be at risk.

A week later, McTominay is starting to change the narrative. His two goals in midweek helped Napoli to their first Champions League win of the season, 4-3 against Bodø/Glimt. On Saturday, he broke his Serie A duck and did everything in his power to deliver another win over undefeated Roma.

McTominay’s three-strikes-in-one had made it 2-0 in the 48th minute, building on Frank Anguissa’s glorious overhead opener. Perhaps McTominay’s willingness to attempt the audacious has been rubbing off on his Napoli teammates too, though the Cameroon international was a title-winner and essential figure before the Scot arrived in 2024.

View image in fullscreen Frank Anguissa succeeds in the spectacular to give Napoli the lead in the first half. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/LaPresse/AP

They could have been further ahead on Saturday. Mathías Olivera had a point-blank effort hacked off the line when the score was 1-0 before half-time. Then again, Bryan Cristante hit the post for Roma moments later.

McTominay’s goal appeared to put Napoli fully in control, until Matías Soulé swapped a one-two with Donyell Malen and picked out the bottom corner brilliantly from outside the box. That was the 69th minute, and Roma were level by the 74th, their centre-back Leonardo Balerdi crashing home from a corner.

And so McTominay answered again, with a wicked finish of his own from almost 30 yards. He matched Soulé’s precision after Roma had failed to clear their lines from a Leonardo Spinazzola attempt, tucking his shot inside the near post.

Against lesser opponents, that might have been the end of it. But Roma are not easily beaten under Gian Piero Gasperini. In the 89th minute, Wesley crossed and Balerdi arrived to head home another equaliser.

It finished 3-3, a marvellously entertaining game, with so many stories to tell. On the Roma side, this felt like a big night for Soulé, the 23-year-old Argentina forward delivering one of the statement performances of his Serie A career to date in a stadium named after Diego Maradona.

Signed from Frosinone in the summer of 2024, Soulé has shown glimpses of immense potential but struggled for consistency, leading to questions about whether he can truly become more than Paulo Dybala’s understudy. But this season, and in the last month especially – which began with a first senior appearance for Argentina, then two assists in a heart-breaking Champions League defeat to Real Madrid – he is stepping ever more confidently from his compatriot’s shadow.

“He’s in his prime, he’s the driving force of this team,” said Gasperini at full-time. “[Donyell] Malen didn’t have a great game, and [Soulé] carried the team. His goal was something crazy; the foot and leg speed reminds you of something [Leo] Messi would do.”

View image in fullscreen Matías Soulé’s goal reminded his manager of ‘something Messi would do’. Photograph: Alessandro Garofalo/LaPresse/AP

And then there is Balerdi, also Argentinian, on loan from Marseille with an option to buy. Gasperini noted how one of Roma’s strategies in the transfer market had been to target players perceived as leaders for their previous clubs. He named Marten de Roon in this category, too, and it was the Dutchman, wearing the captain’s armband, who put in the cross that led to Balerdi’s first goal.

Unsurprisingly, given how the match unfolded, Gasperini seemed content with the draw. Allegri rather less so. He was sent off after Roma’s third goal and though he claimed not to know why, he was later overheard outside the changing rooms insinuating that the opposition had received favourable treatment from the referee. La Gazzetta dello Sport reported him protesting that: “Last year they handed you [Roma] the Champions League and I paid for it at Milan.”

Without relitigating a year worth of decisions, this was a bold line to take. Milan, who spent almost the entire campaign in the top four and much of it as the closest contender to Inter for the scudetto, contrived to miss out on the Champions League by a single point after collecting only seven from their final eight games.

Allegri cut short an interview on Dazn, saying that he was “for the first time in 25 years, not lucid enough to expand on this game”. Another claim that might raise a few eyebrows, from a man who once got halfway to undressing in frustration at the officiating of a final that his own team won.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Torino 3-2 Monza, Cagliari 0-2 Bologna, Como 2-0 Sassuolo, Napoli 3-3 Roma, Lazio 2-1 Parma, Inter 2-1 Fiorentina, Atalanta 4-4 Frosinone, Genoa 1-0 Venezia, Lecce 0-2 Juventus, Udinese 0-2 Milan Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Perhaps his ire on this occasion would have been better directed at one of his own defenders. During the buildup to Roma’s final goal, Sam Beukema collapsed to the floor after tussling with Balerdi off the ball. A generous reading of the replays would be to say that he “made the most” of some contact, which appeared to be arm-on-arm, though the Napoli player went down clutching his rib cage.

If Beukema had stayed on his feet and continued marking Balerdi, perhaps the equaliser could have been avoided. Instead, he got up too late to do anything about it and then fell back to the floor again after watching the goal go in.

An undignified end to a brilliant game. As frustrated as Napoli might feel at throwing these points away, there were lots of positives here to hang on to. Only a week ago we were asking whether Kevin De Bruyne could be persuaded to occupy the deeper role Allegri sees for him and make space for McTominay further forward. In this game, and the win over Bodø/Glimt, there were positive signs.

Putting three goals past this Roma team – who had only conceded that many in the previous seven games of this Serie A season combined – is no mean feat. Napoli with McTominay are more than capable of improving on their current 10th place in the table and at least competing for a top-four spot.

The challenge is to stay lucid, as McTominay did on his triple goal, sticking at a task until it is completed. And perhaps a little longer to make sure.

Sports.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
Sports.content:
At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby.

Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher.

However, Eva Olid’s ever-improving hosts fought back and were good value for the draw, which they eventually earned when Terland found the bottom corner after the ball fell kindly to her in the penalty area.

Olid, in fact, repeatedly said in her post-match press conference that her side had “deserved to win”.

United climbed to fourth in the table, while that late strike meant City dropped to ­second – now behind Chelsea on goal difference – and breathed fresh life and intrigue into the title race. Perhaps more strikingly, if any United fans who saw their men’s team being humbled by Bournemouth earlier on Sunday managed to navigate the winds of Storm Boelo and get to Leigh for this 6pm kick-off, they will have seen a team with characteristics unrecognisable from those wearing red at Old Trafford; hard work, resilience, teamwork, running – real, hard running – and fighting spirit.

This United team markedly improved on last season’s league meetings with their local rivals, both of which ended in 3-0 victories for City. This time Andrée Jeglertz’s visitors were given a real test.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: Show Chelsea came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 3-1 after Molly Bartrip’s shock opener. It was the first time Chelsea had trailed all season and they struck back in the second half with two Melvine Malard goals, before Sandy Baltimore converted from the penalty spot in the 90th minute. London City Lionesses stayed third after drawing 2-2 at Liverpool, with the visitors denied all three points by a stoppage-time own goal from Jana Fernández. Freya Godfrey and Kadidiatou Diani had earlier wiped out Beata Olsson’s penalty. Aston Villa moved level on points with Everton after winning 3-2 at Goodison Park. Amalie Vangsgaard’s double put Villa three up after Noelle Maritz’s early goal, before the hosts made it a nervy finish with two late goals. Birmingham won for the first time this season as Wilma Leidhammar’s effort midway through the second half saw off Charlton 1-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

For spells of the first half, City’s fluid pass-and-move football, their speed down the left-wing with ­Lauren Hemp, and the technical prowess of Yui Hasegawa and Aoba Fujino in particular, made it feel as though there was only one likely outcome, as Fujino fizzed an effort narrowly wide of the United goal.

United, though, proved a tough nut to crack and, against the run of play, created the better chances of the opening 45 minutes.

Terland was unable to reset her feet and ­connect properly with Andrea Medina’s ­cutback. Later Ella Toone and Jess Park both had efforts saved by Ayaka Yamashita.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw blasts Manchester City into the lead against United. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

Park’s powerful, driven shot clipped the top of the crossbar around the hour mark, after Yamashita had saved well from Terland one-on-one.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Not long later, though, last season’s WSL Golden Boot winner Shaw ­delivered the breakthrough with a ruthless, low strike that was hit with too much venom for Phallon ­Tullis-Joyce to react. Shaw, who had been booed by the home fans after exchanging robust challenges with Maya Le Tissier in the first half, ran across to celebrate in front of the City fans, many of whom were waving inflatable bananas in the air. She almost had a second goal moments later but whipped a close-range, rising shot just over the bar.

Shaw glanced a header wide from a City corner and Grace Clinton missed a huge chance to seal it for the ­visitors. Continuing to battle, United were eventually rewarded when Le Tissier’s hopeful, high ball into the box, after a free-kick was taken short, was met by a defensive header from Shaw, but that only dropped as far as Terland who lashed in first time to draw huge roars and clenched fists from the United technical area.

Jeglertz is staying calm, insisting: “Nothing has changed. We are absolutely on the right track, in everything we are doing. We are playing well in most of the games and getting the result in most of the games. But this league is challenging. [We are just going] to stay calm and focusing on the next task.”

As for United, this late goal felt like a pivotal moment for Olid, giving the club a lift. Her tenure began with chastening losses to London City and Chelsea but this rally against their neighbours showed they are rapidly improving. She said: “That was one of our best performances, in general, in terms of fight, hard work, how we were ­pressing and how we played with the ball.

“How this team has built in confidence from day one to now, in a short period of time – just two months and a half working together – the progression has been massive.”

Sports.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.”

Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said.

“My way, my idea, is that the best way to defend is to have the ball.” The problem with that is that only the three promoted sides have had less possession than Palace. “Here every mistake, every situation that is bad for the team will be a goal,” Sage said.

Palace conceded two goals against Besiktas on Thursday to the only shots on target they conceded. Newcastle similarly scored with both their shots on target. “We conceded fewer chances with our defending in open play today but it’s not enough,” the Palace manager said. “For the moment the pressure is always the same because I don’t find the solution. Today was not a tactical problem but a mental problem. When we came back from the dressing room we let our opponents have too many things. When you don’t control the ball you give the initiative to the opposition.”

Sage is sure he can improve ­Palace’s fortunes – they are 17th having lost back-to-back Premier League games, the other being a 5-0 thrashing by their rivals Brighton – and said that although he remains in regular contact with the Palace chair, Steve Parish, the issue of his future has never been raised. “Inside, we are just really focused on solutions,” Sage said. “How to be better, how to create the conditions to compete, and we will continue our work. There’s no noise inside, if you want.”

There was relief for Matthias Jaissle as he oversaw a first ­Newcastle win in three games. “It was a tough game especially in first half,” the ­German said. “We couldn’t get ourselves the reward for the intensity of our possession.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The first half out of possession was not that bad but we didn’t have our attacking mindset. The second half was much better. Even if you don’t play a fantastic game in possession, keeping a clean sheet is the fundamental of football.”

Sports.title: Nicolas Jackson is one of top three strikers in Premier League – he starts for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Nicolas Jackson is one of top three strikers in Premier League – he starts for Arsenal

Is Nicolas Jackson a top three striker in the Premier League?

talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor thinks so, with the Aston Villa frontman scoring four in his last four league games.

3 Jackson has instantly hit form for Aston Villa, scoring seven goals in his first 11 appearances since joining from Chelsea Credit: Getty

Jackson, who signed for Villa from Chelsea for a club record £65million in the summer, has hit the ground running.

In 11 appearances in all competitions for his new side, he has already scored seven goals, with four strikes coming in the top flight.

His double against Manchester City on Saturday showcased just how good he can be - and after that game, Agbonlahor made a bold claim.

He asked on talkSPORT's GameDay Phone-In: "Nicolas Jackson - give me three better centre forwards in the Premier League?"

Agbonlahor firmly put him in among the best and disregarded any inclusion of Brentford's Igor Thiago in the conversation.

The ex-striker also stated that Jackson would start for Arsenal, putting him in their side over Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz.

Is Jackson one of the best three strikers in the Premier League?

After those comments, talkSPORT Breakfast host Jeff Stelling agreed with statement, saying: "I think he [Agbonlahor] is right on current form.

"Erling Haaland and Alexander Isak yeah, but who else can you argue? It's very hard to argue the case for anybody else."

Co-host Ally McCoist then added: "He [Jackson] has got a lot more composure than he's had. He can still be doing with a little more calmness in front of goal.

"But there are not a lot of strikers that are top class that really enjoying playing the role themselves and he's perfect for it, he's been terrific. Gabby's right!"

3 Agbonlahor, Stelling and McCoist all agree that Jackson is one of the best three strikers in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Jackson has found 'a natural home'

Jackson's career in England appeared to be in doubt after struggling at Chelsea and being sent out on loan last season.

He spent last term as Harry Kane's understudy at Bayern Munich, scoring 11 goals in 34 appearances in all competitions.

The Senegal international was then sold to Villa on his return to the Premier League and he is now in impressive form.

Arsenal legend Martin Keown believes Jackson lost his way at Chelsea and that now, working under Unai Emery for the second time after his spell at Villarreal, he has found a 'natural home'.

Keown said: "He worked with him [Emery] before and I think this Villa team is now unrecognisable now from the start of the season.

"Jackson, for me, is a nightmare to play against. He's robust, dynamic and he punishes you with pace.

3 Back working under Emery, Jackson appears to be finding his best form Credit: Getty

"I think the Villa faithful are delighted he's now playing for them and maybe this is a natural home for him.

"I thought he was losing his discipline at Chelsea a little bit... he was getting sent off, getting involved in silly things, he wasn't loved.

"But he has the full love now of the manager and the club and I think it's the perfect place for him."

Sports.title: Burnley interviewing ex-Premier League manager after firing Nicky Hayen
Sports.content:
Rob Edwards is in talks with Burnley over their vacant manager's position, talkSPORT understands.

The former Wolves boss was interviewed by the Clarets on Monday having previously turned down an approach from then in the summer.



3 Edwards was interviewed by Burnley on Monday Credit: Getty

It follows the sacking of Nicky Hayen after Saturday's 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City.

The result leaves Burnley 22nd in the Championship and three points from safety.

Hayen won just one of his 12 league matches in charge after succeeding Scott Parker in July.



Burnley's manager search

He could now be replaced by Edwards, who previously won promotion to the Premier League with Luton Town.

The 43-year-old is without a club as he was sacked by Wolves in June following seven months in charge.



Edwards failed to avoid relegation from the top-flight during his short tenure at Molineux.

Meanwhile, he has won 32 out of 78 Championship matches across his managerial career with Wolves, Watford, Luton and Middlesbrough.



Former West Brom boss Carlos Corberan had previously emerged as a contender to replace Hayen.

The Spaniard has attracted interest from Burnley having left Valencia last month.

Corberan is appreciated by the Clarets' new chief football officer Diego Lopez.

3 Edwards previously turned down the Burnley job in the summer after leaving Wolves Credit: Getty



Burnley on brink of unwanted history

If appointed, Edwards' first match in charge of Burnley could be at home to Portsmouth on Saturday.

The fixture will see the Clarets aiming to avoid setting an unwanted record.

They have not won a home league fixture since beating Leeds United in the Premier League on October 18, 2025.

Pompey's visit to Turf Moor will come 377 days on from that victory, with a draw or defeat for Burnley seeing them set a new record for the longest home winless run in England's top four divisions.



The club's new manager will also be tasked with avoiding relegation to League One this season.

Burnley have not played outside the top two tiers since the 1999/2000 campaign.

3 Burnley have gone over a year without winning a home league match Credit: Getty

The Clarets have since won promotion to the Premier League five times, with their lowest finish in that period being 19th in the second tier 22 years ago.

Sports.title: Ex-England striker explains why Harry Kane should not win Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Ex-England striker explains why Harry Kane should not win Ballon d’Or

Harry Kane should not win the Ballon d'Or this evening - he doesn't do anything that makes you go 'Wow'.

That's the opinion of former England striker Dean Ashton, who thinks Lamine Yamal deserves to win the award instead.

4 Ashton thinks Kane does not have enough of a wow factor to win the Ballon d'Or despite his incredible scoring stats Credit: Getty

Kane is the favourite to become the first English Ballon d'Or winner since Michael Owen lifted the trophy 25 years ago.

He scored a phenomenal 73 goals in the 2025/26 season, breaking records on a weekly basis for Bayern Munich.

For his club and on the international stage, the 33-year-old has become known for incredible finishing and playmaking abilities.

However, Ashton doesn't think Kane's game and style of play is enough to make him a Ballon d'Or winner.

Why Kane should not win the Ballon d'Or

The one-cap ex-England striker explained why he believes the Three Lions captain should be beaten to the award by Yamal.

Ashton said on talkSPORT: "Look, obviously as a fellow Englishman, to see Harry Kane win it would be incredibly special.

"I think he's the best all-round candidate, the best all-round centre forward, his numbers are staggering.

"But he's not a Ballon d'Or winner in my opinion."

Asked to explain why, he added: "Everyone can have their own opinion on what a Ballon d'Or winner should be. Whether it's achievements, winning the World Cup with their country, whatever criteria.

"But for me, the Ballon d'Or winner should be someone that does things that pretty much no one else can do, that even fellow professionals gasp at what they can do.

4 Kane scored 73 goals in the 2025/26 campaign, but he shouldn't win the Ballon d'Or over Yamal, according to Ashton Credit: Getty

4 Yamal, who won the World Cup with Spain this summer, has fans and players gasping at his talent, unlike Kane Credit: Getty

"Harry Kane is a fantastic player and does some wonderful things, but I look at him and think, there's nothing he does that I think wow, I couldn't do that or other players couldn't.

"I watch Yamal and I'm honestly wowed by some of the things.

"Kane doesn't do anything that has me aghast."

Keown defends Kane in Ballon d'Or debate

After hearing Ashton's take on Kane's Ballon d'Or chances, Arsenal legend Martin Keown jumped to the striker's defence.

He thinks that the England captain does deserve to win the award, highlighting just how impressive his goal scoring is.

"Harry is eye-catching too," Keown said. "Some of the stuff that he's playing now, his finishing...

4 Keown disagreed with Ashton's take and believes that Kane deserves to win the Ballon d'Or this evening Credit: Getty

"And going to a foreign country, 102 goals in 101 (Bundesliga) appearances for Bayern, nine consecutive goals in the Champions League.

"He does not stop scoring and he's so significant as an Englishman abroad to do that.

"I honestly feel now that he deserves it.

"I 100 per cent think he should win it...I can't see a more worthy winner of it this year."

The Ballon d'Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium Theatre tonight, beginning at 8pm.

Sports.title: Premier League star tipped as future England player to solve problem area for Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Bournemouth star James Hill has been backed to be a future England player following his impressive start to the season.

The 24-year-old joined the Cherries in the Championship in 2022 but has had to wait patiently to cement his place in the starting XI.

4 Hill has started all eight Premier League games for Bournemouth this season Credit: Getty

The south coast outfit have undergone significant changes to their backline in recent seasons after selling a number of top stars.

The rise of James Hill at Bournemouth

Dean Huijsen, Illia Zabarnyi, and Milos Kerkez were all sold after the 2024/25 season, in which Hill only made six Premier League starts.

However, Bournemouth's No.5 broke into the team under then-boss Andoni Iraola at the start of the year and hasn't looked back.

The England Under-21 international has taken on increased importance since Marco Rose was appointed at the helm, following the summer exit of Marcos Senesi to Tottenham.

Hill has already clocked over 1,000 minutes of game time across three competitions for Bournemouth this term, with 11 starts in total.

The ex-Fleetwood Town player played at right-back for the 3-0 win over AC Milan on Thursday, before moving centrally to help his side beat Manchester United by the same scoreline three days later.

Future England star?

Bournemouth fan Sean messaged talkSPORT Breakfast hosts Jeff Stelling and Ally McCoist on Monday to give a special mention to Hill.

It read: "He sat back and watched Huijsen, Zabarnyi and Senesi all leave. But he's come in and been sensational. Could be an England player in the next few years."

4 Hill (right) kept clean sheets against Milan and Man United in the same week Credit: Getty

Breakfast presenter Stelling replied: "And you know what, Sean? Completely agree.

"And not just this week. Whenever I've seen James Hill, he has been exceptional."

McCoist continued: "It's certainly one of the secrets of it, Jeff. Recruitment. The recruitment.

"I've written down the names of three clubs. Brentford, Brighton and Bournemouth. Brilliant. Absolutely brilliant.

"If you'd ask those clubs 15, 20 years ago where they'd be, again, I mean, they would just have dreamt of being where they are.

"They are fantastically run clubs; [they] know what they're all about. Everybody knows their job."

4 Hill, who came off the bench in the 4-4 draw last season, played the full 90 minutes on Sunday Credit: Getty

That sentiment is underlined by Hill, who has been instrumental in stringing together a four-match win streak across the Premier League and in Europe – Bournemouth's best run since December 2023.

And the man himself believes things are starting to click, telling the club's website after their 3-0 victory over United: "It was a really special performance. Coming here and getting three points is hard for any team.

"But for us to come here and keep a clean sheet as well and score the three goals, credit to the whole team, they were brilliant.

"They [United] are in a difficult position, but we didn't focus on that, we focused on putting a good performance in. We focused on ourselves coming into a massive fixture against a team with a lot of quality.

"We've been really good recently and we're pleased with our clean sheets recently. We were outstanding to a man.

"We have had lots of games recently, but we wouldn't want it any other way, it's been an incredible journey.

"It was an incredible performance from everybody and a good confidence builder for the team. I am absolutely delighted.

"We were unlucky at the start of the season, but things are starting to click under Marco and we have momentum now. It was only a matter of time."

4 Hill's partnership with Senesi in the second half of last season helped Bournemouth record an epic unbeaten run under Iraola Credit: Getty

Hill's sole England U21 cap came in a 5–0 victory away to Kosovo in 2022 alongside players who have made the step up to Thomas Tuchel's senior squad, including James Trafford and Anthony Gordon.

His form, however, is now coinciding with a downturn in performance for fellow English centre-backs, including Marc Guehi.

The Manchester City man, who made a howler in a 3-2 defeat to Spain last month, was named among talkSPORT's Premier League Villains.

Sports.title: ‘Distasteful’ to revel in Michael Carrick’s downfall – he may never manage again after chastening Man United tenure
Sports.content:
‘Distasteful’ to revel in Michael Carrick’s downfall – he may never manage again after chastening Man United tenure

Michael Carrick has been praised for handling his Man United tenure with dignity - those waiting to have a pop are unfair.

talkSPORT understands Carrick is expected to be sacked with the Red Devils 16th in the Premier League.



3 Carrick received incredible support from the Man United fans on Sunday Credit: Getty

In midweek, Man United were crushed 4-1 by Como in the Champions League before being thrashed 3-0 at home to Bournemouth.

Carrick looked emotional at the end of the game as he completed a lap of honour of the Old Trafford pitch.

The home fans clapped and applauded their former player before very loudly booing the players, and after an underwhelming transfer window.



Carrick will no doubt be scarred by the whole experience at Man United and fears have been raised he might never manage again.

Speaking with Sam Matterface and Troy Deeney on the Premier League All Access Podcast, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said: "Is it the Glazers' fault? Yes. Ultimately, all of this is the Glazers' fault, and I don't deviate from that nor do Manchester United fans.



"The matchgoing supporters made their feelings particularly clear towards the hierarchy, and I am not saying Michael Carrick is perfect either.

"I do think it is a little bit distasteful the number of people that are almost revelling in Carrick's downfall.



"This is someone who has handled himself with tremendous dignity.

"The number of people queuing up to have a pop at Michael Carrick I think is unfair.

"I am not sure we'll see him in the dugout again, I don't know if he was desperate to go back into management after Middlesbrough.

"I think he felt a sense of duty to Manchester United. I think he knew he was on a hiding to nothing, certainly long term."

3 Man United have won one Premier League game all season Credit: Getty



Carrick's situation

The Man United legend was appointed as interim manager until the end of the season after Ruben Amorim's departure.

He was in charge for 17 games and won 12 of those losing just two.

The victories saw his Man United side beat Manchester City, Chelsea and Liverpool.

It meant it was impossible for him not to get the job, and he signed a two-year deal.

But in the summer, only three first-team players arrived with defence not significantly strengthened.



Performances and results have been poor since, and after the game, Carrick apologised, but he also vowed to fight on.

He said: "I had really mixed emotions, I'm feeling it for the players, for my group of players, I'm really feeling it for them because they're going through a tough spell.

"Some of it we can help ourselves, some of it the situation unravels. The boys are feeling at the moment.

"Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way, and to have that connection with the supporters in the moment that we're in, is really mixed emotions.



"A little bit of time to digest that, really, but I certainly appreciate their support.

"But the situation is where we're at, we haven't had results and we haven't had performances that have been good enough."

3 Carrick made 464 appearances for Man United in a stellar career at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

But he knows his future is out of his hands.

"I take the responsibility, of course.

"I accept the responsibility. I respect the position I am in. The responsibility is mine. What else can I say right now?



"I totally understand the situation. I am not expecting anything in particular, to be honest.

"I am carrying on as normal. I love this place. I always do what I feel is best for this football club. Whatever decision is made on anything really, that's kind of it. I am not expecting anything."

Problems run deeper

Even if Carrick goes, Crook doesn't believe that a replacement would arrive quickly due to the number of issues at the club.

To him, all of the candidates would have demands that need to be met.

But with the Glazers and INEOS in place, Crook feels the appeal of Man United isn't what it once was.



"So, whoever comes in will have the same pitfalls, and that is why I am not sure it is a case of Carrick being sacked and Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann or Antonio Conte walk through the door.

"In all three cases, they will have certain demands because none of them need the job.

"Manchester United isn't necessarily the draw it once was, and I think the board are a mess.

"You've got certain people pushing for Nagelsmann, others pushing for Howe and all running a mile from Conte."
