Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes appears to make cryptic dig at Michael Carrick after Man United benching
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes appears to make cryptic dig at Michael Carrick after Man United benching

Bruno Fernandes has seemingly fired another subtle dig towards Manchester United manager Michael Carrick.

Last week, the United skipper hit out at the club's tactics following the 4-1 defeat away at Como in the Champions League.

3 Fernandes has liked a social media post that appears to be a cryptic dig at manager Carrick after he was dropped to the bench Credit: Getty

He was then subsequently dropped to the bench by Carrick for Sunday's miserable 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth.

The Red Devils went on to confirm that his decision to drop Fernandes was based on 'pure football' reasons.

But Fernandes appears to not have taken the decision well.

Fernandes' cryptic dig at Carrick

Fernandes has liked a social media video which could be interpreted as a dig at Carrick for his treatment of him.

The Instagram reel shows a giant preventing a boulder from crashing into some buildings in a town before the giant eventually lets it go after the townspeople turned on him.

The caption read: "Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care."

Fernandes is appearing to view himself as the giant, who has been helping prevent Man United - the town - from being destroyed.

The 33-year-old captain broke the Premier League's assist record last season, having a hand in 30 goals altogether and leading the club to a place in the Champions League.

He has also been the Red Devils' standout player for multiple seasons despite things not going too swimmingly off the pitch.

But he may feel that his treatment from the club, e.g. being dropped to the bench by Carrick, has led to him losing his care, so he is now seemingly saying if he isn't respected, he'll let the club get what's coming to it.

3 The Man United captain is clearly not happy with the decision to drop him against Bournemouth on Sunday Credit: Getty

What is the latest on Carrick's future?

Fernandes' dig comes with Carrick on the brink of being sacked as Man United boss after a run of eight games without a win.

He is set to be dismissed, but the club are unable to break the news of a sacking until they have informed the New York Stock Exchange.

United have a day off on Monday, so Carrick did arrive at the training - but chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada did.

It appears the writing is on the wall and that in the coming days, Carrick will be gone, in news that will likely please Fernandes.

So who will replace the club legend in the dugout?

Eddie Howe is a leading contender for the role, while ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann is another in the running.

3 Fernandes liked the social media post with Carrick on the brink of being sacked as United boss Credit: Getty

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery, Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler and Antonio Conte are all also admired by United chiefs.

However, Hurzeler is understood to not want the job at this time.

Meanwhile, Conte would want the role, but he recently released a statement rejecting claims he is in talks with the club.

Sports.title: England Under 15s WALK OFF during World Cup clash with Ireland after youngster accused rival of calling him a 'monkey' in alleged racist slur
Sports.content:
England's Under-15 World Cup match against Ireland descended into chaos after an alleged racist incident in Azerbaijan.

Young Lions boss Matt Thorpe withdrew his players in the 40th minute after one of them claimed an opponent had called him a 'monkey' moments after the England youngster pushed his opponent in the back.

A member of the Irish backroom staff shouted 'no, he didn't' while the English player remonstrated, sparking a shouting match between the two benches.

The England player approached his bench and waited on the touchline as Thorpe spoke to the fourth official. And just before play could resume, the England coach ordered his team off the pitch.

England were trailing 4-1 at the time but it is unclear whether the incident will affect the result, given it played out in the final knockings of the game - consisting of two 20-minute halves.

England's Under 15s walked off midway through their World Cup clash with Ireland

The Young Lions claimed one of their players was labelled a 'monkey' by an opposing player

FIFA, the FA and the Irish FA were all contacted for comment.

A FIFA spokesman told Daily Mail Sport: 'FIFA is aware of an incident at the FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland. The match was abandoned by the referee following England's refusal to continue.

'The official reports are being gathered, and the matter will be referred to the independent Disciplinary Committee who will decide in due course.'

The Young Lions won their first three group games at the experimental eight-versus-eight tournament 16-1 on aggregate and topped the group before their match with Ireland, who were behind on goal difference.

England continued their campaign at 16:45, facing Zimbabwe in their final group match, and the affected player started for the Young Lions.

This was not the first England youth match disrupted by racism allegations. Last year, England's Under-17s had their friendly victory over Venezuela stopped twice after multiple players were accused of racial abuse.

FIFA have comprehensive rules for dealing with racist incidents. Players who cover their mouths during a confrontation can receive a straight red card.

The rule was introduced after Benfica's Gianluca Prestianni was accused of calling Vinicius Jr a monkey while covering his mouth during a Champions League match earlier this year. Prestianni was retrospectively handed a six-match ban for the incident.

Meanwhile, abusive and discriminatory language – if heard by the referee – results in a straight red card.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino was in attendance at the tournament on Monday

In July, the FA announced stricter measures to combat on-field discrimination in England, including a minimum 10-match ban for any player found guilty.

FIFA have a three-step procedure to address discriminatory incidents in stadiums, triggered when players make an X symbol to the referee.

Initially, the referee stops the match while spectators are warned to stop the abuse. It then escalates to a temporary pause before eventual abandonment if the conduct continues.

That protocol was notoriously implemented during England's 6-0 European Championship qualifying victory away to Bulgaria in 2019 when England's black players were tormented by monkey chants and Nazi salutes from the home support.

The game was stopped twice in the first half but the Three Lions opted to finish the game, having walked off the pitch just before half time.

Sports.title: Inside Harry Kane's business empire: Ballon d'Or favourite shares ticketing venture with John Terry, launched his own golfwear brand and has backed the football boffins - with the England captain now closing in on new Bayern Munich deal
Sports.content:
With the Ballon d'Or ceremony looming we may see the best chance of an English player lifting the trophy in over two decades.

Harry Kane, England's talisman and skipper, has gone from strength to strength since swapping north London for Bavaria, with the Bayern Munich star's dazzling display against Arsenal on Wednesday night cementing his status as one of the world's best.

Unsurprisingly, the Germans are hell-bent on building their future around the England captain, despite him closing in on his twilight years.

Daily Mail Sport understands the 33-year-old is on the verge of agreeing fresh terms with the Bundesliga champions, with his £400,000-per-week wage among the most lucrative deals in the game.

While Kane is delivering on the pitch, he is quietly building an impressive business portfolio away from it.

The former Spurs star has found great success in property dealings, commercial opportunities while he has also joined forces with fellow sports stars in new business ventures.

Property is the first area where the three-time Premier League Golden Boot winner has enjoyed steady success. Kane is listed as a director of Edward James Investments Limited, a real estate firm he runs alongside his parents and his brother, Charlie, who also serves as his agent.

Kane's super performance against Arsenal earned him Player of the Match but he is hoping to receive a bigger personal accolade on Monday

Charlie Kane (right) has been his brother's agent and managed his finances since the beginning of the striker's career

Charlie has been a vital force both on and off the pitch, managing Harry's transfers and lucrative contracts while smartly deploying his earnings. Thanks to Charlie's savvy strategy, the company has grown into a roaring success, boasting a UK property portfolio valued at £15million.

England's No 9 has also ventured into business outside the family circle - most notably with fellow former England captain and Chelsea legend, John Terry. While it may seem a surprising collaboration given their past rivalry, the pair have found common ground as investors in ticket and event management platform Seat Unique, which boasts a valuation exceeding £500m.

Yet this is only the tip of a multi-million-pound iceberg. The forward is also heavily involved in HK28 LTD, better known as The Harry Kane Company.

Far more diversified than his other ventures, HK28 combines Kane's passion for football and philanthropy with commercial profitability.

As the company's LinkedIn page explains: 'The Harry Kane Company exclusively manages the football, business, and charity interests of England Captain and Bayern Munich striker, Harry Kane. With specialisms across the sport, business, entertainment, and charity sectors, the team works purposefully with global brands, innovators, and charitable organisations to harness Harry's profile to inspire, educate, and empower others.'

This unique in-house model allows Kane and his team to bypass third-party agencies, keeping all operations and finances firmly under their own roof.

John Terry and Kane were once fierce rivals but have put their differences aside to make money together

Kane clearly envisioned his long-term financial growth early on. He and his family established the business back in October 2014, just weeks after the striker broke into Tottenham's first team at the age of 21.

In the years since, the firm has struck major deals with global brands, securing an eye-watering fortune.

Key commercial partnerships include household names such as Amazon, Cadbury and Topps, alongside sports and health brands like STATSports and Bio&Me. He has even teamed up with German oat brand 3Bears to tap into his local Bavarian fanbase.

However, all these deals pale in comparison to Kane's blockbuster boot deal. Shortly after joining Bayern, the striker made the bold move to step away from traditional giants Nike, adidas and Puma to sign a deal with Skechers.

While the move initially shocked the football world, the terms made total sense: Kane signed a lifetime partnership with Skechers, reportedly earning him an incredible £8million per year.

Kane's business empire shows no signs of slowing down - and with a new Bayern contract extension on the horizon, further growth is almost guaranteed.

Sports.title: Jeremy Clarkson in hot water after he aimed barb at Argentinian F1 driver - despite being a GUEST of his team at the US Grand Prix
Sports.content:
Jeremy Clarkson is in hot water again after making an offensive remark towards Formula One team Alpine's Argentinian driver Franco Colapinto.

Clarkson has a stormy history with Argentina after a controversial stunt in 2014 when his number plate appeared to reference the 1982 Falklands War.

He and his fellow Top Gear presenters had to flee the country after he drove a Porsche 928 with the number plate H982 FKL, which angry locals threw bricks at.

And the 66-year-old has again sparked controversy after joking that he would give Colapinto a grid penalty purely because of his nationality.

To make matters worse, Clarkson was a guest of Alpine for the Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, when he made the remark.

'Franco's got a grid penalty for being Argentinian... Probably. Well I'd give him one for that,' he said in an interview with Sky Sports' Martin Brundle.

Clarkson was invited onto the grid in Austin as a guest of Alpine but has since been criticised for insulting one of the team's own drivers

He then clarified: 'That's just because of what happened when we went there.'

Colapinto's manager Jamie Campbell-Walter said: 'Jeremy Clarkson’s comments about Franco’s nationality were completely unacceptable.

'There is no place for remarks like this in Formula One, regardless of who makes them or whether they are intended as a joke.'

Colapinto, whose career-best Grand Prix finish across his 45 races is sixth, had to deal with a 10-place grid penalty for Sunday's race at the Circuit of the Americas as a result of power unit component changes.

Clarkson's run-in over the Falklands is one of the most memorable scandals to have hit Top Gear. Rock-throwing protesters had vowed to 'barbecue' him after his stunt.

Veterans of the conflict laid siege to the hotel where Clarkson and fellow presenters Richard Hammond and James May were staying after news of the number plate appeared online.

Clarkson said at the time: 'I've been to Iraq and Afghanistan, but this was the most terrifying thing I've ever been involved in.'

Franco Colapinto has urged his Argentinian supporters to refrain for further abusing his team

Jeremy Clarkson, 66, has said he won't be sticking to his healthy diet after getting the all-clear from prostate cancer - because he 'hasn't worked his a**e off for 40 years to have no joy'

It comes after the Falklands War became a major flashpoint during the summer's World Cup, with Argentina's players claiming the archipelago belongs to them, not Britain, following their semi-final win over England.

Argentina's President Javier Milei has also amplified the messaging, saying in September that his nation 'needs to recover' the islands.

Clarkson is in remission from aggressive prostate cancer after being diagnosed in mid-June.

He said he was 'unwell for a short amount of time' after doctors 'found a little something' during his annual prostate check.

Jeremy told The Times it was 'not nice' to have to tell his children he had cancer but simply went into hospital for a procedure and was back in his tractor a fortnight later.

He is now feeling leaner after losing two stone down to weight-loss drug Mounjaro rather than 'steely will' and in series five, Jeremy's girlfriend Lisa Hogan advised him to adjust his diet and start eating healthier foods such as Greek yoghurt.

'Sure, I can eat less and more healthily. I can become a herbivore,' he said. 'And yes, I can go for 20-mile hikes and do 20,000 steps a day.

'But the truth is, there has to be some joy in life as well. And not drinking and not eating a pork chop means there is less joy in life. And I haven't worked my a**e off for 40 years to have no joy in my old age. So I'm having joy in my old age.'

Asked if he is going to stick to his new low-fat protein rich regime, Jeremy defiantly said: 'No,' while breaking out a NiQuitin lozenge.

Jeremy has two grandchildren through his daughter Emily and her husband Alex Andrew: Arlo, aged three, and Xanthe, 18 months.

Sports.title: Carrick's gamble on Bruno may prove his last act as Man United boss but his message is clear: the lunatics have run the asylum for far too long: KIERAN GILL on My Premier League Weekend
Sports.content:
Carrick's gamble on Bruno may prove his last act as Man United boss but his message is clear: the lunatics have run the asylum for far too long: KIERAN GILL on My Premier League Weekend

It carried shades of Ruud Gullit dropping Alan Shearer for Newcastle United against Sunderland in August 1999. Newcastle led 1-0 at half-time. Then Shearer was introduced at 1-1. Then Sunderland won 2-1. Gullit departed the club after that Tyne–Wear derby defeat at St James’ Park.

Michael Carrick may not last much longer at Manchester United either now that he has produced his own famous axeing. One difference between Shearer and Bruno Fernandes is that the latter did not appear at all in their 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford - an unused substitute to the end.

United have Chelsea next, and those at Stamford Bridge are used to facing a United caretaker in his first league game in charge. Carrick in 2021: a 1-1 draw. Ruud van Nistelrooy in 2024: another 1-1 draw. Darren Fletcher in 2026? Quite possibly. All that remains is the picture of the corner flag popping up on United’s social media feed to confirm Carrick’s departure.

Yet in what was potentially his last act as United manager, Carrick took a stand. He refused to placate Fernandes, who is a fabulous footballer, if also the master of moaning. His ego may be dented for being made an example of, but in truth, this was about more than the Portuguese and his hissy fits.

His disobedience as club captain afforded Carrick the opportunity to send the message that the lunatics have been running the asylum for too long. It is a team that have chewed and spewed too many managers.

Fernandes publicly criticised his coaches’ tactics after he was substituted during their 4-1 Champions League loss at Como. He could have been dropped for poor performances sooner, but his outburst forced the issue, and he was deservedly punished for his midweek act of mutiny.

It was a risk by Carrick, and one which did not deliver him the win he would have hoped for. He is not the first, nor will he be the last, manager to potentially use his dying breath to send such a message, however.

Bruno Fernandes's axeing could prove Michael Carrick's final act... 27 years after Ruud Gullit left Newcastle after leaving Alan Shearer on the bench against Sunderland

Michael Carrick acknowledges United fans at Old Trafford after the final whistle - but insisted it was not a wave goodbye and he does not know whether he will keep his job

One of the candidates to replace him, Antonio Conte, did so at Tottenham Hotspur. His speech after their 3-3 draw at Southampton was stunning. He essentially called on the club to end its excuse culture. He went down swinging. Conte was gone a week later.

So Carrick took his own swing. He may have missed, what with losing 3-0 without Fernandes, but it was needed as a reminder to United’s players that they are not bigger than their club.

And for that, good on Carrick, who may now lose his job as a consequence. At least he will have gone out with the supporters at Old Trafford singing his name before they showed the players what they thought of them.

But if United fans want to feel a little better, Newcastle replaced Gullit with the wonderful Sir Bobby Robson, and Shearer finished that same season scoring 30 goals.

Let's take a look at Arteta's dossier

You can think Mikel Arteta is slightly strange, but in this world of managers giving mundane answers to the media we should be thankful that every so often, the man in charge of the champions is willing to provide us with new insight.

This time, after being booked during the 2-0 win over Everton, Arteta told us how he has been clipping up footage of other head coaches stepping out of their technical area during matches. He insists he has evidence that another manager did so more than 30 times in 10 minutes without receiving a yellow.

That was gold dust for the World Wide Web. A glance at one online forum threw up a ton of ideas. Set up sensors around the technical area and have managers wear shock collars! Give the fourth official a water spray to teach them a lesson like a misbehaving cat! Set up rakes around the white lines so when they step on them, they get hit like Sideshow Bob from The Simpsons!

Good suggestions, all. It would certainly give Howard Webb’s Pro Ref one fewer issue to think about when they should have bigger concerns while trying to officiate the Premier League fairly.

Mikel Arteta clashes with fourth official Ruebyn Ricardo at the Emirates on Saturday after stepping out of his technical area

Jokes aside, from an Arsenal perspective, it is good that Arteta is willing to fight the narrative that he is the only one who behaves badly in his technical area. He is not. We all know he is not, and we should believe him when he claims he can prove it to Webb and Co.

Within that dossier might now be a clip of Roberto De Zerbi celebrating Tottenham scoring by invading the pitch at Chelsea. He had already been booked for a bust-up with the opposition bench.

Had this been Arteta, we might have heard more talk of what a naughty boy he is, and how he gets away with too much. But Arsenal should be glad that their manager is happy to hit back.

Cherries taking on the challenge

United lost, so inevitably, the temptation is to purely discuss them and their troubles. But it would be wrong for us to disregard the role played by Bournemouth, who secured their fourth consecutive win without conceding despite juggling European football for the first time ever.

Thursday: 3-0 win over Sturm Graz, Europa League. Sunday: 2-0 win over Sunderland, Premier League. Thursday: 3-0 win over AC Milan, Europa League. Sunday: 3-0 win over United, Premier League. Their fixture list before the November international break has Marco Rose’s team playing Wednesday, Saturday, Thursday, Sunday in three different competitions.

Which is one hell of a slog for a side not used to all this, and the greatest challenge they face. The travelling. The recovery. The training sessions they then squeeze in. Over the last two weeks, Bournemouth have handled it with impressive ease.

If they can continue to handle this workload, it can only help the club convince their players that they should not be seen as a stepping stone.

That is what Bournemouth, led by their owner, Bill Foley, want.

They do not want to be a temporary home to the Antoine Semenyos and Illia Zabarnyis and Dean Huijsens who find their way to them. They want to get to a place where they keep them.

Tactics backfired for Alonso

Chelsea found out the day before playing Tottenham that they would not have Joao Pedro, whose injury is being assessed and with no timeline yet placed on his return.

Xabi Alonso could have simply added Danny Welbeck to his starting line-up as a like-for-like replacement, a striker for a striker. But he tried something different.

He added Geovany Quenda to his line-up. It was his first start for Chelsea, and he acted as another No 10 alongside Cole Palmer while Morgan Rogers was a false nine.

With the power of hindsight, we can say it smacked of Alonso overthinking the problem as Chelsea never looked like beating Spurs with their 11th-hour shake-up. That the tactics then resembled ‘hoof and hope’ only made it more confusing that an actual striker was not used.

De Zerbi's turning point

As for Tottenham, that first victory at Stamford Bridge since 2018 should be a turning point for De Zerbi, more so than their win at Coventry which was helped by Carl Rushworth.

The performance itself was brimming with positivity, even as they impressively coped while losing James Maddison to a second-half injury. His replacement, Conor Gallagher, was like bait for Chelsea as a former player. Palmer fouled him to receive his second yellow. Rogers was fortunate that the refereeing team did not think he deserved red for giving Gallagher a kicking of his own.

Conor Gallagher was a nuisance against his former club and Morgan Rogers was lucky to avoid a red card for kicking him

Is sacking Pierre Sage really the answer?

The man may have taken over a Crystal Palace team which won the Conference League last season, but he inherited problems, and the suits upstairs cannot escape scrutiny for the players now at his disposal. They practically sold their back line without properly replacing them, and now have the worst defensive record in the Premier League.

Delap's image problem

Liam Delap does not help his image. He wants to be known as a footballer, but can sometimes bring to mind that bloke in Sunday league who is more interested in scrapping.

On Friday, the Nottingham Forest striker went for the ball with Ipswich captain Dara O’Shea, who was left with a shirt ripped to smithereens. Chelsea tired of that side to Delap’s game, and his lack of scoring, and did extraordinarily well to secure £50million for him in the summer.

Liam Delap tangles with Ipswich's Dara O'Shea during the 1-1 draw at Portman Road on Friday

Arbeloa's acid test

A text from a Craven Cottage contact a couple of weeks ago told us how even some players inside the Fulham changing room were unsure of Alvaro Arbeloa’s methods.

Arbeloa appeared on the brink at that time, then Fulham won twice in the Premier League, beating Hull City 1-0 and Coventry City 1-0.

Yet two narrow victories against newly-promoted sides will not end the noise entirely. Fulham’s next four league fixtures are against Aston Villa, Newcastle, Manchester City, Bournemouth. That is where he will be judged much more seriously.

Concern for Chappers

Mark Chapman is up there with the best sports broadcasters in the country, and normally such enjoyable company in our living rooms. We have to hope 'Chappers' is doing OK because his subdued appearance on Match of the Day – the BBC show beleaguered of late – was concerning to watch.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick returns to Carrington as bosses decide his Man United future: Glum manager pictured arriving at training base while Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers hold do-or-die summit
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has arrived at Manchester United’s training ground amid increasing uncertainty over his future as head coach. Carrick was pictured driving into Carrington on Monday afternoon following a day of crisis talks among club owners and senior executives over whether to sack him. United’s fringe first-team players and Under-21s including Tyler Fletcher, Harry Amass and Shea Lacey have a behind-closed-doors friendly against Hull City which kicked off at 2pm, but it is unclear if that is the reason for Carrick’s presence on his day off. Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox drove into the training ground early on Monday morning. The majority of the players have a rest day after Sunday’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford, although Bruno Fernandes, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte came into Carrington for treatment. Carrick dropped Fernandes against Bournemouth and left him on the bench following the captain’s criticism of the team’s tactics in last week’s Champions League defeat to Como. Berrada and Wilcox are understood to have held conference calls with co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer, and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to decide Carrick’s fate and identify a successor if the 45-year-old is axed. Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington to watch the under-21s - with his bosses deciding his fate Omar Berrada (left) and Jason Wilcox (right) are seen arriving at Carrington ahead of crisis talks with Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers Bruno Fernandes came into Carrington despite the players being on a day off Manchester United's head honchos are locked in talks about Carrick's future Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, both currently out of work and available to take over immediately, are the leading candidates after bookmakers stopped taking bets on Carrick being sacked. The former United midfielder has 18 months left on the two-year contract he signed in May after guiding the club back into the Champions League. After playing away in Spain and Italy over the last fortnight, United have a free week after going out of the Carabao Cup to Brighton and aren’t in action again until they meet Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday lunchtime. Carrick’s job is hanging by a thread after United suffered a sixth defeat in 12 games this season against Bournemouth. Afterwards the visibly emotional head coach appeared to say farewell to the fans, although he later insisted that was not the case. He also revealed that he had not spoken to Berrada or Wilcox over his future, although it’s understood that discussions have been taking place over the growing crisis among the United hierarchy before Sunday’s defeat. ‘Just briefly they came down like they always do after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary,’ said Carrick. ‘I totally understand the situation. I'm not expecting anything either way. I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. ‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see. ‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now? ‘I've tried to do everything I can to not be in this position, of course I have. For a number of reasons, we've not been able to stop that happening to the position we're in right now. ‘I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful to see us going through this at this moment in time. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough. ‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. ‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’

Sports.title: England captain Harry Kane's camp 'increasingly confident' he will be crowned world's best footballer TONIGHT, Spanish report claims
Sports.content:
England captain Harry Kane's camp 'increasingly confident' he will be crowned world's best footballer TONIGHT, Spanish report claims

Harry Kane's camp are increasingly confident that he will lift the Ballon d'Or tonight, according to a report in Spain.

The Bayern Munich striker is among the favourites to lift the gong in London alongside Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe.

After scoring 73 goals for club and country in the 2025-26 season, he is gunning to become the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

'The feeling surrounding Harry Kane is that, all things considered, his candidacy is the strongest,' write Spanish outlet Marca.

Kane helped fire England to the World Cup semi-finals and also won the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and German Supercup with Bayern.

The most prestigious individual honours in world football will be awarded tonight, with the likes of Lionel Messi, Jude Bellingham, and Rodri also in contention.

Presented by magazine France Football since 1956, it recognises the player judged the best in the world across the previous season. And since 2018, there has been the equivalent prize for the women’s game. Here’s all you need to know about tonight’s ceremony…

Kane is the bookies' favourite to win the Ballon d'Or tonight after scoring 73 goals in 65 games

Why is it in London?

With the exception of 2010-2015, when Zurich took the honour, the Ballon d’Or ceremony is held in France – with the last seven years in the Theatre du Chatelet in Paris. But this year the Palladium in London’s West End will host – perhaps a good omen for Kane. UEFA explained in May that the choice of venue is symbolic in tribute to inaugural winner Stanley Matthews, who received his award at Blackpool Town Hall. Seventy years on, and having accumulated a little more glitz and glamour over the decades, it returns to England.

Tonight’s show will be hosted by Arsenal and France legend Thierry Henry for the first time, alongside presenter Kate Scott, who returns for a fourth year. The 45-year-old is best known for her work on Champions League nights at US network CBS Sports, where she is a regular host alongside pundits Henry, Jamie Carragher and Micah Richards.

Henry – who was nominated for the award nine times – said: 'London is the city I call home, and I have a deep connection to its football culture and the passionate fans here, so to be hosting here alongside my friend and colleague Kate feels like a natural fit.’

Kane is looking to become the first English winner of the award since Michael Owen in 2001

How is it decided?

For the men’s and women’s awards a shortlist of 30 players is decided by journalists from both France Football and L'Equipe newspaper. This shortlist is then ranked by journalists from around the world – 100 for the men’s, 50 for the women’s – with their rankings combined to decide the winner.

Jurors are instructed to consider these factors: individual performances and impressive character; collective performances and titles won; class and fair play.

Who is favourite for the main awards, then?

HARRY KANE

Harry Kane has the best chance of ending England’s 25-year wait for the men’s Ballon d’Or, with the Three Lions captain the bookies’ favourite to take home the award tonight. And for good reason. The 33-year-old enjoyed a staggering year, with his 73 goals in 65 matches bettered only by Lionel Messi’s 79 goals when he won the prize in 2012. After his starring role against Arsenal in the Champions League last week, Kane insisted he remains in the dark as to his fate tonight, a reality that is eating away at his wife, Katie. 'I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rumours flying around and you try to stay away from it,’ he said. ‘I think my wife would prefer to know and my family… it's very stressful for everyone.'

KYLIAN MBAPPE

Kane faces stiff competition though, with Kylian Mbappe a close second among the bookmakers tonight. Mbappe dazzled at the World Cup this summer, where he became the all-time leading goalscorer in the competition’s history, with a total of 22. However, his lack of silverware – both domestic and international – this year could count against the Frenchman.

‘There are many people that speak about me and the Ballon d'Or. Of course I've made history in the most important competition. Maybe it's a good year for this but people can vote according to what they think,’ he said. ‘I always think I'm the best (player in the world) but everyone has their own opinion.’

‘I always think I'm the best (player in the world) but everyone has their own opinion,' Mbappe said of his own prospects of winning the award

LAMINE YAMAL

Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal closely follows Mbappe and Kane in the odds. The 19-year-old has the best trophy collection of the top three contenders – having won the World Cup and LaLiga – but his subdued role in Spain’s triumph may count against the youngster. Yamal’s numbers are dwarfed by Kane’s, too. He recorded 25 goals and 20 assists across 57 appearances, although the Spaniard has argued that the award should go to football’s most entertaining star, not the most clinical one.

Like Mbappe, Yamal has been campaigning ahead of the ceremony as he bids to become the youngest-ever winner. ‘I think the Ballon d'Or should go to the best player in the world, full stop,' he said. 'Not to a player who has scored 80 goals, because if you score 80 goals, you get the top scorer award for that. Those are two completely different things that people do not understand.' Whether Yamal wins the prize tonight or not, he is certainly destined to take home the accolade at some point during what promises to be a special career.

Other candidates: Lionel Messi, Rodri, Erling Haaland, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Women's Ballon d'Or

ALEXIA PUTELLAS

Meanwhile, Alexia Putellas is on course to end Aitana Bonmati’s three-year grip on the Ballon d’Or Feminin tonight. Barcelona midfielder Bonmati is out of the running after suffering a fractured fibula last November, keeping the superstar sidelined until May. She helped guide her side to an historic quadruple but her efforts were not enough to make the shortlist this year. With 24 goals and 13 assists, Bonmati’s former Barca team-mate Putellas – who this summer joined the London City Lionesses – led the way in the midfielder’s absence and is the favourite to be recognised for her exceptional year.

Other candidates: Ewa Pajor, Khadija Shaw, Pernille Harder.

Putellas is on course to end Aitana Bonmati’s three-year grip on the Ballon d’Or Feminin tonight

It’s not just player of the year, right?

The men’s and women’s prize are the two most eye-catching on offer – PSG’s Ousmane Dembele won it last year for the first time and Barcelona’s Aitana Bonmati landed the women’s crown for the third year in a row.

But there are also 11 more awards in a celebration of European football: men’s and women’s Kopa Trophy, for players under 21; the Yashin Trophy, for best goalkeeper, Gerd Muller Trophy for best striker, and Johan Cruyff Trophy for best coach.

Who is in the mix for BOAT? Lionel Messi Cristiano Ronaldo Ronaldo Marco van Basten Michel Platini Karl-Heinz Rummenigge Kevin Keegan Franz Beckenbauer Johan Cruyff Alfredo Di Stefano

There are also men’s and women’s awards for Club of the Year – and a Socrates Award, first given out in 2022 and for a footballer’s humanitarian work.

Last year that went to the Xana Foundation, founded by PSG boss Luis Enrique to support families with children facing serious illnesses – the Enriques’ daughter Xana died in August 2019 after battling bone cancer.

This year will also see the addition of a new prize: the BOAT (Ballon d'Or of All Time). The organisers have been keen to stress that it is not an official award like the ones above but it has already caused plenty of debate online anyway.

Fans are being asked to log-in to the Ballon d'Or website to vote on which past winner they believe was the best. However, they can only pick from one of the ten players to have picked up the golden ball on at least two occasions.

And those who pay the €1 fee to cast their vote will earn a chance at tickets to next year's ceremony.

This year will also see the addition of a new prize: the BOAT (Ballon d'Or of All Time)

How to watch

The ceremony will be free to watch on DAZN for UK viewers.

The Ballon d'Or's official website will also provide live updates.

Who our experts are backing…

OLIVER HOLT: Harry Kane

His record with Bayern Munich has been astonishing, up there with the goalscoring feats of Messi and Ronaldo in their pomp. To hit 73 goals, including his England strikes, in a single season is the stuff of legend and he came desperately close, with Jude Bellingham, to leading his country to its first World Cup final for 60 years. His closest challenger, Lamine Yamal, won the World Cup with Spain and is a stellar talent but did not have a good enough tournament individually to dislodge Kane.

NATHAN SALT: Harry Kane

It has to be Kane. I am one of those that puts a lot of stock in winning the World Cup and Lamine Yamal, my runner up tonight, did that. But the goal totals are staggering, and for that reason it has to be Kane lifting the award tonight. Kane won his domestic league with Bayern Munich, won the Super Cup, reached the semi-finals of the Champions League, and finished third in the World Cup, becoming England's all-time leading World Cup scorer in the process. His total of 73 goals last season blows his competition out of the water. Yamal is an exceptional player and will win multiple Ballon d'Or awards in his career. This year it's got to be Kane, though.

Kane said: ‘I think my wife would prefer to know and my family. It's very stressful for everyone'

IAN HERBERT: Harry Kane

For me, it can only be Harry Kane after a year of such extraordinary delivery: those 61 goals in 51 appearances for Bayern Munich last season and the highest ever goal tally by an Englishman in a single Champions League campaign. That from a creator and initiator, who also builds so much in the deeper-lying areas. The circumstances and pressure under which you achieve must also be factored in and that’s what made his six goals at the World Cup something quite apart. Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal feature in the Ballon d'Or but they pale by comparison.

BOBBY MANZI: Harry Kane

It has to be Harry Kane. Averaged over a goal a game and had a brilliant World Cup. The best goalscorer on the planet. It’s indisputable. He’s already claimed the European Golden Shoe and football’s most prestigious individual award must follow.

Women's Ballon d'Or

TARA ANSON-WALSH: Alexia Putellas

The former Barcelona captain's legacy is already firmly secure with two past wins in this competition, and there's nothing getting in the way of her clinching a record-equalling third tonight to join her national team-mate Aitana Bonmati. Aggrieved NWSL fans will continue to deplore their lack of recognition at this ceremony, but the misalignment between the dates the award covers and the north Americans' season means that the focus remains on Europe, and Putellas its queen. She captained Barcelona to a continental quadruple in 2025-26, clinching the Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and Champions League, and Bonmati's absence from the competition due to injury only makes the end result more clear-cut.

Sports.title: Lucky football punter, 45, wins nearly £1MILLION from a £4 corners accumulator
Sports.content:
There is a good day at the races and then there's this. A Portsmouth-based punter hit the acca of his life over the weekend, winning close to £1million from a £4 stake.

The Aston Villa fan, 45, put his spare change on 12 EFL matches all having over 11.5 corners, a bet that had odds of 249,346/1 on Betfair when placed.

Incredibly the bet landed – and the £997,385 winner is planning to treat his family and betting pals with his newfound wealth.

‘It was emotional, I felt little bit sick at first making sure it was real, and then obviously the reality kicked in,’ he said.

‘My wife was out at the time when I checked, I needed her to come back to clarify the amount that was in there, I kept asking her “this is right isn't it?” It didn't seem real, it's hard to put into words.

‘I didn't sleep much last night, thinking about what we can do with the money. It's a really good feeling, it's brilliant!’

A Portsmouth punter has become a millionaire after his 12 game acca paid out (pictured: Jimmy Dunne scoring from a corner for QPR against Swansea on Saturday)

At half-time on Saturday afternoon the bet looked to be a foolish investment with just one corner between Reading and Barnsley and four between Cambridge and Plymouth.

In the second half, however, the tides shifted and the set-pieces arrived in serious numbers, with Oxford v Bradford having 14 corners between them despite the game finishing goalless.

‘Me and my friends usually do an accumulator on the weekend for a bit of fun, we all pick a leg and put them in our group chat, both teams to score usually, and I like to do corners,’ he explained.

'I had £4 in my account, so I decided to do one of my own with a few more corners in. I'm sure that I'll be treating my mates after winning this one. It will be my round all the time!'

The punter didn't even find out his acca had made him a millionaire until the evening, saying that: 'I didn't actually realise it had come in until about half an hour after all the games had finished.

'I'm an Aston Villa fan and was out with my son watching the early kick-off, which started the day really well! Then we walked back home and got soaked with the weather, and when I checked my account I couldn't believe it.'

The jubilant football fan has humble plans for his £1million prize, hoping to pay off his mortgage, buy a car and book a week in the sun with the family, as well as going to watch more games at Villa Park with his son.

Betfair spokesman Sam Rosbottom said: 'We are absolutely delighted for this Portsmouth punter and couldn't be happier to pay out such a large sum of money.'

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes aims ANOTHER swipe at Michael Carrick: Captain likes cryptic 'loyalty' social media post less than 24 hours after Man United boss dumped star to the bench
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has seemingly aimed another dig at Michael Carrick after being dropped against Bournemouth. The Portuguese liked a cryptic Instagram post about 'loyalty' and 'no longer caring' on Sunday following the club's disastrous 3-0 thrashing at Old Trafford. Fernandes was axed for the clash after criticising his beleaguered manager's tactics in the aftermath of their 4-1 hammering at Como in the Champions League in midweek. 'Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care,' read the post, which the talisman liked. It is not clear why he did so, and his like appears to have been removed. The clip was from an animation film called A Tale of Momentum and Inertia, and shows a huge creature formed from rocks trying to stop a boulder from rolling onto a town. Carrick could be sacked after a dismal run of two wins in 12 games since being appointed on a two-year deal in the summer, with United 16th in the Premier League. The Manchester United hierarchy are in crisis talks over his future after the humbling defeat by Bournemouth, though supporters sang Carrick's name throughout the match. Bruno Fernandes has seemingly aimed another dig at Michael Carrick after Manchester United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth The captain liked an Instagram post which read: 'Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care' His decision to leave Fernandes simmering on the bench seemed to backfire, as United were thoroughly beaten by their opponents but the 32-year-old has failed to capture his best form this campaign. Gary Neville has sided with his old team-mate Carrick, accusing Fernandes of being an 'excuse merchant'. 'Eric Cantona was very unorthodox as a captain. Roy Keane could sometimes be explosive in his interviews after matches, but they weren't whingers about the tactics, about pressing, or excuse merchants,' he said on his Sky Sports podcast. 'Bruno can't press. To come out and whinge after the game about the manager's tactics, when you've just lost 4-1, and a few thousand fans have paid thousands of pounds to travel over in that far corner and get wet through. I'm sorry, read the room, Bruno. 'This is not a time for whingeing, throwing your arms up in the air. This is a time for you to stand up and say, that's not good enough. Be positive. Do something with a positive influence as a captain. But he's not. 'He's gone and basically thrown his manager under the bus the week after [Lisandro] Martinez did the same.' Neville added: 'They weren't singing for Bruno Fernandes to come on today. They're backing Michael Carrick. 'So get in your box. You know where you stand. Michael Carrick's won things for the football club on a constant basis, and proven that he can have the humility, the resilience. And Bruno has got that. Bruno has delivered for Manchester United in more ways than any other player in the last 13 years. Carrick dropped Fernandes to the bench after his recent outburst - but the decision backfired Gary Neville believes Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players 'He's massively talented but he let himself down this week. He didn't need to do that because he's basically stuck the knife into his manager.' Carrick did a lap of Old Trafford at full time, clapping the fans, but insisted he was not saying goodbye in doing so. 'It wasn't a farewell from me,’ Carrick insisted. ‘I probably didn't really expect that off the supporters, if I'm honest, but I've always felt the support and that connection with them. ‘It will take a bit of time to digest, but I certainly appreciate their support. It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. ‘I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. ‘It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility. We'll have to wait and see. ‘Of course, I take responsibility. I respect the position that I'm in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now? ‘I've been at the club a long time. It hurts an awful lot to see us going through this at this moment in time. The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough. United were beaten 3-0 at home by Bournemouth and the manager is hanging on by a thread ‘I'm feeling it for my players, they're going through a tough spell. There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, to be fair. ‘It's not like they don't care or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to, it’s affecting them a lot.’ There are questions about how much support Carrick has in the dressing room after Fernandes' outburst last week. Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle. 'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said. 'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.' But Harry Maguire came out in support of his gaffer after the Bournemouth loss, saying: 'At the moment we're not doing enough as players. Michael turned our season on its head last year and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven't performed well enough as individuals. 'We have got to find something, question yourself, look in the mirror, that's the most important thing - think what you can do more and contribute to the team and if we do that we'll get somewhere.' Former United defender Ashley Young, who won the 2012-13 Premier League title with the club, accused the players of 'giving up'. 'There have been different managers [in recent seasons] but it's the same players,' he said on Sky Sports. 'There have been a few changes in players but they're just not showing anything. You could tell today that it was like they'd given up - they're not running for this manager and they're not wanting to fight. 'The fans deserve so much more, you can tell they want more and they know he's been let down by those players.'
