Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora’s Inside Game Covers Poor Distance Control
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora’s towering stature is frequently billed as a nightmare puzzle for Jaron “Boots” Ennis. His gritty scrap against Ermal Hadribeaj exposed a deeper issue: height means little if you lack the hand speed and sharp timing to protect it.

Shawn Porter zeroed in on those deficiencies while breaking down Fundora’s October 17 win alongside Hadribeaj. The unheralded challenger slipped past the WBC junior middleweight champion’s reach all night, causing chaos until Fundora finally halted him with one tick remaining in round 12.

“He couldn’t time you last night,” Porter told Hadribeaj Porter’s channel. “You were coming after him, and there was not one moment where he saw you coming.”

Porter mentioned Timothy Bradley’s note that Fundora’s father deliberately schooled him in phone-booth infighting, knowing shorter foes would inevitably crowd him. Preparing for the trenches makes tactical sense. It does nothing to develop range control or a punishing perimeter game.

“You don’t have natural speed with the jab. You don’t have natural timing with the one-two,” Porter pointed out.

That gap undermines Fundora’s physical gifts. An 80-inch reach should turn the outside into a minefield, yet Hadribeaj walked into chest range round after round.

Labeling Fundora an inside specialist lets him off the hook. Smothering a foe by choice after dictating terms from the outside is one thing. Living on the inside because you lack the tools to keep opponents off your chest is entirely different. Porter’s critique puts Fundora squarely in that second camp.

Hadribeaj also smothered Fundora so effectively that the champion lost leverage on his trademark uppercuts. Porter observed that while a few broke through, the challenger took away the arc and velocity that crushed earlier rivals.

That pattern should set off alarm bells for Fundora’s camp ahead of a clash with Ennis.

Hadribeaj was an overlooked mandatory, not a pound-for-pound technician, yet he repeatedly forced the champion into disorganized exchanges.

Ennis would not have to wage a simple war of attrition. Boots could exploit those same entry lanes with explosive combinations, fluid stance switches, and evasive angles before Fundora resets his feet. Breaching Fundora’s perimeter would simply trigger a much heavier assault.

Hadribeaj maintains that Fundora’s rare height might still trouble Ennis. His own 12 rounds offered the opposite verdict: a modest puncher penetrated Fundora’s defenses at will.

Boots would still have to respect the champion’s durability, heavy inside clubs, and unrelenting output. Fundora eventually broke Hadribeaj through pure grit, and absorbing that type of heat drains any gas tank.

Fundora cannot gamble on elite punchers gassing out before his defensive gaps catch up to him. Halting Hadribeaj protected his belt, but it never answered Porter’s questions about how effortlessly he was reached.

Sports.title: Lindolfo Delgado Off Saudi Card Amid Safety Concerns
Sports.content:
Lindolfo Delgado is off the October 31 Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli undercard in Riyadh, according to Lance Pugmire, after trainer Robert Garcia publicly questioned the safety of traveling to Saudi Arabia.

“Told definitively that Delgado is off the Saudi card,” Lance Pugmire posted on X.

Delgado was scheduled to face Arthur Biyarslanov for the vacant IBF light welterweight title. His absence follows days of uncertainty over travel arrangements against a backdrop of attacks on Saudi airports.

An October 21 U.S. Embassy security alert reported that operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remained suspended. A separate travel advisory urged Americans to reconsider visiting Saudi Arabia because of drone and missile threats. Those warnings provide substantial context for the concerns Garcia raised before Delgado’s removal.

Garcia had spoken about his worries over taking Delgado and his team into the country while they still lacked travel arrangements. NY Fights reported those comments on October 22, several days before Pugmire’s update.

That makes this more serious than an ordinary fight-week cancellation. A boxer can spend months preparing for a championship opportunity and still face a decision that has little to do with the opponent across the ring. The importance of the belt does not remove the risks involved in reaching the venue.

Robert Garcia made the only sensible move a trainer can make in that spot. When a fighter enters title contention, the camp has to deal with enough variables inside the ropes without having to worry about closed airports, missile alerts, and basic travel logistics falling apart on fight week.

Pushing a fighter onto a plane under those conditions, especially with the U.S. Embassy issuing formal warnings in Riyadh, would have been reckless.

Biyarslanov has already arrived in Saudi Arabia, according to BoxingScene’s earlier reporting. He now faces uncertainty over whether he will fight Saturday and whether the vacant championship will remain available to him on this card.

Pugmire’s brief post does not specify the final decision-making process within Delgado’s camp or establish what happens to his IBF opportunity.

The organizers now have a missing title challenger days before the event. Finding another boxer may fill the slot, but it would not answer the travel and safety questions Garcia raised before Delgado was ruled out.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Didn’t Deserve Fighter Of The Year
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford’s win over Canelo Alvarez secured him 2025 Fighter of the Year honors from The Ring and the BWAA. It belonged in the Performance of the Year discussion instead. Beating an aging champion in a lone appearance was simply not enough to capture the sport’s top annual award.

Mike Coppinger raised that point on X, agreeing with Stephen “Breadman” Edwards that boxing needs a recognized Performance of the Year category. Coppinger argued Fighter of the Year should require at least two bouts, noting he backed Naoya Inoue for that reason. One spectacular night does not equal a complete twelve-month campaign.

Crawford’s backers cite the climb from 154 to 168 pounds to claim undisputed status in a third division. Those accomplishments carry historical weight, but the state of the opponent cannot be ignored. Canelo was 35, well past his physical prime, and later had surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. How much the joint limited him remains up for debate, yet it belongs in any honest assessment of the night.

The win also failed to answer key questions about Crawford at super middleweight. Taking on a dangerous contender like Osleys Iglesias would have tested him against prime physical power rather than an older, damaged champion. Crawford walked away and retired instead, leaving the Canelo bout as his sole 2025 appearance.

A factual detail also got lost in the online back-and-forth. Crawford did not capture the Ring or BWAA awards in 2023. Inoue swept both honors after stopping Stephen Fulton and Marlon Tapales, delivering two elite victories while Crawford fought just once against Errol Spence Jr.

Crawford earned recognition for beating Canelo, but Fighter of the Year went too far. Proving himself against an active, dangerous contender at 168 would have built a real case instead of relying strictly on the star value of a single name.

Sports.title: Zuffa Boxing Faces Expensive Gamble Rebuilding Conor Benn
Sports.content:
Conor Benn’s search for another massive payday puts him in treacherous territory after Ryan Garcia destroyed him in just two rounds. Eddie Hearn insists Chris Eubank Jr. stands as Benn’s lone viable move, openly wondering how Zuffa Boxing navigates this mess.

Benn commands enormous paydays, which makes soft matchmaking nearly impossible. Zuffa needs major events to justify its financial backing. Staging an uncompetitive tune-up becomes a brutal sell coming off an early knockout loss. Paying Benn top-tier money to beat up overmatched opponents turns into a fast way to burn through cash.

“The only fight for Conor Benn now is Chris Eubank. That’s it,” Hearn said to iFL TV. “Chris Eubank, ironically, holds the keys to Conor Benn’s next payday.”

A domestic clash with Eubank carries built-in nostalgia and guaranteed UK attention. In contrast, grinding out a rebuild at 147 pounds demands heavy lifting, since cruising past an overmatched opponent won’t erase the image of Garcia dropping him.

Benn must topple legitimate welterweight contenders to prove he belongs among the elite. His outings against Regis Prograis and Garcia offer plenty of reasons to doubt he can pull that off. Those bouts laid bare technical flaws that a soft touch can only paper over.

Zuffa might purchase some breathing room with careful matchmaking, yet Benn eventually has to face punchers capable of targeting those exact holes. That reality makes a gradual comeback an expensive gamble with zero guarantee of a payoff.

Hearn floated the idea that Zuffa could present Benn with lethal fights like Shakur Stevenson or Jaron Ennis, triggering immediate salary disputes.

“He’ll go, ‘I’m not fighting those guys for that kind of money,’ and they’ll go, ‘See you.’ He may never even fight again,” Hearn claimed.

Hearn didn’t quote Benn’s contract or point to a concrete offer Benn turned down. His forecast leans on speculation, though the underlying business logic holds up. Exactly how many setup bouts will Zuffa finance before demanding a dangerous matchup?

Old grievances clearly color Hearn’s comments. He still resents the way Benn walked out on Matchroom without picking up the phone after years of promotional loyalty.

“You can’t knock Conor Benn for taking the deal,” Hearn admitted. “What you can knock him for is the way that he treated me in terms of not even having a conversation with me.”

Personal bitterness aside, Hearn pinpoints a genuine dilemma. Benn’s price tag creates immediate pressure to deliver marquee fights, while his recent tape gives prospective rivals a clear roadmap to beat him.

Settling the score with Eubank delivers the quick cash grab Benn wants. Attempting to rebuild at welterweight forces Benn to take on dangerous contenders to restore his standing, which is precisely where the entire operation could unravel.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Could Abandon WBO Title Over Raymond Muratalla
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson could soon face a tough business call if the WBO installs Raymond Muratalla as his mandatory challenger at 140 pounds. Taking that fight means accepting real physical risk without the massive financial windfall tied to bouts against Devin Haney, Ryan Garcia, or Gervonta Davis.

Top Rank took the first step by petitioning the sanctioning body to elevate their top-ranked contender. A petition doesn’t make the fight a done deal, yet it instantly forces the question of whether Shakur actually wants the matchup if it gets ordered.

Nobody can say Shakur is running just yet. At the same time, wanting to wear a world title strap and wanting the specific challenger standing behind it are completely separate things.

Muratalla brings zero box office power compared to the superstars Shakur keeps calling out. The challenger hits hard enough to turn lights out, but that kind of heavy-handed grit rarely guarantees a huge network budget or career-best purse. Without any clear financial guarantees on the table, Stevenson would effectively be asked to accept a discounted payday for a fight that could destroy his road to far bigger money.

That threat doesn’t mean Muratalla has to outbox the champion for twelve rounds. Stevenson could easily control long stretches with his southpaw jab, footwork, and outside defense. Still, he would need to stay locked in every second Muratalla steps inside to plant his feet. One slip against a true puncher wipes out entire rounds of clean boxing.

Defending the belt carries obvious perks for Shakur. He retains his hardware, adds a legitimate scalp to his resume, and silences critics who would otherwise claim he ducked the division’s toughest boogeyman. Chasing mega-fights with Haney, Garcia, or Tank always involves tricky promotional hurdles and clashing timelines. A hypothetical super-fight puts no cash in the bank until ink hits paper.

If a genuine blockbuster offer surfaces right as the WBO issues a firm order, dropping the title becomes a very real temptation. Shakur would take heat from fans for walking away from an elite challenger, but boxing remains a business first.

Holding that WBO belt helps Stevenson sell himself as the top dog at light welterweight. If Muratalla gets named mandatory, holding onto the hardware means taking a fight where the physical risk completely outweighs the financial reward. Until Shakur puts his signature on a bout agreement, nobody should be shocked if that belt suddenly loses its shine.

Ghana News.title: Millicent Blay wins second edition of Breast Cancer Awareness Pink-Pong Tournament
Ghana News.content:
Millicent Blay of Nationwide Medical Insurance has won the second edition of the Breast Cancer Awareness Pink-Pong Tournament.

Blay emerged victorious at the tournament, which uses table tennis as a platform to promote breast cancer awareness and encourage conversations about the disease.

Speaking after her victory, Blay highlighted her long-standing relationship with the sport.

“I have been playing since I was a kid,” she said.

The tournament forms part of efforts to raise awareness of breast cancer through sporting activities, using table tennis to engage participants and encourage public conversations about the importance of breast cancer awareness.

Eric Apedo of Safety Communication Consult also highlighted the motivation behind the initiative, emphasising its role in promoting breast cancer awareness.

“This is an initiative to promote breast cancer awareness,” he said.

The event featured the presentation of medals to the winners, recognising their performances in the competition.

The second edition of the Breast Cancer Awareness Pink-Pong Tournament was supported by Ghana Link Network Services, AGL Gas, CBG Bank, Nationwide Medical Insurance Ltd., EMWA, Unicorn Petroleum Limited and Sankofa Spices.

The initiative continues to use sport as a tool to promote awareness of breast cancer and encourage greater public engagement with the cause.

Ghana News.title: ‘My life came down to 50 pesewas after quitting my white-collar job for poetry’ – Nana Asaase
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian poet and writer Nana Asaase has recounted how his decision to leave a well-paying public relations job to pursue poetry left him facing financial uncertainty, with his bank balance eventually dropping to just 50 pesewas.

Speaking on The Career Trail programme aired on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, Nana Asaase said his decision to leave the corporate world was driven by his belief that poetry was a calling he needed to pursue.

After completing his studies at the University of Ghana, he undertook his National Service at Originate, Saatchi and Saatchi, where he gained practical experience in public relations, including documentary production, scriptwriting, voiceovers, event coverage and newspaper reporting.

His career journey, however, began before university, when he combined teaching with newsreading at Eagle FM in Cape Coast.

According to him, his interest in journalism, inspired by the standard of English used by broadcasters he listened to.

Although he gained admission to the University of Ghana, he did not pursue opportunities at the university's Radio Universe, explaining that his academic work and interest in literature already demanded much of his attention.

Nana Asaase later joined Global Media Alliance as a public relations professional, where he earned what he described as a decent salary.

However, he became increasingly concerned about the future of Ghana's cultural and arts industry, particularly the gap emerging as older generations of creatives passed on.

“I realised that within the culture and art space, we already had a generational crisis. There's a gap,” he said.

He explained that the absence of enough people to carry forward the work of established cultural figures made him question how the industry would sustain itself in the years ahead.

However, his conviction to pursue poetry grew after he performed at an event and earned three times what he would have received as his monthly salary.

“So I remember one month where our salaries had delayed a little. It happens with agencies; it's not unusual. And then I had a poetry gig. I had a call from Michael, and I decided to accept. Then I whispered to God, ‘God, if you're really sending me here, don't let any of my media outlets come and cover this event.’ I went for the event, and true to that, none of my outlets came to cover that story. I finished the performance and came back to the office. I got paid three times what I would get paid at the end of the month in my PR job. So it reinforced the fact that if I gave this gift proper attention, it could become a source of income,” he recounted.

According to him, the experience reinforced his belief that he could earn a living from his talent if he gave it the necessary attention, prompting him to eventually resign from his job.

The poet said the financial difficulties began almost immediately. At the time of his resignation, he had only GH¢100 in his bank account, which dropped to GH¢50 after his car broke down the following day.

Despite the uncertainty, he remained committed to his decision, giving himself five years to make poetry work.

“When I quit my job, let me be very open about it, I had 100gh in my account at that time. The next day, my car broke down. Then it came down to 50gh. And my life actually came down to 50 pesewas,” he revealed.

Despite the uncertainty, he remained committed to his decision, giving himself five years to make poetry work.

“I told God, look, I'm giving you five years of my life. If this thing doesn't work, I'll never put a pen to paper in the name of poetry,” he revealed.

He recalled one particularly difficult experience when he and fellow poet Hashmullah performed at the Ephraim Amu Centenary celebration at the National Theatre. The two received an envelope containing GH¢10 to share.

“We were walking from the National Theatre via the British Council down to Adabraka. Then I was like, ‘I’m going to open the envelope and see what’s inside.’ When I opened it, it was not GH¢10 in one note, oh. It was ten one-cedi notes for two people. We took off our shoes, started playing the guitar, and then, praised God. We bought kenkey and fish with that money. I will never forget that day,” he recalled.

His breakthrough, however, came when he received a call from OSJ Consult, which opened doors to major performance opportunities, including RLG’s end-of-year party and Ecobank Transnational’s 25th anniversary celebration.

“I received a miracle call from OSJ Consult at the time. I don't know who had recommended me to them. But it was during that time when President Atta Mills had passed. So Oliver calls me. It was RLG's end-of-year party at the time. We had a discussion, and the money was very good money. Oliver was very helpful and instrumental. He gave me my biggest gigs at the time, RLG and then Ecobank Transnational at 25,” he highlighted.

Reflecting on his 12 years in poetry, Nana Asaase said the journey had reinforced his belief that perseverance could eventually open doors, even when progress appeared slow.

Ghana News.title: ‎Let’s return to plantain leaves for food takeaway – EPA CEO on Styrofoam ban
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Prof. Nana Ama Browne Klutse, has urged Ghanaians to embrace environmentally friendly food-packaging alternatives, including traditional plantain leaves, ahead of the nationwide ban on Styrofoam products scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027.

She called on households, food vendors, schools, traders and businesses to begin moving away from Styrofoam takeaway containers, stressing that early adoption of alternative materials would make the transition easier when enforcement begins.

‎

‎Prof. Browne Klutse made the call during a stakeholder engagement at the Savannah Regional capital of Damongo on Monday, October 26, 2026, as part of efforts to sensitise the public in the Savannah Region to the implementation of the nationwide ban.

‎

‎The event brought together members of the general public, food vendors, restaurant owners, traditional and religious leaders, students and other stakeholders.

Representatives of partner institutions, including the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Health Service and the Department of Food and Agriculture, also delivered solidarity messages and expressed their commitment to supporting the enforcement of the ban.

‎

‎The EPA CEO buttressed the view that the government had provided sufficient time for public education and stakeholder consultations, adding that the country must now move towards practical action to reduce the environmental and health risks associated with Styrofoam products.

‎

She highlighted the availability of alternatives, including biodegradable packaging, reusable containers and other materials that can be recycled or break down naturally.

‎

‎Professor Klutse encouraged Ghanaians to rediscover traditional food-packaging practices, including the use of plantain leaves where suitable, while urging businesses to explore affordable and sustainable alternatives.

‎

‎"The availability and use of alternative packaging materials could increase as demand grows, making it important for consumers and businesses to begin adjusting their practices before the enforcement deadline. And this is something we should commit to." Professor Ama Browne Klutse indicated.

‎

‎The CEO also emphasised that the campaign was not merely an announcement from government offices in Accra but a national responsibility requiring the involvement of everyone, from national leaders to individual community members.

She therefore invited stakeholders to take the message to their homes, workplaces, markets and communities to ensure that residents understand the importance of the ban and the need to adopt sustainable practices.

‎

‎On his part, the Savannah Regional Minister, Salisu Be-Awuribe, assured the CEO of the region of total commitment and dedication to the course of the environment.

Mr Be-Awuribe indicated the region's dedication to enforcing the ban from January 1, 2027, warning that the production, importation, and "Distribution, sale and use of prohibited Styrofoam products would no longer be tolerated in all seven Municipal and District Assemblies in the region after the deadline.

‎

‎According to the Minister,

the Savannah Regional Coordinating Council, the seven Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MDAs), the EPA, the Ghana Police Service and customs officers at checkpoints would be expected to support enforcement.

‎

‎"The time has come for us to act with one concern about the growing use and improper disposal of Styrofoam takeaway containers in communities including Damongo, Bole, Sawla, Buipe, Salaga and Daboya.

‎

‎According to him, "Discarded containers litter streets and public spaces, choke gutters and obstruct drains, contributing to flooding and undermining efforts to maintain clean communities. But I believe the Savannah Region can set the pace."Mr Be-Awuribe.

‎

‎‎The Minister further raised concerns about the harmful smoke produced when Styrofoam is burned and the potential health risks associated with using certain containers for hot foods, and identified other alternatives for redress.

‎"Paper packaging, biodegradable containers, reusable bowls and traditional food-wrapping materials are possible substitutes, while encouraging young people to explore opportunities in producing and supplying environmentally friendly packaging."

‎The Savannah Regional Director of the EPA, Abu Iddrisu, joined the call on residents and stakeholders to support the campaign, highlighting the importance of protecting the region's environment, agriculture, aquatic ecosystems and tourism sector.

‎

‎Dr Abu Iddrisu described the Savannah Region as Ghana's largest region by land area, a major food basket of northern Ghana and home to Mole National Park, one of the country's leading wildlife tourism destinations.

‎

‎He said environmental protection was particularly important to the region because of its contribution to food production, biodiversity and tourism, warning that pollution could undermine these important sectors.

‎

‎According to him, "Styrofoam waste can accumulate on land and in water bodies, damage the natural beauty of communities and contribute to environmental pollution and diseases." Dr Abu Iddrisu.

‎

‎He further explained that improper disposal of waste could affect farming communities through soil and water pollution, while discarded materials entering rivers and other water bodies could threaten aquatic life.

Dr Iddrisu stressed that the environmental "Reset agenda championed by President John Dramani Mahama required collective action from government institutions, traditional authorities, businesses, community leaders and the general public."

‎

‎He urged residents to take responsibility for keeping their surroundings clean and supporting measures aimed at reducing waste and promoting responsible disposal practices.

‎

‎The participation of the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Health Service and the Department of Food and Agriculture underscored the cross-sectoral importance of the campaign.

‎

‎And through their solidarity speeches, representatives of the participating institutions expressed their commitment to supporting efforts to implement the ban and protect the environment.

‎

‎Their involvement highlighted the connection between waste management, public health, agricultural production, tourism development, and law enforcement.

‎

‎The presence of traditional and religious leaders, students, food vendors, restaurant owners and members of the public also provided an opportunity to extend the campaign beyond government institutions to the communities and businesses directly affected by the policy.

‎As part of preparations towards the enforcement, the Savannah Regional Coordinating Council has announced a public education and clean-up campaign exercise to begin from October through to December 2026.

‎

‎The campaign is expected to target food vendors, chop bars, restaurants, hotels, guest houses, shops, plastic retailers, schools, lorry stations and other public spaces.

EPA, as part of its mandate, engages affected groups in local languages to explain the reasons for the ban, the products affected, and the alternatives available.

‎‎The nationwide ban is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027, with authorities intensifying public education and preparations to help businesses and communities transition away from Styrofoam products.

‎

‎The campaign seeks to promote cleaner communities and more sustainable packaging practices, with the EPA urging Ghanaians to begin making the change now rather than wait until the enforcement deadline.

‎

Earlier in the day, stakeholders embarked on a float on the principal streets of Damongo, holding placards with inscriptions such as choose reusable bowls and save money, Ghana bans Styrofoam packs?,and Ghana bans Styrofoam 1st January, 2027, among others, to help create the needed awareness ‎and education among residents.

The message from the three officials was clear: protecting the environment requires collective responsibility, and traditional practices such as using plantain leaves, alongside safe and affordable modern alternatives, could form part of Ghana's transition towards more sustainable food packaging.

Ghana News.title: Marketability of poetry hasn’t been explored enough – Nana Asaase
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian Poet, literary coach, and writer Philip Boakye Dua Oyinka, popularly known as Nana Asaase, has urged young creatives to explore the commercial potential of poetry, saying the art form offers opportunities beyond stage performances.

He believes poetry can be applied in various fields, including public relations, sales, marketing, music and academia, but many practitioners have yet to fully explore its marketability.

He made these comments in an interview on The Career Trail programme aired on Joy Learning TV and Joy News.

“Poetry or whatever craft you choose to get involved in pays you in so many ways. Of course, there is a pecuniary interest where there is fiscal cash. But it will usher you into spaces which other things otherwise couldn't have taken you into,” he said.

Drawing on his own experience, he explained that poetry had given him access to influential spaces, sensitive conversations and opportunities he might not otherwise have encountered.

“Poetry or whatever craft you choose to get involved in pays you in so many ways. Of course, there is a pecuniary interest where there is fiscal cash. But it will usher you into spaces which other things otherwise couldn't have taken you into. Take me for instance, I have walked into rooms I wonder which academic qualification could have opened for me. I have been privy to sensitive and important conversations and entrusted with documents from reputable organisations and individuals,” he shared.

He advised aspiring poets to prioritise developing their skills rather than making money their primary motivation, stressing that excellence in their craft could create opportunities for growth and recognition.

“If you want to do this and you're looking for money, it is good, but money should not lead. Hone the craft. Build it,” he emphasised.

He observed that some emerging poets expected quick financial returns and recognition, without giving themselves enough time to develop their skills, establish professional relationships and learn from experienced practitioners.

“Patience is a lot of strength. Patience is a weapon. Patience is a virtue,” he said.

He further cautioned young creatives against relying on social media engagement as the sole measure of their progress, urging them to accept constructive criticism and remain open to learning.

According to him, the ability to perform well when given an opportunity is crucial, as the quality of a creative's work can influence whether further opportunities come their way.

Beyond performance, Nana Asaase believes poetry has untapped commercial applications that could provide practitioners with additional income streams.

He cited songwriting for musicians, the development of content for public relations and marketing campaigns, sales promotion and teaching as areas where poetic skills could be put to use.

He also highlighted the cultural value of traditional appellations used to hail chiefs before they speak, describing the practice as an example of poetry that could be presented to wider audiences.

Nana Asaase encouraged poets to take advantage of opportunities in churches, schools, communities, weddings and other social gatherings to practise their craft, build confidence and connect with potential audiences.

He said recognising the wider applications of poetry, alongside a commitment to improving one's skills, could help practitioners move beyond the limited perception of poetry as an art reserved mainly for school programmes and special occasions.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi is a critical culprit in Tano Nimiri illegal mining case – Police investigator
Ghana News.content:
A police investigator in the case involving former Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has described him as a “critical culprit” in the alleged illegal mining activities in the Tano Nimiri Forest.

Chief Inspector Eugene Akpo Glover, the fourth prosecution witness, made the assertion during cross-examination by Wontumi’s lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea, at the High Court on Monday, October 26.

Asked who he had identified as a critical culprit in the investigation, Chief Inspector Glover told the court that “A2 (Wontumi) is a critical culprit in the ongoing investigation.”

The investigator, however, admitted that Wontumi had not personally operated any mining equipment in the forest, but insisted that his agents had used mining equipment in the area.

He identified the first and second prosecution witnesses, PW1 and PW2, as among those who had used the equipment.

When Mr Atta Akyea questioned whether the agents could have acted contrary to their employer’s instructions, Chief Inspector Glover maintained that the agents had acted in the interests of A1 (Akonta Mining) and Chairman Wontumi and for their benefit.

He also told the court that Wontumi had instructed his agents to mount barriers and signposts in the forest, insisting that the alleged instructions were captured in the evidence before the court.

The defence lawyer challenged the investigator’s account, suggesting that his understanding of the case was based largely on hearsay.

But Chief Inspector Glover rejected the suggestion, explaining that his conclusions were based on several investigative methods, including witness interviews, site inspections, drone surveillance and a review of documents.

He further cited Wontumi’s caution statement in 2021 and a letter allegedly written by PW1 to the Western Regional Security Council seeking assistance to drive away illegal miners from the concession.

A copy of the letter, he said, was personally handed to the police during interrogation.

Mr Atta Akyea argued that the letter demonstrated Wontumi’s opposition to illegal mining, but the investigator disagreed.

Chief Inspector Glover also told the court that between August and September 2022, security personnel from Akonta Mining took control of the forest and restricted forest guards and other security personnel from entering the area.

According to him, persons seeking to conduct lawful activities in the forest were required to obtain permission from Akonta Mining management and surrender their phones before being allowed entry.

He said the situation was documented in a police report submitted to the Commissioner of Police and the Inspector-General of Police.

When the defence lawyer demanded evidence that A1 and A2 were engaged in illegal mining, the investigator maintained that he had gathered what he described as “clear and convincing evidence” linking them to the activities.

He said the evidence had been captured in exhibits tendered before the court.

Chief Inspector Glover also defended the credibility of the prosecution’s evidence, insisting that the materials presented in court had been verified and authenticated.

However, he acknowledged that the alleged head of security who was said to have prevented officials from entering the forest had not been arrested and was currently at large.

He told the court that video evidence corroborating the allegation had been tendered in evidence.

The case was adjourned to Tuesday, October 27, at 9:30 a.m. by Justice Rugby Aryeetey for continuation

Ghana News.title: Nurse killed in attack while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
Ghana News.content:
A nurse has been killed and another health worker seriously injured in an attack as they were responding to an Ebola alert in north-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The two were targeted by local youths who accused them of contaminating water sources and spreading the Ebola virus, according to the UN-backed Radio Okapi. The World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the attack.

In an attempt to prevent the virus spreading, neighbouring Uganda has banned all non-essential travel to and from DR Congo and says its citizens returning from there will be quarantined for 21 days.

More than 4,800 people have died and nearly 10,000 been infected in DR Congo since this outbreak began in May.

Reacting to the attack in DR Congo, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said health workers "must be able to carry out their duties in safety and dignity", adding that healthcare personnel should always be protected.

The UN agency also extended its condolences to the family and colleagues of the nurse who was killed and wished the injured worker a swift recovery.

The BBC has contacted the Ebola response team for comment on the circumstances surrounding the attack in DR Congo.

This is not the first time such an attack has happened in DR Congo. Last month, a politician was beaten to death after promoting measures to stop the spread of Ebola, while in August, the Red Cross said its volunteers had been injured and an ambulance set on fire in 11 violent incidents during the first 100 days after the outbreak was declared.

Earlier this month, two countries - Kenya and Nigeria - reported their first cases of Ebola linked to the current outbreak.

The patient in Nigeria was on Monday flown from Abuja to Switzerland for further treatment.

She is the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat who had travelled to the Ugandan capital for a holiday, according to the head of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Jean Kaseya. She was evacuated alongside her husband, who has shown no symptoms.

Nigeria's health ministry said she was stable, conscious and able to communicate.

Authorities are now trying to establish where she contracted the virus.

The new restrictions announced in Uganda come after questions were raised over her case and that of a Kenyan businessman. Both tested positive for Ebola after travelling through Uganda, even though no cases have been reported there since August.

The Kenyan had arrived from DR Congo where he had business interests.

Only essential travellers, including aid workers, truck drivers and security personnel, will be allowed to cross the border from DR Congo to Uganda, subject to strict health screening, the health ministry announced.

In addition, all travellers entering Uganda, regardless of their country of origin, will be required to complete locator forms to facilitate contact tracing where necessary.

It said returning Ugandans would "undergo 21 days of quarantine at their own cost".

About 60 people who were being monitored after coming into contact with the Kenyan patient have all been discharged, it added.

In Kenya, the first group of 20 contacts of the first case have gone home, after spending 21 days in quarantine, the health ministry announced on Monday.

Another 98 are still being supervised, while seven people who have tested positive for Ebola were stable it said.

The Kenyan businessman died two days after arriving in Nairobi. A second woman, related to the businessman, died over the weekend.

"All these are measures to ensure that we keep Uganda free of Ebola," Uganda's Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi told the BBC's Newsday programme.

Since the two cases were reported in Kenya and Nigeria this month, Uganda has repeatedly stressed that no cases have been reported within its borders. Uganda recorded 20 Ebola cases and two people died shortly after the outbreak started in DR Congo, but the World Health Organization declared the country free of the disease in August.

The two passengers tested positive after passing through Uganda's Entebbe airport on the same day.

Diana Atwine, the health ministry's permanent secretary, said CCTV camera footage showed no physical interaction between the two patients.

Ugandan officials had previously said the patient in Nigeria had travelled to eastern DR Congo, only transiting through Uganda. On Sunday, however, the health ministry said Uganda and Nigeria were both working to establish her movements, complete travel history and possible routes of exposure.

The Ugandan health minister said the recent cases meant the risk had not ended and further underscored the need to "remain vigilant".

"We share a border with [DR Congo], where transmission continues, and our communities remain closely connected through trade, travel and family ties," Baryomunsi said.

The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind this outbreak is relatively rare and there is still no vaccine or specific treatment - though trials are under way.

Ghana News.title: DStv unveils four new subscription packages with prices from GH¢50 to GH¢570
Ghana News.content:
MultiChoice Ghana has announced four new DStv subscription packages, with monthly prices ranging from GH¢50 to GH¢570, as part of efforts to provide subscribers with more affordable and flexible viewing options.

The packages, which take effect on November 5, 2026, were unveiled at a joint press briefing organised by the Ministry of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovation and MultiChoice Ghana on Monday, October 26.

Speaking at the briefing, the Country Chief Executive Officer of MultiChoice Ghana, Alex Okyere, explained that the new packages offer different channel selections, sports coverage and entertainment content to suit subscribers' budgets and viewing preferences.

Under the new arrangement, the Starter Pack, priced at GH¢50 per month, provides access to 90 television channels, making it the most affordable option.

The Select Pack, which costs GH¢100 monthly, offers 123 channels, providing subscribers with a broader range of entertainment and television programmes.

For sports enthusiasts, the Sports Pack, priced at GH¢250 per month, provides football coverage alongside channels available under the Starter and Select packages.

The Ultimate Pack, costing GH¢570 monthly, is the highest-priced option, combining premium sports coverage with a wider selection of entertainment content.

MultiChoice Ghana explained that the revised subscription structure is intended to give customers greater flexibility in choosing packages that meet their entertainment needs and financial circumstances.

The new pricing arrangement will officially come into effect on November 5, allowing subscribers to select from the four packages based on their preferred content and monthly budgets.

Ghana News.title: Joe Mettle to headline Ɔdadeɛ bonfire night as PRESEC celebrates 9th NSMQ title
Ghana News.content:
Gospel musician Joe Mettle will headline the 2026 Ɔdadeɛ Torch & Bonfire Night as former students of Presbyterian Boys’ Secondary School (PRESEC), Legon, celebrate the school’s ninth National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ) title.

Dubbed the “ADO9 Edition”, the event will take place at the PRESEC School Park, Legon, on Friday, October 30, at 6pm.

Team Eternity Ghana and Daughters of Glorious Jesus will also perform at the celebration, which will combine gospel music, thanksgiving and the school’s torchlight and bonfire traditions.

Joe Mettle, whose songs include Bo Noo Ni, My Everything and Yesu Mo, will lead a line-up centred on praise and worship.

The annual gathering brings together generations of PRESEC old boys, known as Ɔdadeɛ, for fellowship and performances. Its signature activities include a torchlight procession and a bonfire lighting.

According to organisers, this year’s edition draws inspiration from PRESEC’s ninth NSMQ championship, with thanksgiving at the centre of the programme.

The event returned in 2023, while its 2024 edition featured dancehall musician Stonebwoy.

Organisers are inviting old students, year groups and friends of the school to celebrate the quiz champions and reconnect with fellow alumni.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Anthropic’s IPO filing shows explosive growth, risks and staggering costs
World.content:
The filing sets up the company for a wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing SpaceX’s IPO.

Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic has filed papers for what could be the biggest ever initial public offering (IPO) of stock, even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity.

The filing on Monday sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing the SpaceX initial public offering in June that raised a record $86bn.

The filing comes weeks after chief executive and cofounder Dario Amodei argued in an essay for slowing the development of the most advanced AI models. An IPO could provide Anthropic with enormous resources to accelerate its expansion. The amount the company ultimately raises remains uncertain, as does its final valuation and offering price. But even at lower estimates, it would turn the five-year-old startup into one of the world’s most valuable companies and potentially boost the wealth of Amodei and his sister and cofounder, Daniela, by billions of dollars.

The prospectus highlights the AI company’s rapid growth over the past year, fuelled by Big Tech’s breakneck spending that has driven a rally in AI stocks, while raising concerns about lofty valuations and rising debt.

The company also flagged growing risks from AI technology, underscoring concerns over its potential to cause harm, which had led Amodei to call for a slowdown in development of advanced models.

Anthropic’s net loss in the first half of 2026 widened sharply to $80.7bn, largely due to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into the company’s shares. Revenue in the period was about $16.3bn.



The company’s revenue grew a staggering 1,368 percent in the three months ended June 30 from a year ago, but warned in the prospectus that the revenue growth rate could decline over time and fluctuate occasionally.

The IPO, which is anticipated to be before Thanksgiving in the US, late next month, is expected to establish Anthropic, the AI lab behind the viral Claude models, as a benchmark for how Wall Street values leading AI companies, including rival OpenAI.

The IPO push comes despite a once-busy autumn listing calendar thinning out as choppy markets prompt companies to delay their offerings. Analysts said that would give Anthropic access to a deep pool of capital to fund its costly AI ambitions.

Growing investor unease with the debt-fuelled AI investment boom has led to a global selloff in AI and tech stocks, as they start to doubt whether the trillions spent on data centres, chips and computing capacity will generate fast returns to support lofty valuations. Higher borrowing costs and rising bond yields have added to their caution.

However, tech companies are still hungry for cash. Meta is aiming to raise up to $95bn in its largest-ever equity fundraising, while SpaceX has inked a $40bn deal with Apollo to lease AI chips and server hardware.

Some current and prospective investors are valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago, after the AI startup disclosed some financial details at a recent investor event, Reuters reported.

The prospectus also details the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI, from potential misuse and security threats to concerns that advanced systems could produce outputs that “could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative”.

“Anthropic’s IPO will establish a benchmark for valuing leading AI labs, influencing both upcoming listings and confidence in the companies funding the AI infrastructure build-out,” IPOX research associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

“Its success would not necessarily benefit every AI business equally,” he added.

Balancing AI’s promises and perils

Anthropic said that more than half of Fortune 500 companies and over 30 percent of Global 2000 firms were customers generating at least $100,000 each in revenue for the company over the 12 months ended September 30.

The IPO comes as Anthropic’s own research raises concerns about advanced AI systems, which in controlled tests have shown behaviours including code sabotage, fraud assistance and information manipulation.

The findings have fuelled concerns about how companies can keep powerful AI systems under control as they race to deploy them commercially.



The ‌‌‌‌prospectus also highlighted risks associated with its AI models, which it said could exhibit “self-preserving behaviours”, including behaviour “resembling blackmail”.

“Our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate and implement corresponding safety, alignment and security measures,” it said.

The company said it relies on a limited number of cloud service providers, such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft and suppliers such as Broadcom for compute and critical parts of its infrastructure. These relationships can create “dependencies and potential vulnerabilities”, it said.

Anthropic will trade on the Nasdaq after the IPO closes under the ticker symbol “ANT”.

The filing did not reveal the terms of its offering, including the number of shares it plans to sell and the proposed price range.

Red-hot growth

Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers, was valued at $965bn in May in a funding round that drew some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley and Wall Street.

Amazon and Google were among Anthropic’s early strategic partners, investing billions of dollars in the startup while providing the cloud infrastructure needed to train and deploy Claude models.

“We believe this abundance of AI will rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialisation, electricity, semiconductors and the internet,” the prospectus said.

World.title: ‘Everything destroyed’: Hebron businesses count cost of Israeli assault
World.content:
Hebron, occupied West Bank – Sufyan al-Qawasmi stood near the rubble of his factories in the Farsh al-Hawa area of Hebron, lamenting the business he watched vanish beneath the debris.

Israeli bulldozers demolished the factories on Friday without any prior warning or notice, following a shooting attack carried out by two Palestinians that morning near Hebron’s western entrance. The attack killed two Israeli soldiers, as well as the two Palestinian gunmen, and prompted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to announce a large-scale military operation across Hebron and order preparations for a wider closure of the illegally occupied West Bank.

Demolitions are regularly used by Israel to punish Palestinians, typically the family members of attackers, but in al-Qawasmi’s case, for the misfortune of being close to the site of an attack. Human rights groups decry the practice, which is regarded as collective punishment.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich justified the demolitions as “establishing deterrence and exacting a price”.

The Israeli bulldozers destroyed a business that al-Qawasmi’s family had built up for his whole life, and provided a livelihood for more than 70 people. The first factory, which produced ceramics, is the same age as he is – it was established 50 years ago. Fifteen years later, the family opened a marble factory.

Their business flourished, becoming one of the most significant industrial operations in the West Bank, with goods exported to Israel.

In the space of a few hours on Friday, the ceramic factory and marble factory were gone, as well as several neighbouring buildings, including a three-storey house and various commercial facilities. Simultaneously, the city faced an Israeli military incursion that included the closure of all entrances, raids, arrests, and the forced evacuation of more than 3,000 Palestinians from their homes, severely disrupting the lives of residents and the city’s commercial activity.



The message was clear: the whole city would be punished for the actions of the attackers.

A devastating loss

Al-Qawasmi says he was given no chance to retrieve goods from the family businesses’ warehouses and factories before the demolitions began, leaving the stock buried under the rubble, where it remains.

“We managed to retrieve some marble slabs and store them in facilities belonging to friends nearby, but most of the stock was destroyed,” he told Al Jazeera.

Al-Qawasmi says that 1,300 square metres of their business’ property was destroyed, including the family’s offices. He estimates the losses at no less than 60 million shekels ($19m).

Those losses are devastating for al-Qawasmi’s family, but also for the wider economy in Hebron and the Palestinian economy as a whole.

According to the Hebron Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Hebron serves as a primary pillar of the Palestinian economy, contributing approximately 42 percent of the Palestinian gross domestic product (GDP). It is home to more than 23,000 economic establishments, including more than 5,000 industrial and artisanal facilities that employ approximately 40,000 workers.

Hebron’s economy is notably diverse, encompassing sectors such as stone and marble, plastics, metals, food production, leather and footwear, and glass, alongside robust commercial and agricultural activity.

Adnan al-Natsha, vice president of the Hebron Chamber of Commerce, told Al Jazeera that there are no precise figures yet regarding the total losses resulting from the Israeli military operation so far. He noted that work is currently under way to compile statistics on the damage inflicted on businesses and homes, losses estimated to be in the millions of dollars.

Al-Natsha explained that the extensive Israeli measures, including closing off areas of the city, displacing residents from their homes, demolishing buildings and shutting down commercial shops, have exacerbated the already difficult economic situation in Hebron – which already has an illegal Israeli settlement in its commercial centre that severely disrupts Palestinian movement and trade there.

“Business owners have been unable to operate their facilities because workers couldn’t reach their workplaces, and employees have been unable to get to their jobs. The impact of these measures is not limited to Hebron; it extends to the Palestinian economy as a whole,” he stated, adding that work was ongoing to assess the losses and damages of the ongoing Israeli operation so far.

Paralysed commerce

The Israeli military continues to lock down Hebron, including the installation of checkpoints, earthen berms, and concrete blocks across the city, as it conducts raids. As a consequence, economic activity has been severely disrupted.



Ibrahim Ahmaro, who owns a vegetable shop in the al-Jalada neighbourhood, one of the areas targeted by the Israeli operation, told Al Jazeera that he had been arranging his stock on Friday, preparing for Saturday, which is typically the busiest day for commerce due to the arrival of buses carrying Palestinian citizens of Israel shopping for cheaper produce.

Military vehicles suddenly stormed the area, and soldiers forced Ahmaro to leave his shop immediately. He says that he wasn’t given an opportunity to turn on the refrigeration units, which would have kept his goods from spoiling, nor allowed to retrieve his vehicle, which remained parked in front of the shop.

“My brother, the staff and I all left, thinking it would only be for a few hours. Instead, we were met with a total lockdown of the area, and we were unable to reach our shops, meaning everything inside was lost after being left unattended for days,” he added.

On Sunday morning, Ahmaro was able to return to check on his stock, despite the heavy military presence in the area. As soon as he entered, he said soldiers attacked him inside the shop and forced him out. He pleaded with them to let him remove at least a few crates; they granted him a few minutes to do so.

“I placed the crates 400 metres away from the shops so that local residents, facing the lockdown, could take whatever they needed. My losses on these goods alone exceed 50,000 shekels [$16,200],” he said with a sigh.

Economic expert Ali Oweiwi said that the Israeli military’s restrictions and lockdowns imposed on Hebron have created significant challenges for commercial and industrial establishments, which rely on road access to transport production supplies and distribute their products.

He explained that the impact of the closure is not limited to retail shops but extends to companies, factories, suppliers, and the transport and logistics sector, not to mention the workers who are forced to take alternative routes to reach their workplaces, all of which ultimately affect consumers.

Oweiwi said that if the Israeli operation concludes within a day or two, the economy might recover relatively quickly. However, if it persists for more than 10 days, it could lead to significant problems, including the accumulation of goods, disruptions to transport and a decline in productivity due to the difficulty of moving both workers and merchandise.

Israel – which will vote for a new parliament in pivotal elections on Tuesday – has not announced an end date for the lockdown in Hebron.

“The destruction of facilities specialising in vehicle dismantling, spare parts, and tile shops has resulted in losses estimated at 70 to 80 million shekels ($22.7m to $26m), in addition to the seizure of dozens or perhaps hundreds of vehicles belonging to the owners of these establishments,” Oweiwi said.
