World.title: The presidential election in Brazil is a test of Trump’s power as a kingmaker.
World.content:
Conservationists fear a return to the rapid deforestation in the Amazon rainforest if Flávio Bolsonaro carries the vote on Sunday.

A number of right-wing leaders have recently swept into power in Latin America, riding a wave of dissatisfaction with incumbent governments and deepening worries about security and a rising cost of living.

Until now, Brazil, the region’s largest nation, had been the exception. The left-wing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, began his third nonconsecutive term in 2023. His predecessor and rival, Jair Bolsonaro, had been convicted of trying to stage a coup to prevent Mr. Lula from taking office and was sentenced to 27 years, which he is currently serving under house arrest for health reasons.

Now Mr. Lula, weighed down by widespread perceptions of rising crime and economic woes, faces a challenge from the former president’s son, Flávio Bolsonaro, a right-wing senator. Mr. Bolsonaro’s formidable performance in the first voting round this month gave him the edge going into a two-way contest.

The outcome will have a profound effect on Brazil and its relations with the United States in particular. Here are some of the major issues at stake.

Security

Mr. Bolsonaro has already said he would add Brazil to the Trump administration’s anti-cartel coalition, called the Shield of the Americas, and work with the United States to fight Brazilian gangs.

He suggested in social media posts last year that he would welcome U.S. military intervention in Brazil, though he denied that in recent interviews, saying the cooperation would be limited to intelligence. But it was Mr. Bolsonaro who successfully lobbied Mr. Trump to designate two Brazilian gangs as terrorist groups.

Mr. Lula has resisted joining the coalition, warning that intertwining too closely with the United States on security matters could threaten the nation’s sovereignty.

Trade

The Trump administration imposed tariffs on Brazilian products in an unsuccessful pressure campaign to disrupt the prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro. Many of those tariffs were eventually scaled back, and Brazil’s economy has remained largely unharmed by President Trump’s tariff campaign.

Another term for Mr. Lula, however, would increase the risk of more economic conflicts with the United States that might hurt the Brazilian economy. Of course, Mr. Bolsonaro would not be immune to those problems; Mr. Trump has been known to levy tariffs against allies as well as adversaries.

The Trump administration has signaled an interest in importing Brazilian oil to counter disruptions related to the Iran war and the country’s rare-earth minerals to reduce U.S. dependence on China for those resources. Mr. Bolsonaro is expected to align Brazil more closely with the United States than Mr. Lula has on trade issues, but neither leader can afford to anger China, a major trading partner.

The election could also affect Brazil’s ability to negotiate trade with the United States as a bloc with other countries in the region.

“Brazil’s relations with its neighbors have been extremely challenging,” said Carolina Moehlecke, an assistant professor of international relations at Getúlio Vargas Foundation, a research institution. This was especially true of its neighbor, Argentina, she added, whose right-wing president is a close ally of Mr. Trump. Mr. Bolsonaro, she said, might have an easier time cooperating with fellow right-wing leaders in Latin America.

Domestic Policy

If Mr. Bolsonaro carries the vote, conservationists fear a return to his father’s policies of allowing rapid deforestation in the Amazon rainforest, a trend that was largely reversed under President Lula. The younger Mr. Bolsonaro does not believe that climate change is caused by humans and has defended opening up protected lands to mining and farming.

He has also pledged to stem the nation’s rising debt. If he attempts to accomplish that through cuts to public spending, that could prove politically sensitive, Ms. Moehlecke said, especially when it comes to social welfare policies with broad popularity in Brazil. In the lead-up to Sunday’s elections, Mr. Lula had promised to increase welfare payments.

Democracy

Mr. Lula has framed the election as a test of the nation’s democracy and portrays the Bolsonaros as a threat to democratic institutions. Ms. Moehlecke said it was likely Mr. Bolsonaro would take the country in a more authoritarian direction, though his rhetoric is generally tamer than his father’s.

But if Mr. Bolsonaro wins, his party’s gains in the legislature could allow him to deliver on some of his most polarizing promises: amnesty for his father, pardons for rioters who stormed Brazil’s halls of power after the last election, and a Senate more willing to try to remove justices who convicted his father.

If Mr. Lula wins, he most likely will face significant checks against his power. Right-wing candidates, including four other members of the Bolsonaro family, have made significant strides in the nation’s legislative races.

Until now, Brazil, the region’s largest nation, had been the exception. The left-wing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, began his third nonconsecutive term in 2023. His predecessor and rival, Jair Bolsonaro, had been convicted of trying to stage a coup to prevent Mr. Lula from taking office and was sentenced to 27 years, which he is currently serving under house arrest for health reasons.

Now Mr. Lula, weighed down by widespread perceptions of rising crime and economic woes, faces a challenge from the former president’s son, Flávio Bolsonaro, a right-wing senator. Mr. Bolsonaro’s formidable performance in the first voting round this month gave him the edge going into a two-way contest.

The outcome will have a profound effect on Brazil and its relations with the United States in particular. Here are some of the major issues at stake.

Security

Mr. Bolsonaro has already said he would add Brazil to the Trump administration’s anti-cartel coalition, called the Shield of the Americas, and work with the United States to fight Brazilian gangs.

He suggested in social media posts last year that he would welcome U.S. military intervention in Brazil, though he denied that in recent interviews, saying the cooperation would be limited to intelligence. But it was Mr. Bolsonaro who successfully lobbied Mr. Trump to designate two Brazilian gangs as terrorist groups.

Mr. Lula has resisted joining the coalition, warning that intertwining too closely with the United States on security matters could threaten the nation’s sovereignty.

Trade

The Trump administration imposed tariffs on Brazilian products in an unsuccessful pressure campaign to disrupt the prosecution of Jair Bolsonaro. Many of those tariffs were eventually scaled back, and Brazil’s economy has remained largely unharmed by President Trump’s tariff campaign.

Another term for Mr. Lula, however, would increase the risk of more economic conflicts with the United States that might hurt the Brazilian economy. Of course, Mr. Bolsonaro would not be immune to those problems; Mr. Trump has been known to levy tariffs against allies as well as adversaries.

The Trump administration has signaled an interest in importing Brazilian oil to counter disruptions related to the Iran war and the country’s rare-earth minerals to reduce U.S. dependence on China for those resources. Mr. Bolsonaro is expected to align Brazil more closely with the United States than Mr. Lula has on trade issues, but neither leader can afford to anger China, a major trading partner.

The election could also affect Brazil’s ability to negotiate trade with the United States as a bloc with other countries in the region.

“Brazil’s relations with its neighbors have been extremely challenging,” said Carolina Moehlecke, an assistant professor of international relations at Getúlio Vargas Foundation, a research institution. This was especially true of its neighbor, Argentina, she added, whose right-wing president is a close ally of Mr. Trump. Mr. Bolsonaro, she said, might have an easier time cooperating with fellow right-wing leaders in Latin America.

Domestic Policy

If Mr. Bolsonaro carries the vote, conservationists fear a return to his father’s policies of allowing rapid deforestation in the Amazon rainforest, a trend that was largely reversed under President Lula. The younger Mr. Bolsonaro does not believe that climate change is caused by humans and has defended opening up protected lands to mining and farming.

He has also pledged to stem the nation’s rising debt. If he attempts to accomplish that through cuts to public spending, that could prove politically sensitive, Ms. Moehlecke said, especially when it comes to social welfare policies with broad popularity in Brazil. In the lead-up to Sunday’s elections, Mr. Lula had promised to increase welfare payments.

Democracy

Mr. Lula has framed the election as a test of the nation’s democracy and portrays the Bolsonaros as a threat to democratic institutions. Ms. Moehlecke said it was likely Mr. Bolsonaro would take the country in a more authoritarian direction, though his rhetoric is generally tamer than his father’s.

But if Mr. Bolsonaro wins, his party’s gains in the legislature could allow him to deliver on some of his most polarizing promises: amnesty for his father, pardons for rioters who stormed Brazil’s halls of power after the last election, and a Senate more willing to try to remove justices who convicted his father.

If Mr. Lula wins, he most likely will face significant checks against his power. Right-wing candidates, including four other members of the Bolsonaro family, have made significant strides in the nation’s legislative races.

World.title: Italy’s Young Protesters Return to the Streets
World.content:
Demonstrators across Italy on Saturday protested economic inequality and the political establishment. A heavy police presence throughout the country aimed to prevent the looting and violence that occurred during protests last weekend.

Young people demonstrated across Italy on Saturday amid a heavy police presence to prevent the looting and violence that occurred during protests last weekend.

The demonstrations echoed student protests in France that have unleashed a nationwide groundswell of frustration there, sparking the country’s worst rioting in decades.

Italy’s marches on Saturday were largely peaceful, though protesters clashed with the police in Turin, Padua, Bologna and Rome, where a small group of demonstrators stormed the Colosseum. The police arrested just nine people nationwide and reported 87 to prosecutors, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.

In Milan, the site of last week’s largest and most violent demonstrations, some 10,000 people hit the streets, the police estimated — five times as many as had marched the previous weekend.

Throngs of young people chanted about their frustration with the high cost of living and Italy’s political establishment. They held hand-drawn signs denouncing low wages, high rents, economic inequality and Italy’s financial support of Israel, whose war in Gaza is deeply unpopular with Italians.

Protesters said that the country’s sluggish job market and a government they saw as more focused on military spending than on investing in young people had set their generation up to fail.

“I look for work abroad every day of my life,” said Ilaria Carrozza, 27, a design engineer. “And that’s not fair: This is my country, I want to stay here. But I can’t live like this.”

Manfredi Cacioppo, a 26-year-old sales assistant from Sicily, said he was demonstrating in solidarity with truckers and farmers in southern Italy, who had recently blockaded roads and ports to protest high fuel prices caused by the war in Iran.

“It all comes from the same issue: money being spent on war,” he said. “That money would be better to invest in health, education, transport, the housing crisis and help for the workers.”

Last weekend’s demonstrations took Italy’s northern cities by surprise. In Milan, groups of masked young people set fires, looted stores and lobbed projectiles at the police, causing an estimated $1.1 million in damage, according to a local business association. Fifty-one people, most of them minors, were arrested.

Milan’s left-wing mayor accused the national police of “having underestimated the moment” and posting too few officers to the scene. Italy’s right-wing interior minister accused the mayor of pandering to the left.

Giorgia Meloni, Italy’s prime minister, called an emergency meeting on Monday and announced tougher penalties for violent protesters. A cabinet member, Matteo Salvini, said that the government would send 500 soldiers to Milan this weekend to “defend” the city against “criminals.”

On Saturday, army vehicles and police vans dotted many of Milan’s main squares, and numerous stores in the city’s shopping district boarded up their windows. Throughout the city, plainclothes police officers stopped groups of young people to check their identification documents.

For many protesters, the first challenge was figuring out where to go.

A social media account that helped organize the protests was supposed to post a meeting place at 2:30 p.m. But shortly before then, the Milan police said they had detained the account’s owner. The announcement never came.

Image Protesters in Rome on Saturday. Credit... Remo Casilli/Reuters

That left many demonstrators unmoored. In bars and online chat rooms, they argued over where, and whether, to show up.

“We were lost and confused,” said Caterina Sironi, a 23-year-old university student. “We ran all over the whole city.”

Ruggero Lorenzi, 19 and a high school student, crisscrossed Milan on three trains and a tram in search of a demonstration. “On Telegram, on Instagram, in metro stations, everyone was fighting over where to go,” he said.

After several false starts — “ten people over here, ten people over there,” he said — he found about 500 protesters gathered near a subway stop in the city center.

As Mr. Lorenzi’s protest snaked through the city to the Politecnico di Milano, Milan’s oldest university, its ranks swelled.

Many protesters said they were eager to keep the demonstration peaceful, hoping their message would be heard. The police used tear gas and water cannons against protesters in other cities on Saturday, but not in Milan, where they reported that there had been no violence or damage.

“We’re trying to emulate the French protests,” said Joshua Flores, 21, who is unemployed. “I hope this protest continues in a positive way.”

World.title: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
World.content:
Brazil's President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro.

Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil's return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting.

Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a "loss for negativity, lies", adding "long live democracy".

FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has so far refused to recognise the result and called for it to be annulled. World leaders have congratulated Lula on his re-election.

Bolsonaro's rejection comes as no surprise to observers. His father did the same.

But a challenge appears unlikely to succeed.

Firstly, it seems to centre on the unprecedented decision by the Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours. Some Bolsonaro fans are pointing out that Zanin was once Lula's lawyer and alleging bias.

But both teams had requested an extension to voting times - Lula's had argued that voters in SÃ£o Paulo and Bahia could not get to the polling stations because of a lack of buses, while Bolsonaro's campaign cited heavy rain in some areas in the south of the country and in SÃ£o Paulo as their reason.

Both knew every vote would count and did not want their side to miss out.

The president of the Supreme Electoral Court KÃ¡ssio Nunes Marques â appointed by Jair Bolsonaro â confirmed Lula's victory and said that the voter extension did not change the outcome of the race.

The sheer gap between the two candidates' tallies - 4.4 million votes - makes the result more difficult to challenge.

World.title: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
World.content:
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar VuÄiÄ has admitted defeat to a student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections.

Celebrations erupted as crowds descended on the centre of Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities.

The student movement was formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption and negligence, but fought the election with candidates from a cross-section of Serbian society.

"It is clear we have lost these elections," right-wing populist leader VuÄiÄ said as he conceded. With 97% of polling stations counted, Serbia's election commission said the students had won 2.25 million votes and the former ruling party 1.67 million.

The students had secured 52.7% of the vote, while VuÄiÄ's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) was on 39.2%, according to its preliminary figures late on Monday morning.

VuÄiÄ had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017.

He called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a canopy in front of Novi Sad station which killed 16 people.

World.title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack
World.content:
On Monday, the court was shown three pieces of CCTV footage from inside Tape nightclub on the night of the attack.

The attack lasted no more than 20 seconds, but Brown could be seen hitting the victim four times with a tequila bottle, twice to the head.

Prosecutor, Heidi Stonecliffe KC, described the weapon as a "heavy square-shaped tequila bottle" and said Diaw was approached by Brown at around 03:00.

The footage showed that the nightclub was very small and packed at the time.

The defence described Chris Brown as a "dedicated and a loving father of four children," someone who is "positive and present".

The singer is described as having lived "a good and law-abiding life" since his last conviction in 2013.

The events in Tape nightclub were described by the defence as a "short and deeply regretted incident".

Brown's defence lawyer told the court that he apologises to all those present at the club at the time of the attack.

"This is an ugly and unattractive incident," Sallie Bennett-Jenkins KC said.

"It is, however, an incident which was very short-lived, lasting something more than 17 seconds but no more than 20.

"It is something which undoubtedly would have caused distress to those who are present and for which Mr Brown... offers a profound apology to all those present."

The court heard Akinlolu "genuinely believed" that Brown was "under attack" when he joined the attack, punching Diaw.

Brown was described as being like a "brother" to Akinlolu, his lawyer Laurie-Anne Power KC told the court.

She added: "He genuinely believed him to be under attack and became involved, and thereafter accepts his initial involvement very quickly evolved into the events he has pleaded guilty to."

Diaw was taken to St Mary's Hospital in London after the attack. Ms Stonecliffe KC said he was discharged with "pain relief and a diagnosis of head injury and superficial injury of the knee".

An MRI scan taken in early March showed a "high grade injury to a ligament on the inner side of the left knee", the court heard.

Defending Brown, Ms Bennett-Jenkins KC said there was a "relatively low level of force" and disputed how significant the injuries were.

The defence argued that the attack left no fractures or broken skin and there was an absence of serious injuries.

Diaw, the victim, was "not supportive of the prosecution" and "withdrew" his support some time after the incident, the court heard.

World.title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
World.content:
Anthropic has warned artificial intelligence (AI) could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" as it unveiled details of its planned blockbuster stock market listing in the US.

The firm's valuation is expected to exceed that of SpaceX, which was the biggest-ever listing at an initial valuation of about $1.8 trillion in the summer.

Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be released, their price range, or a date for the listing.

The Claude chatbot developer reported $16.3bn (Â£12.2bn) of revenue in the first half of the year, with losses of more than $80.7bn.

Anthropic, which said it will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology.

In a filing ahead of its listing, Anthropic said concerns had been raised by policymakers, regulators and researchers as well as by people within its organisation that AI systems posed a significant risk to humanity.

It said advanced AI systems "could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy".

Anthropic was founded five years ago by chief executive Dario Amodei, his sister Daniela Amodei and five others, and announced its intention to go public in June.

Its main rival, OpenAI, quickly followed suit. That listing is now expected to occur early next year, according to a person familiar with OpenAI's plans.

Those announcements were followed by a wave of cyber-security and other technological breaches involving their AI agents - bots designed to operate somewhat autonomously.

Current and former staff of both companies also warned AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI tools.

As Anthropic revealed its stock debut plans on Monday, the owners of the rights to Elvis Presley's music sued the AI firm accusing it of using hundreds of the rock-and-roll star's songs to train its chatbot Claude.

World.title: Catholic bishops apologise for 'exploited' Trump meeting
World.content:
Two Catholic bishops in the US have said they regret meeting President Donald Trump at the White House, after images of them praying with him were released and prompted many to ask if they were making a political statement.

Photos and video of the 22 October meeting show a group of bishops standing around Trump at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office.

Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, one of those pictured, said he had believed the meeting was private and not "a political photo opportunity".

Trump and Pope Leo XIV have a contentious relationship, and some US bishops have criticised the administration's immigration policies. But Trump has typically enjoyed the support of Catholic voters.

In a statement posted online, Bishop William Joensen of Des Moines, Iowa, said the meeting was arranged by officials with the White House Faith Office to discuss issues including immigration, visas for international clergy and the "exploitation of vulnerable poor persons".

"In no way did any of us intend by our involvement to endorse any political party or any individual candidate," Joensen said.

"I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purposes," he added.

A video of the meeting was released by Margo Martin, a special assistant to the president and communications adviser who frequently shares behind-the-scenes images of Trump on social media.

Archbishop Grob said that after 90 minutes of meetings with officials, the religious leaders were ushered into the Oval Office to pray with Trump.

Grob said images of the meeting later caused concern among some of his congregants.

"I soon began receiving messages of serious concern over the possibility that I had inadvertently participated in a political event less than two weeks before a national election," he wrote.

"I also heard from some who felt wounded because of the ways they or their family have been harmed by the president's policies," he added.

Grob said none of the participants in the meeting gave permission for the public distribution or posting of video or photos of the event.

When contacted for comment by the BBC, the White House did not directly address questions regarding the meeting or subsequent comments by the two bishops.

"There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it," White House Spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said in a statement.

According to Pew Research Center, which analyses religion in the US, opinions of Trump's performance have slipped among all major religious groups. In a survey this month, 30% of all US Catholics said they approved of his job performance, compared to 47% when he returned to the White House in 2025.

That could have an effect on the 3 November midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress. More Catholics in the survey, 42%, said they preferred the Democrats running in their local House of Representatives races, where slightly less, 39% favoured Republicans.

During his second term, Trump has had a tense relationship with the head of the Catholic church, Pope Leo, as he has moved aggressively to remove people believed to be in the US illegally.

Nine days before the Oval Office meeting with the bishops took place, Bishop Brendon Cahill and Walter Kim, the president of the National Association of Evangelicals, issued a statement urging "Christian compassion and wisdom in the immigration debate".

They said the immigration clampdown has led to the "sowing of fear, the fracturing of families, the deprivation of due process, and the vilification of our neighbors."

The US Conference of Catholic Bishops also recently condemned the Trump administration's plans to livestream a military execution, which were later scrapped.

Both Vice-President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are Catholics who have visited the Vatican during Trump's second term.

A Midwestern member of the bishops' conference, Robert Barron of Minnesota, agreed to serve on the president's Religious Liberty Commission last year, as did former New York Archbishop Timothy Dolan.

World.title: US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan
World.content:
A US Marine has been indicted on suspicion of murdering and robbing a woman in Japan earlier this month in a case that has triggered protests, Japanese media reports.

Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who was stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was arrested on suspicion of killing Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in Naha, the capital of Okinawa.

Prosecutors have now indicted him for allegedly strangling Yagi with a telephone cord and then stealing her backpack and wallet on 3 October, media reports, citing the indictment document.

It wasreported Ballard had denied the allegations, but Asahi Shimbun and Kyodo News cited investigators saying he has made some statements suggesting involvement.

Security footage allegedly shows a man believed to be the suspect entering the hotel with the woman and leaving alone with her belongings.

Yagi's death has caused outrage in Japan, with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi describing the crime as "brutal and heinous".

Earlier this month, the Marine Corps said it was "actively cooperating with Japanese authorities, in response to allegations of serious criminal actions by a Marine" and extended condolences to the victim's family.

It is the latest case involving a US serviceman in Okinawa, which hosts the highest concentration of around 55,000 US soldiers stationed in Japan.

Previous criminal cases have sparked anger and protests, the largest of which took place in 1995, when tens of thousands took to the streets following the abduction, beating and rape of a 12-year-old girl.

In 2024 alone, there were four sexual assault cases involving US troops in Okinawa, including that of air force member Brennon Washington, who was given five years for the rape and kidnapping of an underage girl.

In 2025, US marine Lance Cpl Jamel Clayton was sentenced to seven years in prison for sexually assaulting a woman.

Okinawa Governor Genta Koja said the prefecture has repeatedly demanded that the US take action to prevent such incidents, and said he sees the alleged crime as a sign of a lack of discipline.

The prime minister said her government has registered a "strong" protest with the US and called for "strict disciplinary action against US military personnel and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents".

People in Japan have been voicing anger, with some 100 people protesting in both Naha and Tokyo earlier this month. Others took to social media expressing their outrage and demanding justice, with one user saying: "Enough is enough."

World.title: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile
World.content:
Venezuelan opposition leader MarÃ­a Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile.

"I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail.

In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President NicolÃ¡s Maduro.

The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy RodrÃ­guez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US.

Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands.

She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters have lined the route of her journey to the capital.

She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of the sunroof of a car as she entered Caracas late on Sunday night.

"Night of reunion in our Caracas. For the reunion of each family, for the Freedom of each political prisoner, for the Freedom of Venezuela," she wrote on X.

World.title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973
World.content:
Algeria is to send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since sending forces to Egypt during the Arab-Israeli war in 1973.

The deployment follows a visit to Algiers by Niger's defence minister, as the country seeks support against armed groups, some of which are linked to al-Qaeda or Islamic State.

Algeria has economic interests in Niger, including a planned gas pipeline that would carry Nigerian gas through Niger to Algeria. The troops are expected to protect energy facilities in northern Niger, near the Libyan border.

The deployment comes as the two neighbours rebuild ties after a diplomatic rift in 2025, when Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers.

Algeria's upper house of parliament held an emergency session on Sunday to vote on the proposed deployment. According to AFP news agency, 148 of the 174 senators voted in favour. It was later backed by the lower house of parliament.

However, the timing and number of soldiers to be deployed have not been announced.

The move would mark the first use of a 2020 constitutional provision allowing overseas military deployments and a significant shift in Algeria's long-standing policy against sending forces abroad.

"We are not sending our soldiers to wage war in Niger, but for a mission to secure economic infrastructure," Algerian senator Belkacem Boulghiti told reporters after the vote.

Algeria's state-owned energy company, Sonatrach, has also signed an agreement with Niger's petroleum ministry to explore for oil in the Kafra region. Two exploration wells are estimated to contain 168 million and 100 million barrels, respectively, Reuters reported.

Relations between Algeria and Niger have not always been smooth in recent years.

Algeria condemned the 2023 coup that ousted Niger's elected President, Mohamed Bazoum, and brought Gen Abdourahamane Tchiani to power.

Tensions rose again in 2025 after Algeria shot down a Malian drone near its border. Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers in solidarity with Mali, a close ally which is also under military rule.

Relations have since improved. Tchiani visited Algeria in February 2026, and in late August, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune sent fighter jets to Niger to help suppress a coup attempt and also donated four military helicopters.

World.title: UBA launches Group-Wide Climate Action Week to advance green finance and sustainability across Africa
World.content:
Africa’s Global Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has launched a Group-wide Climate Action Week to deepen climate awareness, promote responsible environmental practices and advance sustainable finance across its African and international operations.

The five-day campaign, running from 26 to 30 October 2026, is themed “Banking on Africa’s Climate Future” and reflects the Bank’s commitment to integrating environmental responsibility into its operations, customer engagement and financing solutions.

The initiative commenced with the deployment of waste segregation bins across UBA offices and measures to reduce the use of single-use plastics at the Bank’s head offices. These activities underscore UBA’s commitment to translating sustainability principles into practical actions within its workplace and across its wider ecosystem.

Throughout the week, UBA will disseminate educational content across its media and digital platforms to highlight the causes and consequences of climate change, including its impact on food prices, energy consumption and urban flooding. The campaign will also promote responsible plastic disposal, recycling and the critical role of financial institutions in financing clean energy, sustainable agriculture and other environmentally responsible businesses.

As part of the campaign’s community engagement component, UBA staff volunteers will participate in a Group-wide clean-up exercise on Saturday, 7 November in major cities across its markets. In Nigeria, the exercise will take place in Lagos, Kano and Port Harcourt, mobilising employees to contribute directly to cleaner and healthier communities.

UBA’s Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Oliver Alawuba, emphasised the importance of collective responsibility in addressing the growing impact of climate change.

“Climate change is no longer a distant environmental concern; it is increasingly shaping everyday life across Africa. We see its effects in rising food costs, increased energy demand and flooding that disrupts homes, businesses and livelihoods.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“At UBA, we believe that building a sustainable future requires collective action, beginning with the choices we make at work, at home and in our communities. Through this Climate Action Week, we are encouraging every member of the UBA Tribe, alongside our customers and other stakeholders, to embrace practical, sustainable habits and inspire others to do the same,” Alawuba said.

As part of its stakeholder engagement activities, UBA will sponsor Climate Convergence Week in Lagos on Friday, 30 October where the Bank will deliver a speaking session and participate in a panel discussion. The engagement will provide an opportunity to showcase UBA Green Finance, highlight the Bank’s sustainability initiatives and explore how financial institutions can support Africa’s transition to a more sustainable and climate-resilient economy.

Alawuba, noted that climate considerations were increasingly important to business resilience, risk management and long-term economic growth.

“Climate change presents significant risks to businesses, communities and economies. These risks can affect business continuity, operating costs and financial performance, making sustainability an increasingly important consideration for both businesses and the financial institutions that support them.

“Through UBA Green Finance, we seek to support eligible businesses investing in cleaner technologies and more sustainable operations. By helping customers explore financing solutions aligned with their needs, we can contribute to a more resilient private sector while unlocking opportunities for sustainable economic growth across Africa,” Alawuba further said.

In a step towards further strengthening its sustainability capabilities, UBA is set to join the Sustainability Professionals Institute of Nigeria (SPIN). The move is expected to deepen the Bank’s environmental, social and governance (ESG) expertise and support the continued professional development of its employees in sustainability-related disciplines.

The Climate Action Week forms part of UBA’s broader sustainability strategy, which integrates environmental responsibility into its Customer First philosophy through responsible business practices, employee engagement, community initiatives and green finance. By combining awareness, practical action and financing solutions, the Bank aims to encourage more sustainable choices while supporting businesses and communities in navigating the challenges and opportunities of climate change.

United Bank for Africa is one of Africa’s leading financial institutions and one of the largest employers in the continent’s financial sector, with approximately 25,000 employees and over 45 million customers globally. Operating in 20 African countries, as well as the United Kingdom, the United States of America, France and the United Arab Emirates, UBA provides retail, commercial and institutional banking services, advancing financial inclusion and leveraging technology to deliver innovative financial solutions.

World.title: Wazirin Tinubu: The influence and burden of Ibrahim Masari, By Umar Farouk Bala
World.content:
As a young Nigerian involved in TMS, the political culture I want to see is one grounded in evidence, respectful dialogue, accountability and measurable performance. If Masari’s political philosophy truly rests on results over rhetoric and honest engagement over inflated claims, then those principles deserve attention.

When the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation, widely known as Tinubu Must Stay (TMS), inaugurated its national leadership in Abuja, I accepted the responsibility of serving as its National Youth Leader. For me, it was more than an appointment. It raised a larger question about the political culture into which young Nigerians are being invited.

The Foundation’s structure includes a Board of Trustees, National Coordinators and six directorates focused on citizen engagement and evidence-based communication. It is chaired by Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, director-general of NITDA, while Dr Benjamin Obi Nwoye serves as national coordinator (South). Former Obidient coordinator, Marcel Ngogbehei, was appointed director-general, with Engineer Ibrahim Uba overseeing mobilisation and data management.

At its inauguration, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi emphasised simplifying government reforms, connecting data to everyday realities and confronting misinformation through technology-driven outreach, town halls and grassroots engagement. Benjamin Obi Nwoye similarly argued that many government interventions remain inadequately communicated.

Since then, one question has stayed with me: What values should define the politics young Nigerians inherit?

For me, that conversation leads naturally to Ibrahim Kabir Masari, special adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on political affairs and an increasingly influential figure in the president’s northern political engagement.

At the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on 14 October, Masari reportedly challenged party leaders to abandon inflated claims about votes and focus instead on measurable results at state, ward and polling unit levels. His instruction was strikingly simple: “Stop talking to yourselves and start talking to the people.” He also urged campaigners to explain the administration’s work in areas such as education, healthcare, economic reform and infrastructure; to acknowledge outstanding challenges; and avoid misinformation and hate speech.

That message matters because young Nigerians increasingly demand more than slogans. We want evidence. We want to be listened to. We want claims that can be measured against our own experiences.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Masari’s political journey also offers context for understanding his approach. His background includes service as national welfare secretary of the All Progressives Congress. In 2022, his name was submitted to INEC as Tinubu’s temporary running mate before Kashim Shettima emerged as the substantive vice presidential candidate. Masari stepped aside, saying the decision would give Tinubu greater flexibility to accommodate wider interests. Following the 2023 election, he was appointed senior special assistant on political affairs and was later elevated to special adviser on political affairs.

But perhaps the most symbolic indication of his growing political profile is the title increasingly associated with him: “Wazirin Tinubu.”

President Tinubu has publicly addressed Masari as “My Waziri.” In northern Nigerian usage, the traditional title carries connotations of counsel, responsibility and proximity to leadership. In this context, it is better understood as an expression of presidential trust than as a constitutional office.

Yet this is precisely where admiration should give way to scrutiny.

The significance of being Wazirin Tinubu cannot ultimately be measured by access to the president, titles or public recognition. It must be measured by what that access produces.

A trusted political adviser occupies one of the most sensitive spaces in government. He must understand the president’s priorities while remaining alert to the concerns of party members, elected representatives and citizens. He must know when to speak and when to listen, when to intervene and when restraint is more useful. Such a position demands discretion, political maturity and the capacity to reconcile competing interests. That are exactly what he does in promoting and protecting the reputation of President Tinubu.

For Masari, therefore, presidential confidence is both an advantage and a burden. Influence creates access, but access creates responsibility.

Recent reports have portrayed him as a significant convener in northern politics and one of the Ppresident’s closest political figures in the region. Such influence will naturally attract scrutiny, and it should. The closer any political adviser stands to presidential power, the more legitimate the public interest becomes in how that access is exercised.

This is why I find his emphasis on measurable performance important. If political leaders insist that campaign organisers should abandon exaggerated claims, communicate honestly and speak directly to citizens, then those principles should also become the standards against which their own influence is judged.

For those of us trying to encourage greater youth participation in public affairs, this distinction is crucial. Young Nigerians should not be introduced to a political culture in which proximity to power is itself an achievement. We should be introduced to one in which access creates an obligation to solve problems, listen to inconvenient truths and help government understand citizens beyond the atmosphere of political praise.

Nor should evidence-based politics mean communicating only achievements. Credibility also requires acknowledging shortcomings. A genuine conversation about government must have room for what worked, what did not work and what still needs correction. Otherwise, “evidence-based communication” risks becoming another sophisticated name for political marketing.

This is perhaps the heavier meaning behind the Waziri symbolism. Counsel is valuable when it tells power what it needs to hear, not merely what it wants to hear.

Ibrahim Kabir Masari today occupies a position from which political relationships can be built and disagreements mediated. His emergence as one of Tinubu’s prominent northern political interlocutors makes his choices consequential.

The ultimate question, therefore, is not how close Masari is to the president. It is what that closeness achieves for governance and political engagement.

As a young Nigerian involved in TMS, the political culture I want to see is one grounded in evidence, respectful dialogue, accountability and measurable performance. If Masari’s political philosophy truly rests on results over rhetoric and honest engagement over inflated claims, then those principles deserve attention.

But they also deserve consistent application. Because the greater the influence, the heavier the responsibility. And for Wazirin Tinubu, that may ultimately be the real burden of presidential trust which he has so far performed exceedingly well.

Umar Farouk Bala is national youth leader of Tinubu Must Stay (TMS).

World.title: Mutilated body of motorcyclist found as similar mystery killings rise
World.content:
The mutilated body of a motorcycle rider has been found along Longvel Road in Shendam Local Government Area of Plateau State, with his motorcycle reportedly stolen.

The killing, reported on Monday, bears similarities to previous attacks on motorcycle riders in other parts of the state and adds to a series of violent incidents involving farmers, travellers, vigilantes and traditional leaders in recent weeks.

The identity of the latest victim and the circumstances surrounding his death remained unclear as of Monday.

Henry Homsuk, a community resident, said residents woke up to the disturbing news.

“Sadly, someone would be killed and his motorcycle taken away,” Mr Homsuk said.

He said the incident had been reported to security operatives and urged them to investigate the killing, recover the stolen motorcycle and arrest those responsible.

Mr Homsuk also called for increased security along Longvel Road and other vulnerable areas in Shendam, saying residents should be able to carry out their lawful activities without fear.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Efforts to reach security operatives to confirm the incident were unsuccessful at the time of reporting.

The Shendam incident bears similarities to several reported killings of motorcycle riders in Plateau, where victims were allegedly attacked and their motorcycles stolen.

On 23 September, an unidentified person was killed along the Maikatako–Foloh Road in Butura District, Bokkos Local Government Area, in an incident suspected to have involved armed robbers who stole the victim’s motorcycle.

According to a report by security-focused publication Zagazola Makama, troops of Operation Enduring Peace responded to the incident at about 3:50 p.m. and found the victim’s body after the suspected assailants had fled.

The body was subsequently handed over to the police in Bokkos for further action, while security forces began efforts to track down the perpetrators.

Earlier, on 25 August, gunmen reportedly killed Danladi Idi Dakum while he was riding his motorcycle along the Matelem–Ndung Road in Tangur District, also in Bokkos.

A report by Zagazola Makama said troops deployed in the area responded to information about the attack and found Mr Dakum dead at the scene. Preliminary information suggested that the attackers might have been motorcycle snatchers.

In another incident, an unidentified motorcyclist was killed along the Nyong–Bodel Road in Bokkos on 4 September.

According to Zagazola Makama, troops responding to the attack found the victim’s body beside his motorcycle. The attackers had fled before the troops arrived.

The incidents have raised concerns about the safety of motorcycle riders and other road users, particularly on routes linking rural communities where residents depend on motorcycles for transportation and commercial activities.

However, there is no evidence that the killings are connected or that the same perpetrators were responsible.

The Shendam killing also recalls the discovery of a mutilated body behind Monday Market in Pankshin Local Government Area earlier in October.

Residents discovered the unidentified man’s body on 6 October and alerted security operatives.

A community source, Panshak Rogo, told journalists that some parts of the body, including the ears and nose, had been cut off.

The remains were evacuated to General Hospital, Pankshin, as residents urged anyone with information about missing relatives or the deceased’s identity to contact the police.

The discovery came two days after separate attacks in Jos South, Mangu and Riyom local government areas reportedly left at least 13 people dead.

In one of the attacks, nine passengers travelling towards Jos were killed when gunmen opened fire on their vehicle at Dungus in Jos South.

Two people were also reportedly killed in an attack on Vodni community in Pushit District, Mangu, while two others died in a separate attack at Tahoos in Riyom.

The killings heightened concerns about the security situation in the state, where communities have continued to report attacks on residents and travellers.

Violence has also affected traditional institutions and local security groups in Plateau.

On 12 October, gunmen attacked Jatau Samkwar, the Mishkaham Bokkos, at his residence in Daffo, Bokkos Local Government Area. He later died after receiving medical attention.

The Mwaghavul Traditional Council, Bokkos branch, announced his death, while community peace observers expressed concern over recurring attacks in the area.

Earlier in October, four vigilantes were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Shurum village in Dorowa Babuje District of Barkin Ladi Local Government Area.

Community sources said the victims were on duty protecting residents when the attackers struck.

On 24 October, a woman was reportedly killed and two other people injured while harvesting groundnuts at Gwom-Ajang in Foron District, Barkin Ladi.

The attack prompted community representatives to renew calls for improved security and protection for farmers.

The incidents have affected farmers, travellers, vigilantes, traditional leaders, and commercial transport operators, highlighting the risks residents face across several local government areas.

In Shendam, residents are urging security agencies to investigate the circumstances surrounding the rider’s death, recover the stolen motorcycle and bring the perpetrators to justice.

As of Monday, security operatives had not publicly confirmed the incident or announced any arrests.

World.title: Standard Chartered Nigeria wins International Banking Excellence Award at 2026 BAFI Awards
World.content:
Standard Chartered Bank Nigeria Limited has won the International Banking Excellence Award at the 2026 Banking and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards, organised by BusinessDay.

The award comes as Standard Chartered continues to draw on its international network and local market expertise to connect clients in Nigeria to opportunities across global markets.

Commenting on the recognition, Ayodeji Adelagun, Chief Executive Officer, Standard Chartered Bank Nigeria Limited, said:

“We are honoured to receive the International Banking Excellence Award. The recognition reflects the strength of our franchise, the commitment of our colleagues and the trust our clients continue to place in us.

Nigeria remains an important market for Standard Chartered. By combining deep local expertise with the breadth of our international network, we are able to connect clients to capital and opportunities across markets. We remain focused on supporting their ambitions, delivering innovative solutions and contributing to Nigeria’s economic growth.”

The recognition comes against the backdrop of Standard Chartered’s continued role in significant transactions supporting investment, trade and economic activity in Nigeria and across Africa.

In September 2026, Standard Chartered acted as Financial Adviser, Global Coordinator, Lead Arranger and Bookrunner for the US$1.1 billion financing supporting the IMA Gas Development Project, a joint venture between TotalEnergies and Amni International. The financing supports a major gas development project in Nigeria and demonstrates the Bank’s ability to combine international capital, structuring expertise and local market knowledge to support strategic infrastructure.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Earlier in the year, Standard Chartered and the International Finance Corporation announced a US$300 million risk-sharing facility aimed at strengthening supply chains and supporting business growth across eight African markets, including Nigeria. The facility supports companies in sectors including agriculture, healthcare and manufacturing, with Standard Chartered acting as originator and provider of supply chain and trade finance.

Standard Chartered NIgeria also received recognition in 2026 for its digital and transaction banking capabilities, including Best Data Analytics Initiative – Africa, Best API Initiative of the Year – Nigeria, Best Virtual Account Initiative – West Africa, and Outstanding Payments Solution for Corporates.

The International Banking Excellence Award adds to these recognitions and comes as Standard Chartered continues to combine its international network, local expertise and product capabilities to support clients in Nigeria and across its markets.

World.title: Tinubu pens tribute to veteran journalist Lade Bonuola at 80
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has paid tribute to veteran Nigerian journalist Lade Bonuola, who marked his 80th birthday last week.

In a statement he personally signed, the Nigerian leader said Mr Bonuola “reminds us of your enduring contributions to journalism, your professional excellence, and your commitment to developing Nigeria’s media industry.”

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Bonuola was honoured last week by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), which launched “Lade Bonuola: A Life in Print,” a collection of essays documenting the veteran journalist’s career and contributions to Nigerian journalism.

In his tribute, President Tinubu also celebrated Mr Bonuola’s contribution to journalism.

“At 80, you stand tall as one of Nigeria’s most respected figures in journalism, a man whose professional excellence, editorial courage, integrity, and commitment to the truth have left an enduring imprint on the nation’s media landscape,” the president wrote.

Read the president’s full statement below.

PRESIDENT TINUBU’S TRIBUTE TO LADE BONUOLA AT 80

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

I extend my warmest congratulations to Mr Oyinlade “Ladbone” Bonuola, veteran journalist, distinguished editor, and former Managing Director of The Guardian Newspaper, on his 80th birthday.

This milestone birthday reminds us of your enduring contributions to journalism, your professional excellence, and your commitment to developing Nigeria’s media industry.

Recognised by media peers and mentees as a craftsman par excellence, Bonuola began his career at the Daily Times in February 1971 as a trainee sub-editor, rose through the ranks, and joined The Guardian in 1982 as pioneer editor, later serving as Managing Director till 1999. He later co-founded the defunct Comet newspaper, where he served as Managing Director. He also served as Managing Director of Nigerian Compass.

At 80, you stand tall as one of Nigeria’s most respected figures in journalism, a man whose professional excellence, editorial courage, integrity, and commitment to the truth have left an enduring imprint on the nation’s media landscape.

As one of the 20th century’s exceptional editors, your contributions to Nigerian journalism remain indelible. Through decades of dedicated service, you helped shape the language of media reporting, uphold responsible journalism, and strengthen the media’s role as a vital pillar of democracy and a keeper of factual records. Your commitment to accuracy, fairness, integrity, and public accountability is a value that remains integral to the media’s responsibility to inform citizens, hold public institutions accountable, and strengthen democracy.

At the Daily Times, your weekly column, Caught Out, was a must-read for practising journalists, students and the public at large.

As former Managing Director of The Guardian and co-founder of The Comet, which later became The Nation newspaper, you demonstrated exceptional leadership, intellectual depth, and a keen understanding of the press’s power to build a just, informed, and progressive society.

Your career reflects a profound belief that journalism must serve the public interest, hold leaders accountable, and give citizens the information they need to make informed decisions. Your influence extends beyond the newsrooms you led.

As we celebrate this remarkable milestone with you, I acknowledge your legacy of professionalism, mentorship and service to our country. We celebrate your invaluable contributions to Nigeria’s democratic journey.

Your life and career remind us that journalism’s enduring value lies not merely in reporting events but in shaping ideas, nurturing informed citizens, and preserving the truth for future generations.

On behalf of my family, the Government, and the people of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, I wish you a happy 80th birthday and many more years of good health, peace, fulfilment, and continued service to our dear nation.

May your remarkable legacy continue to inspire generations of journalists and media practitioners.

Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR

President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces

Federal Republic of Nigeria

October 25, 2026

World.title: Ebola: Nigeria may declare outbreak over in December – Minister
World.content:
Nigeria may declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as 7 December if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, has said.

Mr Pate made this known in a statement shared on his official X handle on Monday, following the medical evacuation of Nigeria’s imported Ebola index patient to Switzerland earlier in the day.

He said the date remains provisional and would depend on the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and the World Health Organisation (WHO) validating the required 42-day countdown.

“Any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria,” Mr Pate said.

The minister said Nigeria’s immediate priorities are to continue monitoring all identified contacts, promptly investigate alerts, and strengthen preparedness across health facilities.

He said the response teams, working with the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), state health authorities and partners, remain focused on containing the disease and preventing community transmission.

Mr Pate urged Nigerians to “remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow updates” from the NCDC and Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Patient evacuated

Earlier on Monday, Mr Pate confirmed the medical evacuation of the imported Ebola patient and her husband to Switzerland.

The patient, who is Nigeria’s only confirmed Ebola case, had been receiving treatment in isolation in Abuja after testing positive for Bundibugyo virus disease, a form of Ebola.

WHO subsequently said Nigeria has no active Ebola cases following the evacuation.

The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said the patient was clinically stable and that Switzerland would assume responsibility for her continued medical management and follow-up for her husband, a contact.

Nigeria confirmed the imported case on 20 October, after the patient arrived in the country following international travel through Uganda.

World.title: Ebola: Plateau reopens isolation centres, steps up surveillance
World.content:
The Plateau State Government has reactivated isolation centres and intensified disease surveillance to prevent an Ebola outbreak in the state amid growing national concern over the disease.

The state Commissioner for Health, Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this during a press briefing in Jos on Monday.

Mr Ba’amlong said the state government had also directed its emergency preparedness team to assess safety measures at the airport and alert local government areas bordering neighbouring states.

Mr Ba’amlong urged residents to maintain proper hygiene, avoid contact with potentially infected persons and report suspected cases promptly to health authorities.

“Wash your hands regularly and avoid direct contact with the blood and body fluids of suspected infected persons,” the commissioner advised.

He said public cooperation was essential to preventing the spread of the disease, urging residents to remain vigilant and comply with public health guidelines.

The measures come as part of the state government’s broader efforts to strengthen its capacity to respond to public health emergencies.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ba’amlong said 10 resolutions were approved at the 12th Plateau State Council on Health meeting held last week to improve healthcare delivery and strengthen the state’s preparedness for disease outbreaks.

The resolutions include the establishment of a state health trust fund, improved disease surveillance, measures to address shortages of health workers and the creation of an emergency fund to respond to public health threats.

According to the commissioner, the initiatives are designed to improve the state’s ability to detect and respond to disease outbreaks while addressing challenges affecting healthcare delivery.

He reiterated the need for residents to follow public health guidance and promptly notify health authorities of suspected cases.

The state government did not disclose the number of isolation centres reactivated or provide details of the airport safety assessment during the briefing.

World.title: Africa Magic adds five dramas, thrillers to October lineup
World.content:
Africa Magic has unveiled five new original productions for October, featuring a mix of relationship drama, psychological suspense and indigenous-language stories across its entertainment channels.

The lineup includes Better Half and The Ten, along with Hausa drama Sirrin Amarya, Yoruba series Afobaje, and Igbo production Onu Ahia Nwanyi.

Better Half, executive produced by Rogba Arimoro, airs on Africa Magic Showcase, DStv channel 151 and GOtv channel 8, from Mondays to Wednesdays at 8:30 pm.

The series follows a relationship influencer who gets a reality television show to demonstrate her approach to love, only for secrets surrounding her fiancé’s family to threaten her beliefs about relationships.

It features Treasure Enagbare, Nnamdi Agbo, Demi Banwo and Tolu Asanu.

Mystery, suspense lead new productions

Another addition to the Showcase channel is The Ten, created by Lota Chukwu. The psychological thriller follows 10 kidnapping survivors who reunite for a vigil led by Matthew, a guilt-ridden head pastor played by Patrick Dibuah.

Their gathering takes a disturbing turn when one of the survivors is murdered. With a local festival leaving them trapped inside the church, the group must confront the possibility that the killer is among them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The series premiered on Thursday, 8 October, at 8:30 pm.

Speaking about the October slate, Atinuke Ngozi Babatunde, Executive Head, Content and Channels, West Africa, MultiChoice Nigeria, said the new productions reflect the range of genres, languages and perspectives Africa Magic seeks to bring to viewers.

“From the psychological tension of The Ten to the relationship dynamics at the heart of Better Half, alongside new titles in Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo, we are bringing depth to this month’s content lineup,” she said.

Babatunde added that the platform aims to create opportunities for local talent to develop their ideas while giving audiences more of the stories and genres they want to watch.

Indigenous dramas explore family secrets, betrayal

Three of the new productions premiered on Saturday, 10 October, across Africa Magic’s indigenous-language channels.

On Africa Magic Hausa, DStv channel 156, Sirrin Amarya, which translates to The Bride’s Secret, premiered at 8 pm.

The series centres on the disappearance of a young bride shortly before her wedding to one of Northern Nigeria’s influential businesspeople.

As the disappearance sparks a scandal involving both families, the businessman’s eldest son begins investigating and uncovers a decade-old conspiracy of betrayal, corruption, forbidden love, and revenge.

Executive produced and showrun by Chidozie Christian Ahaiwe, the series features Norah Ego as Zainab, the missing bride, alongside Aysha Usman Adam.

Meanwhile, Africa Magic Yoruba, DStv channel 157, introduced Afobaje, a drama set in the Ekinrinade Confederation that revisits a betrayal dating back 29 years.

The story follows kingmakers who overthrew the old monarchy, then turned against their spiritual guardian, Ajangbadi. His return alongside the last royal heir forces Crown Prince Aderounmu to investigate a series of deaths and uncover disturbing secrets about his lineage.

As the crisis threatens his land, the prince must choose between vengeance and wisdom. The series airs on Saturdays and Sundays at 7 pm and features Antar Laniyan, Aina Gold, Murphy Ray, Mr Paragaon and Abija, among others.

The third indigenous title, Onu Ahia Nwanyi, premiered on Africa Magic Igbo, DStv channel 159, at 7:30 pm.

Directed by Smart Ifeanyi Chukwu Abugu, the story follows Nkem, a young woman who enters a traditional bride contest in an attempt to escape a difficult family situation. However, she develops feelings for the man she is competing to marry, complicating the contest as hidden ambitions and family secrets emerge.

The unfolding events threaten to reshape the futures of several powerful families.

Expanding local storytelling

The October slate brings together contemporary relationship stories, psychological mysteries and dramas rooted in Nigerian cultures and traditions.

According to Africa Magic, the new productions build on its longstanding focus on showcasing Nigerian stories, developing local talent, and entertaining audiences across the continent.

The titles are available on their respective Africa Magic channels and can also be watched on DStv Stream.

World.title: Nigeria could declare Ebola outbreak over by Dec 7 – Pate
World.content:
Ali Pate, coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare

By Sola Ogundipe

Nigeria could declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as December 7, 2026, if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected following the medical evacuation of the country’s imported index patient.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, disclosed the provisional date on Monday as health authorities intensified contact tracing, investigated suspected cases and strengthened preparedness across health facilities to prevent further spread of the Bundibugyo virus disease.

Writing on his X handle, Pate said the 42-day countdown towards declaring the outbreak over would be subject to validation by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and the World Health Organisation (WHO), in line with established outbreak management criteria.

The development follows the evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient to Switzerland for further medical care, a move that has heightened attention on the country’s capacity to sustain containment measures and prevent community transmission.

According to Pate, “Following the imported Ebola index patient’s medical evacuation from Nigeria today, 26 October, our immediate priorities remain active monitoring of all identified contacts, prompt investigation of alerts and strengthened readiness across our health facilities.

“If no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, Nigeria could progress towards declaring this outbreak over under @WHO criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026. This date remains provisional, subject to @NCDCgov and WHO validating the 42-day countdown. Any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria,” Pate noted.

He said the proposed December 7 date is therefore not a final declaration that Nigeria is Ebola-free, but a conditional target that depends on the absence of further cases and the completion of the required surveillance period.

Further, he said, “Our teams, working with FCTA and state health authorities and our partners, remain focused on containment and preventing community transmission.

“I ask Nigerians to remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow regular updates from @NCDCgov and @Fmohnigeria.”

World.title: Alleged N582m fraud: Court fixes Nov 23 for trial of ex-NNPCL boss
World.content:
threatens to issue bench warrant

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA – A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Monday fixed November 23 for the arraignment of a former President of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Abuja, Mr. Olalekan Ogunbayo, over his alleged complicity in a ₦582 million fraud.

The court, presided over by Justice Lesley Wike, further threatened to issue a bench warrant against the defendant should he fail to appear before it to enter his plea to an eight-count charge preferred against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

After the case was called, the anti-graft agency drew the court’s attention to the absence of the defendant, who was billed for arraignment.

According to the prosecution, the development marked the third time the defendant had stayed away from court despite being aware of the case.

EFCC’s lawyer, R. U. Adagba, who informed the court that only the 2nd defendant in the matter, Abolade Nurudeen, was available for the proceedings, alleged that Ogunbayo had jumped the administrative bail granted him by the Commission.

He told the court that all efforts to locate the 1st defendant for service of the charge on him had been unsuccessful.

Consequently, he applied for a bench warrant to be issued to enable security agencies to arrest and produce the defendant in court for trial.

The prosecution counsel premised his application for the bench warrant on the provisions of Sections 35, 113 and 114 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015.

However, Mr. Innocent Adoo, who announced his appearance for the defendants, opposed the application.

He accused the EFCC of failing to properly serve a copy of the charge on the defendant.

The defence counsel argued that arraignment in a criminal trial cannot proceed without proper service of the charge on the defendant.

He submitted that a defendant must be informed of the allegations against him and given adequate opportunity to prepare his defence, adding that service could not be waived by any party.

Adoo told the court that Ogunbayo was still on administrative bail and was unaware of the scheduled arraignment.

He explained that the defence had used the information available to it to communicate with Ogunbayo, who was said to be in Warri, Delta State, and unable to secure a flight to Abuja for the sitting.

He therefore prayed the court for an adjournment to enable both defendants to appear and take their pleas in the interest of justice.

In his ruling, Justice Wike held that, in the interest of justice, the matter should be adjourned to enable the first defendant to appear for arraignment.

The judge, however, warned that the court would take the necessary steps if Ogunbayo failed to appear on the next adjourned date.

The charges against the defendants border on alleged criminal misappropriation, abuse of office, corrupt practices and obtaining money by false pretence.

The defendants were accused of involvement in the sale of the cooperative society’s property at Plot 50, Karsana North, Abuja.

The prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired in January 2024 to misappropriate proceeds from the transaction.

In one of the counts, the defendants were accused of dishonestly misappropriating ₦582 million realised from the sale of the property.

Ogunbayo was also accused of receiving ₦100 million, ₦10 million and ₦50 million through different bank accounts in connection with the transaction.

The prosecution further alleged that the 1st defendant received ₦180 million into an account belonging to his firm after representing that the property had been sold for ₦1 billion.

Both defendants were also accused of involvement in an alleged ₦160 million corrupt transaction.

World.title: Man swept away by flood while trying to rescue drowning teenager in Abia
World.content:
. Rescue team in desperate search for duo

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — In a heartbreaking twist of fate, a good Samaritan who risked his life to save a teenage girl from a flooded gutter in Aba, Abia State, was swept away by the same rushing water alongside the girl he tried to rescue.

The tragedy occurred on Sunday evening at Ukwu Mango, Faulks Road, during a downpour, leaving residents and sympathisers scrambling desperately to find the two missing persons.

The Samaritan reportedly slipped into the gutter while attempting to rescue the girl, only for the surging floodwater to sweep both of them away.

Residents immediately launched a frantic search, hoping to find the pair alive, but their efforts yielded no result, fuelling fears that the victims might have been carried into the Aba River.

The desperate search entered a new phase on Monday as the Abia State Fire Service and other government officials joined residents in combing the drainage channels for the missing duo.

Police personnel also arrived at the scene to control the crowd and maintain order as the rescue operation continued.

However, as of the time of filing this report, the victims remained missing, leaving their families and the community in agonising uncertainty over their fate.

When Vanguard contacted the Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO Maureen Chinaka, she promised to revert but had yet to do so at the time of filing this report.

Aba’s flat terrain makes the commercial city prone to flooding, particularly during heavy rainfall.

World.title: APC accuses ADC of owing staff salaries, urges Nigerians to reject Atiku
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of owing its workers more than 12 months’ salaries, urging Nigerians to reject the party, its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and its candidates in the next general elections.

The council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake, made the call in a statement, accusing the ADC National Working Committee, led by Senator David Mark as chairman and Rauf Aregbesola as secretary, of neglecting party workers despite their reliance on salaries for their daily needs.

Alake described the alleged failure to pay the workers as “wicked and reprehensible”, questioning the party’s capacity to manage the country’s affairs if it could not meet its obligations to its own employees.

“We find it unconscionable that a political party that has made many grandiose promises to hoodwink Nigerians owes its workers for more than 12 months,” he said.

“Owing staff who come to work every day and who rely on the salaries for their daily sustenance is wicked and reprehensible.”

The APC PCC spokesperson said the allegation exposed what he described as the insincerity of the ADC leadership, adding that Nigerians should reject the party at the polls.

“We have clearly stated that ADC leaders and their presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, do not mean well and can do nothing for our country,” Alake said.

He further alleged that Atiku had a history of failing to pay workers, claiming that employees of Gotel Communication and other businesses linked to the former vice-president had previously gone months without salaries and staged protests over unpaid wages and other benefits.

Alake also criticised Aregbesola’s record as governor of Osun State, alleging that his administration struggled to pay workers and pensioners during his eight-year tenure.

He said the state government had introduced quarter-salary and, at times, half-salary payments, while pensioners allegedly went unpaid for more than four years.

“We are therefore not surprised that ADC, harbouring birds of the same feather, cannot pay its workers’ salaries,” he said.

Alake urged Nigerians and workers to reject the ADC, Atiku and all candidates running on the party’s platform in the next general elections.

“We are sounding a warning to Nigerians and working people now: reject ADC. Reject Atiku Abubakar and reject all ADC candidates in the next general elections,” he said.

He argued that a party seeking to govern Nigeria should be able to demonstrate responsible management of its own affairs and the welfare of its workforce.

World.title: LAWMA begins expansion works at Olusosun dumpsite to boost waste evacuation
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, has initiated critical stabilisation and expansion works on tipping platforms E1 and E2 at the Olusosun dumpsite in Ojota.

​The upgrade, executed in partnership with Zoomlion Nigeria Limited, aims to expand platform capacity, allow more waste collection trucks to discharge simultaneously, and significantly enhance operational safety and speed.

​Speaking at the agency’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa on Monday, LAWMA Executive Director of Finance, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi, disclosed that construction on the site is progressing according to schedule.

​Adebiyi noted that the Olusosun upgrade is part of a broader infrastructure plan that includes ongoing improvements at other major dumping facilities, such as Solus III and Epe.

“Together, these upgrades are expected to strengthen the state’s overall waste evacuation network, dramatically reduce truck turnaround times, and improve service delivery across Lagos,” he stated.

​To minimise disruption during the construction phase, Adebiyi appealed for cooperation from Private Sector Participation, PSP operators, waste truck drivers, and other key industry stakeholders.

​The agency therefore reaffirmed its commitment to upgrading waste management infrastructure and maintaining a cleaner, healthier environment for all residents of Lagos State.

World.title: Arik Receivership: Court admits AMCON board resolutions
World.content:
court

By Henry Ojelu

The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Monday admitted certified board resolutions of the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON) as evidence in the ongoing criminal trial of its former Managing Director, Ahmed Kuru, and others over the receivership of Arik Air Limited.
