World.title: Drivers in Croatia Could Have to Pay 3X Higher Fines
World.content:
October the 26th, 2026 – Drivers in Croatia could need to pay 3X higher fines for driving offences as stricter traffic rules loom.

Last year, out of a total of 320,046 recorded speeding offences, cameras detected 200,137 of them, or 62 percent. Poslovni reports that a new Rulebook (Pravilnik) proposes a reduction of the so-called safety margin, which means that speed exceedances recorded by cameras will be tolerated significantly less than until now. Under the current rules, 3 km/h is deducted from the measured speed up to 50 km/h. For speeds from 51 to 100 km/h the tolerance is 10 km/h, and above 100 km/h 10 percent of the measured speed is deducted, rounded up to the higher value.

With the new rulebook, for example, a driver travelling at 86 km/h in a built-up area with a 50 km/h limit would be granted a tolerance of only five instead of the current 10 km/h. The relevant speed would be 81 km/h, which is 31 km/h above the limit, and the fine would amount to €390 instead of €130.

cameras record the vast majority of driving offences

If current trends continue, such a change would also significantly increase revenues from fines. Data from the Ministry of the Interior show that fixed speed monitoring devices recorded the majority of such offences. Last year, out of a total of 320,046 established speeding offences, cameras recorded 200,137 of them, or 62 percent. In the first eight months of this year, out of a total of 226,302 speeding offences, fixed devices recorded 145,129 of them, which is 64 percent. Data for last year also show that the most numerous were those exceeding 10 to 20 kilometres per hour above the permitted speed in built-up areas, with a total of 124,611 such cases.

more locations than cameras

Croatia currently has 206 fixed cameras that are distributed across a total of 807 locations. The Ministry of the Interior explains that the cameras are relocated at different time intervals, depending on the assessment of the competent police administration. The highest number of locations for installing cameras is in the area of the Split-Dalmatia Police Administration and the Zagreb Police Administration, with 86 in each, followed by the Međimurje Police Administration with 62 locations. The fewest are in the area of the Karlovac Police Administration, with 12, and the Požega-Slavonia Police Administration, where there are 13.

Although fixed cameras primarily serve to determine speeding, they can also record other traffic offences. “If, for example, the offence of using a mobile phone while driving, not wearing a seat belt or some other unlawful behaviour is visible on the recording, the driver or passenger can also be fined for such offences,” the Ministry of the Interior explains.

revenue from fines is increasing

The Ministry of the Interior states that it does not keep separate statistics on the amounts collected by type of offence, but collectively for all monetary fines under the Road Traffic Safety Act. Nevertheless, the Annual Report on the Execution of the State Budget shows that last year, 2025, €80.77 million was collected from fines for traffic and other offences under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of the Interior. That is €11.6 million more than in 2024.

World.title: Croatia is the Leading Charter Power, But Earns Less Than Greece – Why?
World.content:
October the 26th, 2026 – Croatia is the world’s leading charter power, yet it earns less than Greece does from the same sector. The big questions is why?

Croatia is the number one charter power in the world with nearly five thousand vessels in its fleet. In the first eight months of this year, more than 431 thousand charter guest arrivals and more than 2.7 million overnight stays were recorded. However, market saturation has led to charter prices, especially for sailing yachts, falling by 50 percent or more during the peak season. As Alenka Juricic Bukarica reports for Glas Istre, this is not only the case this year. At the same time, competition in other Mediterranean countries is growing, especially in Greece, which last year had just over 3,000 vessels in charter. That is still fewer than Croatia, but with a clear upward trend.

Rising operating costs in recent years have also significantly changed conditions on the Croatian charter market, particularly for smaller vessels, and have negatively affected the return on investment and, consequently, the interest of new investors. Croatia is no longer perceived as a cheap destination, and there has also been a change in the structure of guests: instead of professionals, charter is increasingly chosen by people who are not normally involved in sailing, which increases demand for skippers and hostesses. Ultimately, people from the industry say that in some cases better prices can be achieved on the market in September than in the peak season…

in typical croatian style, there’s a paradox…

The current situation on the Croatian charter market was recently analysed by Ani Trstenjak, head of the Yacht Rent charter agency, and Daniela Gračan from the Faculty of Tourism and Hospitality Management (FMTU) in Opatija. Nautical charter has become, they emphasise, an important part of the tourism economy. It has attracted domestic and foreign capital and created a business ecosystem that includes vessel owners, charter companies, marinas, service providers, intermediaries and numerous providers of supporting services.

However, the success that for decades was measured by fleet growth, number of bookings and total revenue is opening an increasingly uncomfortable question – can Croatian charter continue to grow in the same way without endangering its own profitability.

“Market analysis by the vessel rental platform Yacht-Rent.com for 2026 points to an interesting paradox. Namely, Croatian sailing yachts and catamarans are among the cheapest compared to competing markets, while at the same time achieving high occupancy. Croatian charter does not primarily suffer from a lack of demand, but from a structural problem where demand is increasingly difficult to convert into revenue and profit. At the same time, it is clear that revenue is necessary to cover operating costs, financing, maintenance, depreciation and fleet renewal,” Trstenjak explained.

She clarified that Yacht-Rent’s market analysis for this year compares prices and bookings of vessels across six Mediterranean markets. It covers the operating season from 1 April to 2 November 2026, and expresses prices per person (berth) per week so that different vessel sizes can be compared on a comparable basis. According to that analysis, Croatia has the lowest average weekly price per berth among the compared markets for both sailing yachts and catamarans.

an exceptionally demanding market

Specifically speaking, sailing yachts in Croatia achieve an average weekly price per berth of €355, compared to €454 in Greece and €494 in Turkey. The price in Croatia is 22 percent lower than for a sailing yacht in Greece and 28 percent lower than in Turkey. At the same time, Croatian sailing yachts have an average of 19.4 booked weeks, slightly more than 19 weeks in Greece and significantly more than 17 weeks in Turkey. The estimated gross seasonal revenue per berth in Croatia amounts to €6,887, compared to €8,626 in Greece and €8,398 in Turkey.

The situation with catamarans is similar to that of sailing yachts. The average price of €706 per berth per week in Croatia is 16 percent lower than in Greece and 14 percent lower than in Turkey. Catamarans in Croatia are on average booked for 18.8 weeks during the season, which is close to 19.2 weeks in Greece, but significantly more than 15.4 weeks in Turkey. Despite this, the estimated gross seasonal revenue per berth in Croatia amounts to €13,273, while in Greece it reaches €16,147. Turkey achieves €12,659 in seasonal revenue per vessel.

“These data shows that Greece in the observed sample manages to combine high utilisation with a higher price. Croatia, on the other hand, achieves high capacity utilisation with a significantly lower price,” pointed out the head of the Yacht Rent agency. Adding that Croatian charter today operates on a highly competitive Mediterranean market, she also recalled that a guest can today easily compare prices, year of construction, equipment and capacity of vessels, rental conditions, additional costs and available destinations. And when vessels are very similar to each other, price becomes one of the most important decision criteria. However, she stresses, price is not the cause of the crisis, but its symptom.

higher and higher costs

Although not all segments of charter are equally price-sensitive, Trstenjak explains that luxury crewed vessels, differentiated service, special routes and a top customer experience can have greater pricing power. A standard sailing yacht comparable to dozens of other vessels at the same destination has significantly less room to raise its price independently. Charter companies today face high costs for berths, servicing, spare parts, insurance, labour, cleaning, administration, sales and distribution. Financing, depreciation and the need for fleet renewal, berth prices and insurance also play a significant role. All of this leads charter firms to accept a lower price in order to still rent out the vessel. In the short term such a decision can be rational, our interlocutor says, if the booking covers the additional costs of the rental and contributes to covering fixed costs. However, in the medium or long term, such a decision can be disastrous.

“When discounts become a permanent way of doing business, a serious problem arises that Croatian charter has been facing since 2023. Revenue may cover part of the costs, but it very likely no longer leaves enough funds for equipment renewal, major services, vessel replacement and return on capital. A company can therefore have high turnover, positive operating profit and at the same time an insufficient return on the capital invested in charter management. Every charter company wants to have enough vessels to attract guests, expand its offer and increase turnover.

But when a large number of investors make similar decisions, total supply can grow faster than demand. The number of available vessels increases, but the number of guests and attractive periods does not necessarily grow at the same speed. Therefore, an individual discount may be rational, but collective reliance on discounts can reduce the profitability of the entire market because supply does not adjust quickly enough,” Trstenjak says.

capital investment

She also addressed the problem of charter management, i.e. the fact that many Croatian citizens or companies, as well as foreigners, have in recent years seen the purchase of a sailing yacht or catamaran as a profitable form of capital investment. For the vessel buyer, the charter company handles the rental business, while the owner can use it for part of the year and collects income from the rental. Maintenance costs of the boat are borne by the owner. In such a model, the vessel owner expects a return on capital, the charter company wants to achieve the highest possible margin, while the guest wants the best price-quality ratio.

“If the vessel was purchased with excessively high expectations regarding rental price and number of booked weeks, a change in market conditions can seriously endanger the profitability of the investment. The owner expects a return, while the charter company has to choose between a lower price and the risk of unfilled periods,” our interlocutor warned. She concludes that the Croatian charter market has matured and that it is actually very important to make better use of the season and develop the offer outside the main summer months. At the same time, marinas, anchorages and the preservation of the sea must not be neglected, because it is precisely the quality of the destination that attracts guests. “The future of the charter sector does not depend only on further growth, but on how sustainable and profitable that growth will be,” concluded Ani Trstenjak.

a charter loss of €35 million…

The HUP Nautical Sector Association presented the Blue Book of Croatian Nautics and an initiative for the establishment of a National Nautical Council that should define a common development vision until 2040 at the Biograd Boat Show.

According to HUP’s analysis, entrepreneurs in nautics last year achieved €2.8 billion in business revenue and €1 billion in export revenue, employing 18,323 people. Business revenues rose 9.4 percent and exports 14.8 percent compared to the previous year. The analysis is based on HUP’s register of more than 3,200 mapped economic entities in activities related to nautics. In the period from 2021 to 2025, exports grew 70.8 percent, from €597.1 million to more than €1 billion. The share of gross investments in fixed assets in business revenues simultaneously increased from 11.7 to 18 percent. In the Blue Book, however, a warning was issued about pressure on the profitability of charter, which last year recorded a net loss of €34.7 million. “For the further growth of Croatian nautics, safer investment conditions, faster procedures and the availability of qualified workers are needed.

The Blue Book shows that revenue per employee in the sector from 2021 to 2025 rose by 43 percent, from €108.5 thousand to €155.1 thousand, which confirms the potential for creating greater added value. We want more design, production and servicing to take place in Croatia and for a larger part of the value created to remain in the domestic economy, while preserving the sea and the coast,” said Irena Weber, Director General of HUP. Luciano Beg, president of the HUP Nautical Sector Association, also pointed out that in addition to counting berths and overnight stays, the success of nautics should be measured by the production of vessels and equipment, overhauls, innovations, exports and quality jobs, and that this requires a long-term vision and better coordination between the economy, state institutions and the scientific community.

World.title: “I Won’t Shoot My Own People” – How Perišin Escaped the JNA in a MiG
World.content:
October the 26th, 2026 – Rudolf Perešin refused to shoot at his own people, instead escaping the JNA and flying to Austria.

On the 25th of October 1991, pilot Rudolf Perešin, then a member of the Yugoslav Air Force, defected in a Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21 fighter from the JNA base in Bihać to Klagenfurt, Austria. Index writes that with that act, he became one of the symbols of resistance and the struggle for Croatia’s independence. After landing in Austria, the public forever remembered his statement: “I am a Croat and I won’t shoot at my own people.”

His MiG-21 was never returned to the Yugoslav People’s Army. It remained in Austria, and Perešin soon joined the Croatian Army and the Croatian Air Force. He became commander of the 1st Fighter Squadron and took part in numerous combat missions during the Homeland War.

During the military-police operation Flash, which took place on the 2nd of May 1995, Perešin’s aircraft was hit in the sky above western Slavonia. He managed to eject, but landed in territory controlled by enemy forces and was killed. His remains were found only two years later – on the 4th of August 1997. He was buried with full military honours on 15 September 1997 at Mirogoj Cemetery in Zagreb. Rudolf Perešin has remained a lasting symbol of courage, patriotism and professional honour of Croatian pilots. His legendary MiG-21 is today exhibited in Zagreb as a reminder of one of the most important moments in the history of the Croatian Air Force.

The aircraft in which Perišin defected was displayed in a museum in Klagenfurt until 2019, when it was returned to Croatia.

World.title: He Survived a Shipwreck and Built a Church – 900 Years Later, Croatia Officially Protected it
World.content:
October the 25th, 2026 – A merchant surviving a shipwreck and then building a church in gratitude that Croatia officially chose to protect almost 1,000 years later is the story behind a construction on an island few know about.

It’s believed that the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian (Crvka sv. Kuzme i Damjana) on the island of Ugljan dates from the 11th or 12th century. It is located in a peaceful cove, right by the sea, not far from the hamlet of Guduće. Olive groves, dense pine forests, beautiful coves, old fishing villages, crystal-clear sea and views of the Zadar archipelago are what await visitors to Ugljan.

As Ivana Vasarevic writes for Putni Kofer, it’s widely known as one of Croatia’s greenest islands, which also carries the flattering nickname “the garden of Zadar.” It’s just 22 kilometres long, has a little over 5,600 inhabitants, is separated from the mainland by the Zadar Channel, and is connected to the neighbouring island of Pašman by a bridge across the Ždrelac passage. Among Ugljan’s main attractions is the fortress of St. Michael above Preko; nearby is also the islet of Galevac, known for its Franciscan monastery, while in Muline you can visit the remains of an ancient oil mill where the Liburnian olive oil was once produced.

TODAY IT IS CONSIDERED THE OLDEST PRESERVED CHURCH IN THE SETTLEMENT OF UGLJAN

The island’s special charm comes from its small stone churches. One of them was recently declared a cultural asset by the Ministry of Culture and Media of the Republic of Croatia. It is the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian, located in Ljokine Cove, not far from the hamlet of Guduće, on the southwestern side of the island. This modest stone building stands right on the shore and is the oldest preserved church in the settlement of Ugljan: it is believed to date from the 11th or 12th century.

Besides its exceptional historical value, the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian is also interesting because of the unusual legend that has accompanied it for centuries. According to the story, a merchant and sailor named Toricella was shipwrecked in the waters around Ugljan. He managed to save himself and swim to the shore in Ljokine Cove, and on that spot he decided to build a votive church. He dedicated it to Saints Cosmas and Damian, early Christian martyrs and physicians, in gratitude for his rescue.

THE ROOF OF THE SIMPLE LITTLE CHURCH WAS COVERED WITH BROKEN STONE SLABS

Although the shipwreck story cannot be historically confirmed, the name Toricella also appears in old documents. The little church is first mentioned on 6 August 1512 in the will of F. Toricella from Bergamo in Italy. In it he stipulated that a piece of land should be given for use to the priest who celebrates a sung Mass in the little church on the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian. According to the interpretation of don Marko Dokoza, a priest who for years led tours of Ugljan’s little churches as part of Open Doors Days, Toricella was only later identified with the seafarer from the shipwreck legend.

The original church was a very simple, square stone building, 4.8 metres long and 2.8 metres wide. Its walls were about 80 centimetres thick, and at the rear it had a lowered semicircular apse. The roof was covered with broken stone slabs, and there were two small windows in the side walls. The interior had a half-barrel vault, while the simple architectural details reflected the modesty and age of the building.

PAINTINGS DEPICTING SAINTS COSMAS AND DAMIAN AND THE BLESSED VIRGIN MARY WITH THE CHILD

At the beginning of the 20th century the little church was significantly enlarged. A new nave, ten metres long and 3.8 metres wide, intended for gatherings of the faithful, was added to its front part. Today its interior contains an altar, pews and paintings depicting Saints Cosmas and Damian as well as the Blessed Virgin Mary with the Child. On the façade a small round window stands out, and above it a stone bell-gable with a bell made in the workshop of Jakov Cukrov in Split.

Saints Cosmas and Damian, to whom the church is dedicated, were twin brothers and physicians who helped the sick free of charge. Their feast day is celebrated on the 26th of September. For centuries that date held special significance for the inhabitants of Ugljan: according to records in the parish chronicle, numerous pilgrims from all the settlements on the island, as well as from the neighbouring areas, used to come to the little church on that day.

IN THE NEARBY HAMLET OF GUDUĆE YOU CAN ALSO SEE A UNIQUE MOSAIC BENCH

The tradition, of course, lives on today. Mass is still celebrated in the little church, during which blessings are invoked upon Ugljan sailors and ships all over the world. Thus this small place of worship has remained connected with the sea and seafarers, just as in the legend of its origin. The Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian on the island of Ugljan is also interesting as an excursion destination.

It is located in a peaceful cove, and a gravel road through a pine forest leads to it. In the nearby hamlet of Guduće you can also see an unusual mosaic bench created back in 2019 by the retired Božica Kliman, known as Boška. On its front side is a depiction of the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian itself, along with a magical sunset, a squid and a lighthouse — colourful reminders of the islanders’ unbreakable connection with the sea and fishing.

World.title: The 3,500 Year Old Settlement Found Near Split
World.content:
October the 25th, 2026 – There is a fascinating 3,500 year old settlement in the suburbs of Split, with archaeologists coming upon the remains of houses, ovens and ancient graves.

Split is well known as the second largest city in Croatia and one of the best-known tourist destinations. It boasts an exceptionally long and proud history, but many don’t know that in its suburbs lies a settlement that is even older than this Dalmatian gem. As Lana Mindoljevic writes for Putni Kofer, over more recent years, archaeologists visiting the settlement of Stobreč have been discovering remains of life from the Bronze Age, long before the arrival of the Greeks and the Romans. Stobreč is formally a suburban settlement of Split and a popular tourist area, but it has its own exciting history that many people simply overlook.

the remains of an ancient epetium

Stobreč has long been known to archaeologists as the site of ancient Epetium, or Epetion. However, extensive protective research that began back in 2024, the largest so far conducted at this site, has also opened a much older chapter of its history. According to the information available so far, the earliest finds date approximately to 1500 BC, and detailed processing of the material is still ongoing.

over 10,000 fragments have been found

In a scientific paper written by Marina Ugarković and Niko Romac, published on the Hrčak website, parts of Hellenistic defensive walls and a tower, a Roman road and drainage system, and late antique buildings are described. Among these layers, the remains of an earlier prehistoric settlement have for the first time been unequivocally confirmed. Already in the research covered by that paper, more than 100,000 fragments of objects and other movable finds from different periods were documented. The soil under Stobreč has proven to be a vast archive of life that changed and built upon itself here for centuries.

ancient homes and grave sites

Archaeologist Niko Romac also described finds of ovens, possibly intended for food preparation, and complete ceramic vessels: trays, cups and jugs. Precisely such objects bring the ancient inhabitants of Stobreč closer to us. Someone made them, took them in their hands and used them in everyday life. Based on traces of burning and the arrangement of the remains, researchers assume that the house was destroyed by fire. Among the particularly sensitive finds, the grave of a newborn in its floor was also recorded.

an archaeological park is being considered

These remarkable discoveries have also opened the question of the future of the very special site. According to the response of the Ministry of Culture and Media, a zone of approximately 3,000 square metres is currently being planned for the presentation of the archaeological heritage. On an additional around 2,500 square metres construction is possible, but it depends on the results of further research. The sensitive Bronze Age finds require special protection. The Ministry states that the ovens and the find interpreted as a threshing floor should be moved to the Archaeological Museum in Split, while the appearance of the settlement could be presented with three-dimensional models and virtual reconstructions. An archaeological park currently exists only as an idea, and time will show whether it will be realised.

Stobreč is located on a peninsula east of Split, near the mouth of the Žrnovnica. In the central part of the place there are sandy and pebble beaches, while towards the southwest the coast becomes rockier. Because of the beautiful beaches and the proximity of Split it is a popular summer destination, and the proximity of Perun and Mosor also opens possibilities for trips into nature. Interestingly, even the name of Stobreč itself preserves the memory of its long past. As the Croatian Encyclopaedia notes, archaeologist Frane Bulić etymologically linked the present-day name of the place with the name of Saint Lawrence, i.e. the Roman martyr Laurentius, to whom the local early Christian basilica was dedicated. In its apse a small church of Saint Lawrence was later arranged, later dedicated to Our Lady of Carmel. Along with the preserved remains of the ancient walls, this is another reminder that in Stobreč different periods of history can be encountered during a completely ordinary walk.

World.title: Croatia is Introducing a New Digital Customs System
World.content:
October the 25th, 2026 – Croatia is set to introduce a brand new digital customs system as of November the 1st this year, with the hope of making crossing the border more efficient.

As of the 1st of November 2026, the Customs Administration is introducing a new digital service called eObračun of customs duties in passenger traffic (eODPP). Index reports that this brand new service is intended for passengers who bring goods into Croatia, i.e. the EU, on which import duties are payable, and its aim is to facilitate and speed up border crossing.

how it works…

Via the new application, passengers will be able to check in advance whether there is an obligation to pay duties on the goods they are bringing in their personal luggage. The service also enables them to declare goods whose value or quantity exceeds the permitted limits and to pay online the customs duties and taxes calculated on the basis of the declaration. Goods can be declared up to five days, i.e. 120 hours, before the planned arrival at one of the international border crossings within the territory of Croatia.

Upon arrival at the border, a customs officer will check the declaration and the goods in a short procedure. If no irregularities are found, the import procedure will be quickly completed. The Customs Administration states that the application is designed to be intuitive, and the data-entry procedure for calculating duties has five steps.

no registration required

The brand new Croatian digital customs service will be available to all passengers entering the EU via Croatian road, railway, air and maritime border crossings. No registration is required to use it. The system is adapted for computers, smartphones and tablets, and will be available from the 1st of November 2026 here.

World.title: Croatia is at Back of EU When it Comes to Electric Car Purchases
World.content:
October the 25th, 2026 – Despite the global climb in people buying electric vehicles, Croatia ranked at the very back of the EU when it comes to electric car purchases.

The share of fully electric cars among new cars is growing around the world, and in many countries it has reached record levels. Vedran Salvia reports for Index that this is clearly shown by the latest data from the international energy organisation Ember, which analysed car sales on global markets. Croatia is significantly lagging behind the other EU countries.

croatia is at the very back of the eu

According to Ember’s analysis, which tracks the share of fully electric cars (BEVs) among newly registered cars, Croatia recorded its own record during 2026, but despite that remained in last place in the European Union. From March to August such cars accounted for around 4.3 percent of all new registrations in Croatia. The data are based on rolling six-month periods because this presentation allows clearer tracking of trends.

The research covered 56 countries, while 49 of them are shown on the interactive chart, i.e. only those that achieved record shares during 2026. The difference between Croatia and the European leaders is extremely large. In Norway, which is not a member of the European Union, the share of fully electric cars reached as much as 97.8 percent, in Denmark 79.8 percent, in Finland 49.7 percent, in the Netherlands 42.8 percent and in Sweden 40.8 percent. The European Union average was 22.5 percent, more than five times higher than in Croatia. As for the EU members that are not shown on the chart, these are Poland and Romania, which did not achieve record shares of electric cars during 2026. However, both are ahead of Croatia. From March to August the share of fully electric cars among new registrations was 4.8 percent in Poland and 7.4 percent in Romania.

why is croatia lagging so much?

One of the reasons for the weaker sales of electric cars across Croatia could be their high price, especially in relation to average local purchasing power. That Croatian buyers are largely turning to used vehicles is also shown by data from the Croatian Vehicle Centre, according to which more used cars are imported into Croatia than new ones are registered, while the average age of passenger cars is more than 13 years. The European Commission in its 2026 report on Croatia also warns of the high costs of public charging of electric vehicles, problems with different charging systems and limited possibilities for home charging, especially for citizens who live in apartment buildings.

State incentives also play an important role; they are not awarded continuously but through occasional tenders. Available funds can sometimes be used up in just a few hours. Thus in 2024 citizens reserved all 15 million euros earmarked for subsidies in only four hours, after which the Environmental Protection Fund closed the tender. Such a system makes purchase planning more difficult because citizens cannot count on the constant availability of incentives.

large market differences

There are also significant differences among the large European markets. In France the share of fully electric cars was 30.6 percent, in Germany 27.5 percent and in Italy 8.3 percent. Germany and France have in recent years been moving towards an ever higher share of electric cars, while their penetration in Italy is considerably slower. Nevertheless, the Italian market is also recording growth, especially during 2026. Looking at absolute numbers, China is by far the world’s largest market for electric cars by the number of vehicles sold and is in a category of its own. According to Ember’s data, from January to August 2026 almost 4.46 million fully electric cars were registered there, which is almost half of the total of 9.33 million registered worldwide. In the EU in the same period around 1.65 million such cars were registered.

electric cars are conquering even emerging markets

The data show that the growth in the share of electric cars is no longer limited to developed European countries and China. Among the countries with high shares, Uruguay stands out with 40.2 percent, while in Thailand the share reached 28.8 percent and in Indonesia 24.2 percent. “Strong growth outside the USA and China was key to the continued growth in electric vehicle sales. Excluding the USA and China, global BEV sales rose by an estimated 45% in the period from January to August 2026 compared with the same period of the previous year,” the research states. At the same time, electric cars in some large countries still occupy a relatively small part of the market. In India their share is 7.4 percent, in Japan 3.3 percent and in Mexico only 2.1 percent.

the usa didn’t even make it on the chart

Ember particularly highlights the example of the United States of America, which did not even make it among the 49 countries with record shares of electric cars shown on the chart. After last year’s abolition of federal support for electric vehicles, their share among new vehicles fell to only six percent in the first eight months of 2026. Looking at everything in absolute numbers of electric cars sold the USA stands considerably better. From January to August around 640 thousand such vehicles were registered there, which puts it in second place in the world, immediately behind China. However, the American car market is so large that electric cars still make up a small part of total sales. According to Ember’s analysis, as many as 49 of the 56 observed countries now have a higher share of electric cars than the USA, and during this year alone 15 countries overtook it, among them Brazil, India, Italy, Malaysia and New Zealand.

electric cars and energy security

Ember emphasises in its analysis that the spread of electric cars affects not only the car market but also the energy security of states. According to the organisation’s estimates, electric cars in oil-importing countries from March to August this year replaced oil consumption worth around 20 billion dollars.

The authors of the research conclude that the electrification of transport can reduce states’ exposure to disruptions on the oil market and sudden changes in fuel prices. “Countries that invested in electric cars before this crisis are now better protected, and their example is being followed by an increasing number of other countries. Every electric car on the road reduces exposure to volatile oil markets, and as their number grows, so does protection against future supply disruptions,” the research states.

World.title: Iraqis mark 7th anniversary of 2019 Tishreen Uprising
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Thousands of Iraqis gathered on Sunday in Baghdad’s Tahrir Square and southern provinces to mark the seventh anniversary of the 2019 Tishreen (October) Uprising.

Major centers, including Baghdad, Najaf, Nasiriyah, and Basra saw a resurgence of protests, with activists bringing national and local problems back to the scene.

Activists are still calling for justice and the punishment of those who murdered more than 600 demonstrators during the initial crackdowns in 2019.

Protesters explicitly voiced their opposition to regional external influence, shouting anti-Iranian chants and demanding an end to foreign interference in Iraqi politics.

The muhasasa system, a sectarian political quota system that divides political posts and state resources among controlling parties, is still being opposed by protesters.

Protesters demanded that all weapons be restricted to state authority, targeting the power of Iranian-backed armed militias operating in the country.

Popular infrastructure failure, significant young unemployment, and widespread government corruption continue to be major sources of public frustration.

Iraqi security officials deployed forces to safeguard important squares and public areas ahead of the anniversary, putting soldiers in Baghdad on high alert to prevent possible escalations.

The 2019 Tishreen Uprising was the largest, longest-lasting, and most significant social movement in Iraq’s post-2003 history.

The nonviolent movement, which was mostly spearheaded by frustrated youth, broke out in Baghdad and southern Iraq on October 1, 2019, demanding a complete reform of the country’s political system.

World.title: Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe
World.content:
Manchester – Winless in eight games and hovering just above the Premier League relegation zone, struggling Manchester United are facing the prospect of yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick likely to pay the price.

The former United midfielder was warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel after his team’s chastening 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise.

Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson.

An emotional Carrick denied his lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday was a goodbye as he struggles to come to terms with his team’s precipitous decline.

“I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way,” he said.

Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job.

The United boss, who won multiple titles in the club’s golden era under Ferguson, was the seventh permanent appointment since the Scot retired.

David Moyes was proven in the Premier League, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho had stellar records and Erik ten Hag and Amorim were seen as rising stars of coaching.

– Sentimental choice –

Carrick is in the same category as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge for three years from 2018 — a sentimental choice as a former player who played a major role in the club’s glory years under Ferguson.

“The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular,” former United captain Gary Neville told Sky Sports.

“But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.”

The problems at the club, as Neville points out, go far beyond the dugout.

Despite fierce, ongoing protests from fans, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts.

Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have been dashed.

Ratcliffe has overseen cost-cutting measures including widespread redundancies and ticket hikes but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.47 billion).

United, who for years bullied their rivals in the transfer market, lost out on the biggest names as they targeted a summer midfield rebuild, with Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes all choosing other clubs.

United instead recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — none of whom have made a strong impression — for combined fees of about £150 million.

Significant rifts have emerged in recent weeks.

Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox for not doing more to strengthen Carrick’s squad.

Last week captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 humbling by Champions League debutants Como.

Carrick is expected to take the blame, but the route back to the top for one of the world’s biggest clubs appears tougher than ever.

“It can’t just be the manager again. There has got to be consequences above that. You can’t keep letting the people pick the manager who keep getting it wrong,” said Neville.

“It’s years now without a Premier League title. That will be another five or 10 before you know it because there are other clubs set up for success and Manchester United aren’t.”

World.title: Kane tipped to beat Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d’Or glory
World.content:
London – Harry Kane is favourite to become England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years when the award is presented in London on Monday, but he faces stiff competition from La Liga pair Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas is the clear frontrunner to win the women’s prize for a third time, with Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign set to come to an end after an injury-hit spell.

The ceremony to decide the world’s best male and female footballers is being held in London for the first time — 70 years after England winger Stanley Matthews was presented with the inaugural award.

Bayern Munich and England forward Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.

But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and at the World Cup in the United States mean a triumph for Kane at the London Palladium is far from certain.

“I’d love to be able to achieve something like that. It would be a massive milestone in my career,” said the 33-year-old former Tottenham forward.

“I think my wife would prefer to know and my family… it’s very stressful for everyone,” added the England captain.

Only four players from England have won the Ballon d’Or. Michael Owen was the last to triumph in 2001, following in the footsteps of Matthews, Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany praised Kane’s focus on his team, saying: “What made Harry happy the most in recent years is that he finally won his first team trophies here.

“Now if he can crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be deserved for the way he plays for the team.”

– ‘I deserve it’ –

Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembele last year and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d’Or winner one day.

However, a hamstring injury ended his club season early and he failed to show his most irresistable form during Spain’s World Cup triumph, which was built on impressive teamwork.

But that has not diminished his confidence ahead of the ceremony.

“For me, Mbappe and me, we’re the two best players in the world,” Yamal said last month.

“I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I’ve won.”

Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France.

The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies.

His 10 World Cup goals in North America made him the top goalscorer in the competition’s history, on 22.

“Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out,” said Mbappe.

“Who am I voting for? Myself.”

The Ballon d’Or was established by the magazine France Football, with the first award given to Matthews in 1956.

One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA’s rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist.

Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners as well as increasing a player’s overall market value.

Putellas, winner of the women’s award in 2021 and 2022, was a member of the Barcelona side that regained the Champions League last season before moving to London City Lionesses.

Her former Barcelona team-mate, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, is Putellas’s main challenger after scoring 11 Champions League goals in Barca’s latest triumph.

World.title: Iraqi PM makes official visit to Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived on Monday in the Jordanian capital, Amman, for his first official visit to the neighboring country since taking office.

King Abdullah II received Al-Zaidi at Amman Civil Airport. Leading a high-level delegation, al-Zaidi’s visit comes in response to an invitation from the Jordanian king.

Amid ongoing tensions, the two leaders are meeting to discuss security concerns in the region, joint development initiatives, and economic cooperation.

The two countries are expected to sign several memoranda of understanding (MoUs) to advance joint economic initiatives.

Al-Zaidi and King Abdullah II are expected to discuss approaches to strengthen bilateral relations, as well as mechanisms for cooperation to address various challenges.

Furthermore, the two leaders will chair an expanded meeting between the delegations of the two countries and oversee the signing of several memoranda of understanding aimed at fostering cooperation, integration, and economic partnership, while safeguarding mutual interests.

The trip reflects a shared vision between Baghdad and Amman to expand regional dialogue and promote solutions that ensure long-term stability across the Middle East.

World.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia before high-stakes talks in Tehran
World.content:
Riyadh – Yemen’s Houthis have kept up their attacks on Saudi Arabia as senior officials from the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold high-stakes talks with Iran in Tehran on Monday, following warnings of a return to war.

Fresh explosions rattled Riyadh overnight, along with a text message warning to residents, after the Iran-allied Houthis claimed a new attack on the Saudi capital’s international airport on Sunday.

Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, has become deeply embroiled in the eight-month war since hostilities in its long-running conflict with the Iran-allied Houthis resumed in July.

Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is among the delegations travelling to Tehran, made up of officials from the three countries that signed a defence alliance in Mecca in August.

Their visit follows warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could resume.

Tensions have increased ahead of Israel’s pivotal election on Tuesday and next week’s US mid-terms, where US President Donald Trump’s Republicans are battling to keep control of both chambers of the US Congress.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei will take part in Monday’s meeting with Prince Khalid, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri Kani, told state TV.

“This historic meeting in Tehran may be the last chance before escalation spirals out of control, an attempt to impose a path of de-escalation before it’s too late,” Hesham Alghannam, a Saudi security analyst and researcher, posted on X.

“The presence of military and security figures at this level together means that the remaining time is extremely limited.”

– ‘Serious tensions’ –

On Sunday, as blasts rang out over Riyadh and authorities sent texts warning residents of a “hostile aerial threat”, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it struck missile launchers and storage facilities in Yemen.

The Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport once again. The repeatedly targeted facility has been largely closed since 13 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in a major attack this month.

Mediation efforts between the US and Iran have been led by Qatar and Pakistan. A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Sunday, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said.

“Our region is in the grip of serious tensions, and neighbouring countries are striving to convey a message and put forward initiatives,” Baqaei said on Monday.

Andreas Krieg of London-based risk consultancy MENA analytica said Prince Khalid’s presence in Tehran was “hugely significant”, calling him the “strategic mastermind of Saudi Arabia”.

Prince Khalid, brother of Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has emerged as one of Saudi Arabia’s key diplomatic interlocutors, dispatched on sensitive regional missions.

“For him to go to Iran directly in this very sensitive time is a very, very strong signal that the kingdom is not just… sitting and waiting for things, events to unfold,” Krieg told AFP.

“There’s a clear effort by the Mecca alliance to signal to Iran that they’re ready to work together to defend the kingdom and defend the kingdom’s borders,” he added.

“And so should Iran think to escalate, which they will likely do if Israel and the US strikes, and they will most likely strike Saudi Arabia, Iran will have to bear the consequences.”

– ‘Don’t test us’ –

Comments by senior officials have raised speculation about renewed hostilities.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday “there has been talk of a new war” but that Tehran’s policies remain unchanged.

Trump said on Friday that Washington “may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the US-Israeli campaign against Iran that began on February 28.

On Sunday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned that Iran may try to disrupt the Israeli elections, where he is in a close-fought race to stay in power.

“We have intelligence signs that our enemies, Iran and its proxies, could challenge us with attacks in order to disrupt the elections,” Netanyahu said.

“Don’t test us. You will suffer disproportionate blows,” added Netanyahu, who has campaigned heavily on his security credentials.

The remarks came as Israel’s Channel 12, citing unnamed sources, reported a confrontation between Netanyahu and army chief Eyal Zamir over an unspecified new directive in the war with Iran, which the premier denied.

World.title: France’s Macron to visit Marseille after protest violence
World.content:
Marseille – The French government sought to draw a line Monday under weeks of protests that have been marred by violence, with President Emmanuel Macron headed to Marseille and the prime minister to meet with students demanding better school conditions.

France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country’s worst rioting in years.

The demonstrations have come at a critical moment for France, six months ahead of a presidential election to replace centrist Macron.

The frontrunner — far-right leader Marine le Pen — held an election rally in Orleans Sunday, a day after yet more demonstrations also saw some violent clashes on the sidelines.

She vowed to “restore the rule of law” if elected next year. Polls show the protests and ensuing disorder have boosted her support, as the government and Macron faced sharp criticism over the unrest.

Authorities have admitted to security and intelligence failures that paved the way for the clashes, large-scale looting and vandalism of public property that erupted on October 17, and had stepped up security for Saturday’s protests.

While Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the outcome of Saturday’s rallies was more “positive” than a week ago, street violence still erupted in the French capital and a number of other cities including Marseille.

The Elysee said Macron would visit the city hall in Marseille, France’s second-largest city, on Monday, after it was damaged in the protest violence on October 17.

He was also due to meet shopkeepers who had fallen victim to looting and vandalism, the Elysee said.

“He will also pay tribute to and thank the internal security forces that helped restore republican order,” the presidency said.

After this weekend’s protests, many shopfronts in the city centre were still boarded up early Monday, just hours before Macron’s arrival.

Macron’s visit was intended to demonstrate that “the state is present, standing firm and fulfilling its mission to protect,” an aide said.

– ‘High level of violence’ –

A total of 1,435 people were arrested on the sidelines of the most recent weekend protests, Nunez said on Monday.

“The day was brought under control and there were no serious incidents,” he told broadcaster BFMTV.

“Nevertheless, we saw a very high level of violence directed at the internal security forces,” Nunez added.

He said that 267 police officers and gendarmes were injured, along with 150 protesters, including three who were seriously hurt in Toulouse, Reims and Clermont-Ferrand.

The unrest followed weeks of demonstrations by students campaigning for better learning conditions.

Several teenage protesters have been seriously injured and thousands arrested.

The police response to their demonstrations, which included blockades of schools, has been criticised as heavy-handed and sparked a broader movement against the cost of living and police violence.

In Paris on Monday, Lecornu was to meet student leaders, with National Education Minister Edouard Geffray and Higher Education Minister Philippe Baptiste joining him for the talks. Following that meeting, Geffray and Baptiste will hold a news conference.

Macron already met representatives of secondary school pupils last Friday, but they emerged from the talks urging students to keep protesting until the government put forward concrete proposals to address their demands.

On top of the protests, the country was last week shaken by a shooting that killed one person and wounded five, including a 12-year-old girl, outside Paris.

Macron has branded the shooting a “racist terrorist attack”, as most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds.

World.title: Russia says open to mini Ukraine ceasefires, but no let up in war
World.content:
Moscow – Russia said Monday that it would not slow down its offensive on Ukraine despite upcoming US-brokered talks on ending the conflict but that it could agree local “humanitarian” ceasefires.

The Kremlin said that it was open to short-term “humanitarian” ceasefires along the front line, ahead of a truce in the ravaged Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.

A ceasefire is to start in the southern Ukrainian city early Tuesday, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump after months of reports that residents faced dire food, water and medicine shortages.

Asked whether Russia would consider more local truces, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters: “For humanitarian purposes, absolutely.”

But Moscow vowed not to let up in the overall pace of the war, even as the sides prepare to restart stalled talks under US mediation next month.

“The decision to resume trilateral talks does not imply any restrictions on combat operations,” Peskov said.

“Our armed forces continue to carry out massive strikes on Ukraine’s military-industrial complex,” he added.

Russia has intensified drone and missile attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, hitting energy sites around major cities in what Kyiv says is a bid to plunge the country into cold and darkness throughout the winter.

Strikes last year left millions without heating or electricity with temperatures as low as -20C.

The two sides are to meet next month with US envoys to discuss ways to end Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.

Several previous rounds have failed to move the sides closer to a deal. Russia demands more territory in eastern Ukraine and sweeping military and political restrictions on Kyiv.

Ukraine and its allies say the demands are tantamount to a capitulation that would leave the country exposed to a future Russian attack.

World.title: Anthropic’s AI model accessed US voter data: Axios
World.content:
Washington – Anthropic’s Claude AI model bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available voter data in the US state of Georgia without human authorization, Axios reported on Sunday.

The case is the latest in a string of security scares at the world’s top AI developers ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3.

Claude accessed aggregate voter counts in Georgia, where more than one million voters have already cast early ballots, Axios reported, citing an Anthropic spokesperson.

According to the spokesperson, the model, which was being trained as part of an internal statistics project, accessed the information behind a paywall by bypassing the system “without being asked to.”

It did not access the state’s voter registration system or change or download any voting records, the spokesperson said, adding that the company has since taken measures to prevent these kinds of actions.

The disclosure adds to mounting unease over how well leading labs can control increasingly autonomous systems.

In July, a group of OpenAI agents broke out of their test environments and launched a cyberattack on AI firm Hugging Face, causing international alarm. Other companies have since reported similar incidents.

The incidents have fueled calls in the United States and abroad for tighter oversight of AI development.

American tech executives signed in September what President Donald Trump described as a “morally binding” commitment to build adequate safeguards around AI models.

World.title: 'Who checks the power?' Ex-SC judge calls for safeguards in poll panel appointments

NEW DELHI: Former

judge Abhay Oka has called for a legal framework to ensure that the appointment of election commissioners remains free from political dominance. He stressed that independent institutions are essential to protecting democracy.

Speaking at a lecture titled "Freedom of Speech and Us" in Thane on Sunday, Justice Oka (retd) questioned the safeguards in place to ensure accountability in constitutional appointments and called for a more independent selection process.

Oka cited a proposal by former deputy prime minister Lal Krishna Advani for a collegium system to appoint election commissioners. "Former Deputy Prime Minister Lal Krishna Advani had proposed a collegium system nearly 14 years ago, which would have included the Prime Minister, Law Minister, Leaders of the Opposition in both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India, to ensure a truly independent selection process," he claimed.

He also questioned what would happen if an election commissioner, such as Gyanesh Kumar, were removed from office, highlighting the need for clear legal provisions governing such appointments and ensuring institutional independence.

Reiterating the importance of free and fair elections, Oka said freedom of speech was equally vital to democracy. Every citizen must be able to express their views and perspectives, he said, adding that disagreements should be addressed through debate rather than violence.





"To preserve our nation's democracy, freedom of speech must be protected, as life loses its meaningful essence without it," he added.

The former judge also criticised what he described as "systematic environmental exploitation", linking rising temperatures in Thane and Mumbai to the loss of green cover.

World.title: At least 6 shot dead at hotel in Guwahati, police launch manhunt
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At least six people were shot dead at a hotel in Guwahati,

.

World.title: 'Ball is in their court': Congress asks PM Modi to sack CEC if concerned about Delhi traders

In a post on X, Congress MP Pawan Khera said the government's refusal to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar was the real issue, not the protests.

"If Modi and Shah are truly concerned about Delhiâs traders and genuinely want to stop the 1st November rally, they must sack Gyanesh Gupta and address our demands immediately. The ball is in their court," Khera said.

"Protests, rallies and demonstrations demanding an end to ECI-administered Vote Chori and election rigging for the RSS-BJP are acts of patriotism.

The protests are not the problem. The problem is the governmentâs obstinacy to save the chair of a bureaucrat who wins elections for them. Delhiâs traders, too, must fulfil their patriotic duty by demanding that the government remove Gyanesh Babu," he added.

This comes after Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi expressed solidarity with Delhi's traders and accused the government of disrupting business by shutting metro services, sealing roads and locking down the capital.





"To every trader in Delhi: We love you and hear you. The Govt shut the metro, sealed our roads and locked down our capital. With a stolen vote nothing is safe - your shop, your savings, your childrenâs future. Tell Modi to sack accused no. 4, Gyanesh Kumar and the protests will stop in 30 seconds," Rahul said.

World.title: 'Travesty of justice': SC flays UP Police for 'slipshod probe' in murder case, orders reparation for undertrial
World.content:
The verdict came on a plea challenging an Allahabad high court order in January that had denied the man bail. The Supreme Court had directed the trial court on March 23 to conclude the proceedings within three months. The trial was subsequently completed, and the accused was acquitted.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Uttar Pradesh government to pay Rs 6 lakh in reparation to a man who spent six years in jail as an undertrial in a murder case before being acquitted. The apex court said that the years lost to a faulty investigation were a travesty of justice.Slamming the state police for a âslipshod investigationâ and the prosecution for its haphazard handling of the case, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran called the man a âvictim of the systemâ. It said six years of his life had been erased based on a âconcocted storyâ built on mere surmises and conjectures.The man had been in custody since November 14, 2019, in a murder case registered in Agra.The Supreme Court noted that the trial court acquitted him after finding that none of the four circumstances cited by the prosecution, including electronic evidence, had been proved.âThis is a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with, resulting in the prosecution putting into jeopardy a person's life and liberty,â the bench said.The court directed the state to pay the compensation within one month, acknowledging that the amount was small compared with the years he had spent behind bars.âWe, hence, direct the state to pay an amount of Rs 6 lakh; though paltry in comparison to the years spent in custody, within a period of one month to the petitioner herein,â it said.The verdict came on a plea challenging an Allahabad High Court order in January that had denied the man bail. The Supreme Court had directed the trial court on March 23 to conclude the proceedings within three months. The trial was subsequently completed, and the accused was acquitted.The bench said the case highlighted the failure of investigating and prosecuting agencies to safeguard an individual's liberty despite the presumption of innocence.âThe state cannot shirk from its responsibility to protect its citizens, especially when a person arraigned in a criminal case is presumed innocent until proven guilty,â it said.The court stressed that the role of investigating and prosecuting agencies was not simply to secure convictions, but to ensure justice for all parties, including the accused.âThey should recognise themselves to be essential stakeholders in the justice delivery system, ensuring justice, not only to the victim, the de facto complainant and the injured, but also to the accused,â the bench said.The judges also expressed concern over the wider implications of such cases, saying they had encountered similar failures but that this one stood out for its severity.âWe come across such travesty of justice in many matters, but in some, so blatant and shocking, as in this case, which requires reparation to the accused, who in turn is a victim of the system,â it said.The bench directed that a copy of its verdict be sent to the Uttar Pradesh director general of police and the state's home secretary. It also urged the police to train officers in proper investigative procedures, criticising the manner in which the case had been handled.The court said the acquittal was fortunate, given the consequences of the flawed investigation and prosecution for the man's life and liberty.

World.title: India is working hard to reduce fiscal deficit, says Nirmala Sitharaman
World.content:
India is among the few nations working actively to reduce its fiscal deficit in the global economy, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said in Tiruchi on Monday.

Speaking to reporters after attending the platinum jubilee celebrations of her alma mater Seethalakshmi Ramaswami College in Tiruchi, she said the government had been consistently working to bring down the fiscal deficit despite challenges posed by developments such as the COVID-19 pandemic.

“When you study the credit situation of nations in the post-COVID era, our country’s efforts to reduce our debts before and after the pandemic, have borne fruit, as seen in the steady decrease of the fiscal deficit in the past three years. We are confident of achieving the target of reducing national debt to 50% of the gross domestic product by 2030,” she said.

“So when you compare us with foreign countries, Many leading global organisations acknowledge that India is making the most creditworthy efforts to reduce its fiscal deficit. We are also working actively to increase the per capita income of every Indian citizen, but we have had a series of challenges, such as the pandemic, then war [in West Asia] and the soaring rise in fuel prices. We are trying to control the burden of inflation faced by the public,” she added.

Ms. Sitharaman declined to answer questions on Tamil Nadu’s borrowings. “As a Union Minister, it would not be fair for me to comment on the situation of one particular State. However, queries regarding the finances of Tamil Nadu should be raised by the Opposition parties in the Assembly. The matter is of great importance and needs detailed discussion,” she said.

The stabilisation of the Indian rupee’s value depends on a number of factors, she said, adding that: “The Reserve Bank is engaged in efforts to protect the rupee from market volatility.”

‘Democratic way’

Commenting on the protests against the Election Commission of India regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, Ms. Sitharaman said: “Many complaints have been raised about the SIR in the Supreme Court, and these are being currently heard. One can participate in the hearing and present arguments to seek justice through legal means; many are doing it. Protesting against SIR on the streets is a political way as an Opposition party and that is also happening now.”

World.title: Hare Krishna Vaikuntham begins month-long Damodara Deepotsavam

World.title: Karnataka SIR: Final electoral roll out on October 27; net additions remain minuscule
World.content:
After more than three months of a clean-up drive under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Karnataka’s final electoral roll will be published on October 27. The list will be uploaded on the website of the Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka.

The exercise, which began with the stated aim of ensuring that no eligible voter was excluded and no ineligible voter remained on the rolls, led to the deletion of 1.07 crore names across the State. Karnataka had 5.54 crore voters when the exercise began. The final roll will have around 4.54 crore voters, with one crore names struck off the rolls. Details on the number of ineligible voters identified, or the count of foreign citizens — another stated aim of the SIR — remain unknown so far.

During the draft roll stage, 16.39 lakh names were deleted on the ground that the voters were dead, while over seven lakh were identified as duplicate entries. Another 3.83 lakh names were deleted under the “Others” category, which is not seen in many other States that conducted the SIR. Even as the exercise comes to an end, the CEO’s office has not clearly explained what the “Others” category comprises, apart from stating that it includes people who refused to sign.

However, the largest category of deletions — 80.62 lakh names — comprised voters who had shifted residence or were not found at their addresses during the enumeration phase. Unlike those identified as dead or duplicate, these voters were not necessarily ineligible to vote. They would have had to apply through Form 6 to have their names restored to the rolls. Yet, only 7,87,534 applications for inclusion were received, a figure that also includes applications from new voters.

The scale of deletions under the SIR has not been offset by additions in any constituency across the State, with applications for inclusion falling far short of the number of names struck off the draft roll.

World.title: Hennur–Bagalur Main Road may be made signal-free or get elevated corridor after feasibility study
World.content:
Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Monday (October 26) said the Hennur–Bagalur Main Road could either be made signal-free over the next five years or get an elevated corridor, depending on the outcome of a feasibility and viability study.

“An elevated corridor is the preference. The Chief Minister also wants that, but we cannot go for it until a survey is done and feasibility and viability are studied,” he said during an inspection of the ongoing roadworks. Calling it an important stretch that needs “comprehensive, long-term development,“ he said a decision on the proposed elevated corridor would be taken after the study.

The inspection comes amid continued complaints from residents about the condition of the road, where the situation has worsened since white-topping began in 2024. Work on side drains and footpaths remains pending.

‘Speed up work’

Mr. Gowda directed officials to expedite the ongoing works on the stretch between the junction and Geddalahalli. “One contractor is already working on the road, and another will be hired within a week to take up work in the opposite direction and speed up construction,“ he said.

The three-km white-topping project, which began in 2024, has missed several deadlines, with the most recent ones in October and June this year. Parts of the newly white-topped road have already developed cracks and uneven surfaces. The stretch that falls under three different jurisdictions — the Bengaluru East City Corporation, Bengaluru Smart Infrastructure Limited and the Public Works Department — serves as an alternative route to the Kempegowda International Airport.

Mr. Gowda directed officials to identify alternate routes and put traffic arrangements in place during construction to minimise inconvenience to commuters. He also asked officials to widen footpaths wherever feasible and repair damaged slabs. “Drainage systems must also be upgraded wherever necessary and planned alongside road development to ensure the free flow of rainwater and prevent flooding,“ he said.

Officials were directed to expedite pending land acquisition and handover processes that could delay the works. Mr. Gowda said the road had been taken up under previous governments as an alternative route to the Outer Ring Road, as the airport road faced traffic congestion and high toll charges. Of the 18-km project, 70% of the work has been completed, he said, adding that land acquisition in the remaining stretches would be expedited.

White-topping

When asked about white-topping works lagging across several areas, with the deadline approaching in December for the 126-km road network, Mr. Gowda said 20% of the work had been completed and the project would be completed by December-end. Attributing the delay to heavy rain, he said the focus was on ensuring quality rather than completing the work quickly.

World.title: Anthropic files for IPO as revenue jumps 14-fold to $16.3 billion in H1
World.content:
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, has filed to go public in the United States, disclosing rapid revenue growth, expanding enterprise spending and the high cost of developing and running advanced AI models.

The company filed a registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 26. It intends to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT”. The number of shares to be offered and the price range have not yet been determined.

The public filing follows Anthropic’s confidential submission of a draft registration statement to the SEC on June 1, 2026. The proposed IPO remains subject to regulatory review.

One of the key disclosures is that revenue from a group of existing customers was about nine times higher in the three months ended September 30, 2026, than in the same period a year earlier. The calculation includes customers who generated at least $1 in revenue in the earlier period but excludes subscribers to Anthropic’s Claude Pro and Max plans.

The company reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in revenue over the preceding 12 months as of September 30, up from more than 950 a year earlier. More than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million, while approximately 250 generated at least $10 million.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.16 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. Its net loss widened to $80.7 billion from $13 billion, largely because of accounting expenses arising from changes in the estimated value of certain financing instruments as the company’s valuation rose.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of $693 million in the first half of 2026, compared with $2.14 billion a year earlier. However, using its own adjusted measure, which excludes certain expenses, the company reported operating income of $1.6 billion, with a margin of about 10%.

It reported $8.95 billion in computing and infrastructure expenses in the first half of 2026, reflecting the costs of developing and running advanced AI models. As of June 30, the company held $131.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, according to the filing.

The prospectus flags risks including dependence on computing infrastructure providers, competition and the cost of developing increasingly capable AI models. Major cloud providers supply Anthropic with computing capacity and help distribute its products, while also developing competing AI services.

The filing also outlines a governance structure intended to protect Anthropic’s long-term public-benefit mission. An entity formed by its seven co-founders will hold a special share carrying 50.1% of general voting power, while the company’s Long-Term Benefit Trust will have the right to appoint a majority of the board. This would limit the ability of ordinary shareholders to influence corporate governance, even after the company lists publicly.

Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be offered or the proposed price range. The timing and terms of the IPO will depend on the regulatory process and market conditions.

World.title: Two Reserved Forest Areas in Maharashtra to Be Declared Wildlife Sanctuaries; Approval Granted for 14 Conservation Reserves
World.content:
Two reserved forest areas in Maharashtra will be declared as wildlife sanctuaries, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Monday (October 26, 2026). He was speaking after chairing the 26th meeting of the Maharashtra State Board for Wildlife. In addition, proposals for 14 conservation reserves in Pune, Raigad, Nashik, Nandurbar, Thane, Palghar and Chandrapur districts were approved.

The State Board for Wildlife on Monday (October 26) approved the proposal to declare the Kolamarka Conservation Reserve in Gadchiroli district, known for its population of wild buffaloes, as a wildlife sanctuary. Approval was also granted to declare the newly expanded Tansa Wildlife Sanctuary, adjoining the existing Tansa Wildlife Sanctuary, as a wildlife sanctuary.

Also Read: Third long march in Maharashtra highlights forest rights act lapses

To make Tansa Wildlife Sanctuary free of human habitation, the Board approved the proposal to include 588.767 hectares of revenue and private land from six villages—Ogda, Khodde, Tirmal, Pachghar, Phanasad and Amle—in the newly expanded Tansa Wildlife Sanctuary.

The Board also approved proposals to declare 100.139 square kilometres in Koka Wildlife Sanctuary and 255.79 square kilometres in Jayakwadi Bird Wildlife Sanctuary as critical wildlife habitats.

Conservation reserves

It approved proposals for 14 conservation reserves in Pune, Raigad, Nashik, Nandurbar, Thane, Palghar and Chandrapur districts. These include Velhe-Mulshi in Pune and Raigad districts; Bhor-Girigad in Pune district; Dindori, Surgana and Taharabad in Nashik district; Chinchpada in Nandurbar district; Alibag and Ghera Manikgad in Raigad district; Lonavala in Pune and Raigad districts; Gumtara in Thane district; Jawhar, Asherigad and Dhamani in Palghar district; and Ekara in Chandrapur district.

Chief Minister Fadnavis directed that routine works such as dam repairs, rehabilitation and desilting within wildlife sanctuaries should be incorporated into the respective sanctuary management plans. “Necessary amendments to these plans should be made within three months by preparing standard operating procedures consistent with the applicable rules. Instead of obtaining separate approvals on every occasion for such works, a system should be established under which the concerned wildlife officials are informed in advance,” he said.

Proposals concerning various infrastructure facilities in protected areas, eco-sensitive zones and tiger corridors were also approved at the meeting. These included irrigation, healthcare, water supply, bridges, roads, underground optical fibre cables, electricity lines and other infrastructure projects.

The meeting also discussed proposals to notify the core, buffer and notified eco-sensitive areas of the state’s six tiger reserves as silence zones; to declare human-wildlife conflict a natural disaster; and to formulate a policy for the rehabilitation of villages in buffer zones of tiger reserves whose residents are willing to relocate. The Chief Minister directed that further action be taken after examining the coordination between the responsibilities of District Collectors under the Disaster Management Act, the existing compensation mechanism and the powers of the Forest Department.

World.title: Campus Connect
World.content:
Free uniforms distributed

Anandhalatha Educational Trust has been providing educational support to underprivileged students for the past 20 years. The trust aims to promote education among economically disadvantaged families and help students pursue their studies without financial difficulties.

As part of its educational service, the trust has been distributing free uniforms and providing other essential educational assistance to deserving students. This initiative has helped many students from economically weaker sections continue their education with confidence and dignity.

The trust has been extending its services to Government school students from Classes 9 to 12 in several areas of Theni district, including Pannaipuram, Melasokkanathapuram, Highwavys, Odaipatti, Kottur and Thevaram. Over 300 students have benefited from this initiative.

The free school uniforms were distributed by trust founder of M.M. Anandavel, general secretary of the Theni Melapettai Hindu Nadargal Uravinmurai.
